balance/tuning.json:
{
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "_note": "TODOS N95 tuning layer. Applied on top of the generated Data/Balance.json by GameData.Load (Sim/Game/GameData.cs BalanceTuning). GameData.LoadRaw skips it, so browser goldens keep the raw export. Each row names Balance keys and an op: mul multiplies, set replaces. Every row: source A = assumption (owner to tune) with a why.",
  "rows": [
    {
      "id": "newBuildRent",
      "keys": [
        "r_shops",
        "r_grocer",
        "r_rest",
        "r_qsr",
        "r_fit",
        "r_apt",
        "r_town",
        "r_office",
        "r_med"
      ],
      "op": "mul",
      "value": 1.4,
      "source": "A",
      "why": "Every building in this game is new construction, and the browser rents read as existing-stock comps: new retail and new Class A apartments ask a premium over existing space, and the developer's whole margin is that premium. Raw rents left yield on cost about 1 point UNDER the cap rate on the Builder traces (glade s1 5.59% vs 6.63%, strip s2 4.83% vs 5.85%; TODOS N53), so no developer would build. A 1.40 multiplier lifts yield on cost to about cap rate + 1 point (glade 7.8% vs 6.6%, strip 6.8% vs 5.9%). Rents, not costs or cap rates: rents are the only single lever that also lets NOI cover construction interest; costs are only part of total cost (land and interest do not move), and lowering cap rates raises value without fixing the cash flow. Top of the defensible range: owner to tune."
    },
    {
      "id": "renewMinDscr",
      "keys": [
        "due_renewMinDscr"
      ],
      "op": "add",
      "value": 1.25,
      "label": "Loan renewal: lowest debt coverage (NOI / debt service) a bank renews at",
      "source": "A",
      "why": "Banks renew a performing, leased loan that covers its debt service about 1.25 times even when values dip below the LTV test; at the browser LTV-only rule the bank took 98% leased buildings over a 1.1M gap (TODOS N53, N67). Read by Sim/Capital/LoanDue.cs; absent on a raw load, so the browser due9 rule still holds there."
    },
    {
      "id": "softNetOfCityFee",
      "keys": [
        "soft"
      ],
      "op": "set",
      "value": 19.6,
      "label": "Soft costs, % of hard, net of the city fee",
      "source": "A",
      "why": "N82 W6 (plan-5 P7.1): the city impact fee is now charged on its own on the non-land cost (CityFee.StartCost, browser line 970), at city_fee 2% to start. The browser soft row (22%) is an all-in soft-cost factor that already carries permits and fees, so charging the fee on top would count it twice and leave the golden starter layout 46,637 short of the 12M start. 1.22 / 1.02 = 1.196: at the starting fee the total cost is the same as before (within 0.01%), and every fee raise voted later still costs more. 19.6 is inside the row's 18 to 28 range."
    }
  ]
}

{
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "_note": "P1.8 capital stack. Every value carries a source: A = assumption (owner to tune), or a browser-build-v30.html line. Senior spread, LTV cap and DSCR, mezz spread and combined LTV, investor pref and split are NOT here: they are read from Balance.json (sp_bank, lv_bank, dscr18, mz_sp, mz_ltv, jv_pref, jv_split) so the stack and the existing lender quotes never disagree.",
  "values": {
    "prefEquityRate": { "value": 12, "source": "A", "why": "Preferred equity costs more than the bank loan and less than the mezz loan (bank rate + mz_sp); 12% a year sits between them at the default 7% market rate." },
    "playerSplitAtLeastCommonShare": { "value": 1, "source": "A (N59 default, owner call)", "why": "N59: jv_split 30 is a promote for a player who puts in about 10% of the equity. On a stack your share of profit after the investor's pref is never below your share of the common equity (times this value), so Balanced, where you and the investor put in the same cash, splits the profit 50/50 instead of 30/70. 1 means pro rata; above 1 gives you a promote." },
    "mezzMinCoverage": { "value": 1.05, "source": "A", "why": "Mezz lenders stop lending once income covers senior plus mezz payments less than 1.05 times; thin on purpose so Risky is fragile." },
    "playerEquityFloorPct": { "value": 10, "source": "owner 2026-11-24", "why": "Owner: set a minimum on your own cash in a deal. At least 10% of the deal cost is your own cash on every plan, so a deal is never mostly other people's money. When a plan would go under it, the most junior outside money shrinks first: preferred equity, then the mezz loan, then the bank loan, and the investor's slice of the common equity is cut to leave you 10%." },
    "foreclosureQuarters": { "value": 3, "source": "A", "why": "Three quarters in a row of income short of the loan payments and the senior lender takes the building; long enough to cure, short enough to bite." },
    "graceQuarters": { "value": 8, "source": "A", "why": "p1-grace: construction and bridge loans carry an interest reserve and their covenants start at stabilization, so no foreclosure strikes while a new project leases up, for at most 8 quarters (two years, a typical lease-up reserve) after opening or until it stabilizes, whichever comes first. Shortfalls in grace still pile up as arrears you owe." },

  "formatVersion": 1,

  "openQuarters": { "value": 2, "source": "browser", "why": "Same as v11 due = turn + 2 (:1937)." },
  "fairRentYears": { "value": 1.0, "source": "A", "why": "A fair HQ package is about one year of the tenant's rent in build-out and perks, the usual big office deal size." },
  "pitch": { "kind": "meeting", "slots": 2, "source": "A", "why": "Selling a company on its HQ is a long sit down, two blocks of the day like a tour (slots.json tour = 2)." },
  "charm": {
    "skill": "charisma",
    "requiredLevel": 2,
    "baseChance": 0.35, "perLevel": 0.12,
    "bonus": 8, "missPenalty": 0,
    "source": "A", "why": "Charm can swing about as much as 16% more money (8 of 50 money points). Level 1 lands 47%, level 5 lands 95%. A miss costs nothing but the slots."
  },
  "maxMoneyRatio": { "value": 1.5, "source": "browser", "why": "v11's top offer is 1.5 times fair (bidSteps All in, :1931). Paying more than that does not raise the score, so the Tycoon levers cannot run away with the hunt." },
  "odds": { "low": 0.4, "good": 0.6, "source": "A", "why": "Normal shows a word, not a number. Word bible odds row (open decision 19 default): Low under 40%, Even 40 to 60%, Good over 60%." },
  "honorPerRank": { "value": 1.5, "source": "A", "why": "Honor rank 4 is worth 6 points, like a 12% richer package. Negative honor subtracts." },
  "famePer10": { "value": 1.0, "source": "A", "why": "Fame 50 of 100 adds 5 points: famous developers get the call back." },
  "heatPerStar": { "value": 3, "source": "A", "why": "Each heat star costs 3 points: a company board does not want its name next to a scandal." },
  "brandPerPoint": { "value": 0.1, "source": "A", "why": "Brand is not built yet (P4.7). The hook returns 0, so this does nothing until then." },
  "maxSocialBonus": { "value": 15, "source": "A", "why": "Honor, fame, heat and brand together never move the score more than 15 points so money and place still decide most hunts." },

Losing adds their court costs (25%)." },
    "tenant":  { "fightMonths": 4, "winChance": 0.55, "settleShare": 0.5,  "restructureShare": 0.3, "loseShare": 1.0,  "baseSueChance": 0.02, "blocksSale": false, "source": "A", "why": "Tenant claims are often weak or partly fair, so a fight is close to a coin flip and they take half to go away. 2% a month per angry tenant keeps suits rare." },
    "partner": { "fightMonths": 6, "winChance": 0.5,  "settleShare": 0.6,  "restructureShare": 0.35, "loseShare": 1.2, "baseSueChance": 0.015, "blocksSale": false, "source": "A", "why": "Partner fights are long and even. Rarer than tenant suits because there are fewer partners." },

{
  "_note": "Broker NPCs (plan P3.11). Read by Sim/Brokers. Every number is source A (an assumption for the owner to tune) except FeePct, which is the browser build's broker fee. Each block says why. Brokers are separate from the cast broker (top_broker); see Docs/agent-notes/p3-brokers.md.",
  "Rules": {
    "StartStanding": 10,
    "MinStanding": -100,
    "MaxStanding": 100,
    "FirstLookAt": 30,
    "DryAt": -10,
    "BadSportBlocksFirstLook": true,
    "Source": "A",
    "Why": "Standing runs -100 to 100 and starts at 10. At 30 or more a broker texts you before the site goes on the market (two closed deals with fees paid gets you there). At -10 or less the broker stops texting. One cut price after a handshake (-40 or worse) drops any broker from the start straight to silence. A Bad Sport gets no first looks from anyone."
  },
  "Points": {
    "FeePaid": 6,
    "FeeSkipped": -20,
    "DealClosed": 10,
    "FastAnswer": 2,
    "Pass": -1,
    "LateAnswer": -8,
    "Retrade": -40,
    "RetradeCeiling": -30,
    "Meeting": 4,
    "MeetingEveryDays": 30,
    "Source": "A",
    "Why": "A closed deal plus the fee is worth 16, a lunch 4 (once a month), a quick answer 2. A plain pass costs 1 so saying no is fine; a quick pass costs 0 (the quick-answer bonus can cancel the pass, never turn it into a gain); a late answer costs 8 and also counts as a pass. A cut price after a handshake costs 40 times the broker's temper, and leaves standing at -30 or lower however good it was, so the broker goes quiet; sites that broker brought you before the cut price earn no standing when you close them or pay their fees; about six monthly lunches win the texts back."
  },
  "Fees": {
    "FeePct": 0.02,
    "Source": "Docs/browser-build-v30.html:3512",
    "Why": "The browser build charges a 2% broker fee on a sale (close22: 'The broker fee was money(px*0.02)'). We charge the same 2% of the closed price when a broker's site closes. Using the sale side fee for a buy is an assumption."
  },
  "Honor": {
    "FeePaidHonor": 1,
    "LateAnswerHonor": -1,
    "Source": "A",
    "Why": "Paying a broker's fee is a small kept promise (+1 honor). Leaving a broker hanging past the deadline is a small broken one (-1). Small on purpose: honor.json owns the big moves (a cut price is already -6 there)."
  },
  "Flow": {
    "EveryDaysMin": 25,
    "EveryDaysMax": 50,
    "FirstDealDayMax": 20,
    "MaxOnMarketEach": 1,
    "Source": "A",
    "Why": "Each broker finds a site every 25 to 50 days (about two a quarter at 30 days a month), an average of 37.5 days, so about 2.4 sites per broker and about 14 a quarter between them. The first one shows up in the first 20 days. Each broker keeps at most MaxOnMarketEach site on the market at a time (so at most 6 broker sites). Broker sites use their own slots: they are set aside while the market refreshes (BrokerMarket.RefreshQuarter), so the market still fills its own 8 (deals.json MaxListings) exactly as with no brokers, and the list never passes 8 plus 6 plus the quarter's tip and backroom extras. With no room the broker sells the site elsewhere and nothing is made. Fix pass finding 1, second fix pass F1."
  },

skills/odds.json:
{
  "_note": "P3.4 skill check odds shown on unlocked dialogue replies. Formula: odds = clamp(AtRequiredPct + PerLevelAbovePct * (level - required), MinPct, MaxPct). Display follows the word bible odds row: Easy shows none, Normal shows a word, Tycoon shows a whole %. Locked replies show LockedText.",
  "AtRequiredPct": { "value": 55, "source": "A", "why": "Just meeting the bar should feel a little better than a coin flip, so a new unlock is worth picking." },
  "PerLevelAbovePct": { "value": 10, "source": "A", "why": "Each level past the bar adds a clear step the player can see. Level 5 on a level 1 check reaches the cap." },
  "MinPct": { "value": 5, "source": "A", "why": "Nothing unlocked is hopeless." },
  "MaxPct": { "value": 95, "source": "A", "why": "Nothing is a sure thing; a slip can still happen." },
  "LowBelowPct": { "value": 40, "source": "A", "why": "Same cut as Data/company/hq.json odds.low (word bible odds row, open decision 19 default)." },
  "GoodAbovePct": { "value": 60, "source": "A", "why": "Same cut as Data/company/hq.json odds.good (word bible odds row, open decision 19 default)." },
  "Text": {
    "locked": "Needs {skill} Level {level}",
    "low": "Low odds",
    "even": "Even odds",
    "good": "Good odds",
    "pct": "{pct}% odds"
  }
}

story/tutorial.json:
{
  "_note": "P5.7 first play, about 20 minutes. One step at a time; TutorialRun (Sim/Story/TutorialDirector.cs) moves on only when TutorialChecks finds the WaitFor done in the game state. Skippable any time. Words short for a 12 year old. Presses = presses needed from when the hint shows (rule: 3 or fewer). HostOnly steps (walk, truck, drive, tablet, phone; restored from 0ceb820 for N310) are for the web walk mode and Unity: the console and TutorialRun skip them, the host reports their WaitFor through TutorialDirector.Report.",
  "MaxWordsPerStep": 14,
  "MaxPresses": 3,
  "Steps": [
    { "Id": "t_walk", "Text": "Walk to your truck. It is the red one.", "WaitFor": "reach_truck", "Presses": 1, "HostOnly": true },
    { "Id": "t_enter", "Text": "Press the A button to get in.", "WaitFor": "enter_truck", "Presses": 1, "HostOnly": true },
    { "Id": "t_drive", "Text": "Drive to the lot with the For Sale sign.", "WaitFor": "reach_first_lot", "Presses": 1, "HostOnly": true },
    { "Id": "t_buy", "Text": "Talk to the owner. Pick a fair price.", "WaitFor": "buy_first_lot", "Presses": 3, "HostOnly": true },
    { "Id": "t_tablet", "Text": "Open your tablet. Press Y.", "WaitFor": "open_tablet", "Presses": 1, "HostOnly": true },
    { "Id": "t_name", "Text": "Pick your name. Then name your company.", "WaitFor": "name_company", "Presses": 3 },
    { "Id": "t_place", "Text": "Open the build screen. Place shops on your land.", "WaitFor": "place_building", "Presses": 3 },
    { "Id": "t_start", "Text": "Press Start building. The crew gets to work.", "WaitFor": "start_building", "Presses": 1 },
    { "Id": "t_quarter", "Text": "Press End quarter to let time pass.", "WaitFor": "end_quarter", "Presses": 1 },
    { "Id": "t_open", "Text": "Read the recap. Keep ending quarters until your building opens.", "WaitFor": "project_open", "Presses": 1 },
    { "Id": "t_lease", "Text": "A tenant wants space. Read the offer, then press Sign.", "WaitFor": "sign_lease", "Presses": 2 },
    { "Id": "t_rent", "Text": "End the quarter. Your first rent comes in.", "WaitFor": "rent_paid", "Presses": 1 },
    { "Id": "t_fill", "Text": "Fill more space. Sign three leases in all.", "WaitFor": "lease_three", "Presses": 3 },
    { "Id": "t_refi", "Text": "Now take a new loan on it, or sell it for cash.", "WaitFor": "refi_or_sell", "Presses": 3 },
    { "Id": "t_phone", "Text": "Your phone shows your goals. Press Up to look.", "WaitFor": "open_phone", "Presses": 1, "HostOnly": true }
  ]
}
tenants/business.json:
{
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "note": "P3.17 tenants as businesses. Every value is a guess shaped like small retail rules of thumb; verify before calling it sourced.",
  "live": { "value": 1, "source": "owner 2026-11 tracker answer tenantslive: calibrate, then turn on (P7.1, Docs/agent-notes/p71-tenants.md)", "why": "1 lets struggling tenants ask for help and failing ones go dark in the quarter step; 0 only computes the numbers for the card" },
  "shopTypes": { "value": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8], "source": "Data/traffic/trips.json rate rows that are stores, food or fun", "why": "building types whose tenants sell to trips; office, homes and hotels are not modeled" },
  "dailyPerPmPeak": { "value": 10, "source": "rule of thumb: the PM peak hour is about 10% of daily trips (guess, verify)", "why": "PM peak trips to daily trips" },
  "daysPerQuarter": { "value": 91, "source": "365 / 4 rounded", "why": "days in a quarter" },
  "tripsPerVisit": { "value": 2, "source": "one visit is a trip in and a trip out", "why": "trip ends per shopper visit" },
  "lostSalesShare": { "value": 0.5, "source": "P7.1 calibration (guess, verify): the bots' shops sat at the 60% lost-trip cap and scored 0 health; half of the shoppers who find the lot full park on the street, walk over or come back later", "why": "share of the site's lost trips (full driveways and parking) the shop actually loses; 1 is the old full loss" },
  "spendPerVisit": { "value": 45, "source": "guess: $300 per SF a year over about 85,000 visits a year for a 13,800 SF strip (verify)", "why": "dollars a shopper spends per visit" },
  "crossShop": { "value": 0.15, "source": "guess (verify)", "why": "share of the rest of the site's visitors who also stop at this shop, split over the open shops" },
  "rentPerSfQuarter": { "value": 6, "source": "guess: $24 per SF a year for a strip shop (verify)", "why": "rent the health math uses per SF each quarter, times the lease rent vs market; billed rent needs the economy NOI, which this step cannot see" },
  "cogsShare": { "value": 0.65, "source": "guess: retail goods cost so a typical strip shop clears about a 13% margin (verify)", "why": "goods cost as a share of sales" },
  "staffPerKsf": { "value": 1.0, "source": "guess: one worker per 1,000 SF (verify)", "why": "staff count per 1,000 SF" },
  "wagePerQuarter": { "value": 9000, "source": "guess: about $36,000 a year per worker (verify)", "why": "cost of one worker for a quarter" },
  "otherPerSfQuarter": { "value": 2.0, "source": "guess: utilities, supplies, insurance (verify)", "why": "other costs per SF each quarter" },
  "healthAtZero": { "value": 50, "source": "design: break even reads as a coin flip", "why": "health score at zero profit" },
  "healthPerPoint": { "value": 3, "source": "design: 10 points of margin is 30 health", "why": "health per point of profit margin" },
  "struggleBelow": { "value": 45, "source": "design", "why": "below this health a tenant asks for help" },
  "failBelow": { "value": 25, "source": "design", "why": "below this health a tenant is failing" },
  "failQuarters": { "value": 2, "source": "design: one bad quarter is not a closing", "why": "failing quarters in a row before a tenant goes dark" },
  "expandAt": { "value": 75, "source": "design", "why": "health at or above this reads as ready to renew and grow" },
  "reliefShare": { "value": 0.3, "source": "design", "why": "share of rent given back each quarter under rent relief" },
  "reliefQuarters": { "value": 4, "source": "design", "why": "quarters rent relief lasts" },
  "marketingCost": { "value": 25000, "source": "guess (verify)", "why": "player cost of one co-marketing push" },
  "marketingLift": { "value": 0.2, "source": "guess (verify)", "why": "extra sales share while the push runs" },
  "marketingQuarters": { "value": 2, "source": "design", "why": "quarters a co-marketing push lasts" },
  "bustLeaveBase": { "value": 0.2, "source": "P7.1 design (guess, verify): owner said leave bust depth alone; leverage should hurt through tenants who do not renew in a downturn", "why": "chance a tenant up for renewal during a recession walks away instead of renewing" },
  "bustLeaveStruggleMul": { "value": 2, "source": "P7.1 design", "why": "bust walk-away chance multiplier for a shop the tenant sim scores struggling" },
  "bustLeaveFailMul": { "value": 3, "source": "P7.1 design", "why": "bust walk-away chance multiplier for a shop the tenant sim scores failing" },
  "deferQuarters": { "value": 2, "source": "design", "why": "a deferral hands back one quarter of rent now and bills it back this many quarters later" }
}

time/slots.json:
{
  "_note": "P3.5 daily time slots. The browser build (Docs/browser-build-v30.html) has no time slots, so every number here is source A (author guess) with a rationale. Tune in play-tests.",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "slotsPerDay": { "value": 5, "source": "A", "why": "Persona-style days have a few blocks. Five means a hearing (2) plus a tour (2) plus one call fills the day, so the player has to choose (P3.5 done-when)." },
  "slotNames": ["Early morning", "Late morning", "Lunch", "Afternoon", "Evening"],
  "missedRelationship": { "value": -6, "source": "A", "why": "A no-show hurts about as much as a lowball offer (relationships.json lowballed = -6) but less than breaking a deal (-15)." },
  "cancelRelationship": { "value": -2, "source": "A", "why": "Calling ahead to cancel is rude but honest, so it costs a third of a no-show." },
  "travel": {
    "_note": "Slots spent driving between districts. Uses Data/city/city.json district centers when the city is loaded; the table below is the fallback.",
    "sameDistrictSlots": { "value": 0, "source": "A", "why": "Anywhere in one district is a short drive." },
    "metersPerSlot": {"value": 840, "source": "A", "why": "On the P13.1 city the 15 district pairs split at 720 m (same slot) and 952 m (one slot); 840 sits between, so neighbors stay free and the far pairs cost one slot."},
    "maxSlots": { "value": 2, "source": "A", "why": "No drive across the city should eat more than two blocks of the day." },
    "fallback": {
      "glade|corner": 0, "glade|creek": 0, "glade|hill": 1, "glade|green": 1, "glade|lake": 1,
      "corner|creek": 0, "corner|hill": 0, "corner|green": 0, "corner|lake": 0,
      "creek|hill": 1, "creek|green": 0, "creek|lake": 1,
      "hill|green": 0, "hill|lake": 0,
      "green|lake": 1
    }
  },
  "kinds": {
    "meeting":   { "name": "Meeting",     "slots": 1, "delegate": true,  "source": "A", "why": "A sit-down with one person takes about one block." },
    "tour":      { "name": "Tour",        "slots": 2, "delegate": true,  "source": "A", "why": "Walking a building and its roof and basement takes most of a morning." },

{
  "_note": "World bible (P3.15b), machine-readable. Human version: Docs/world/bible.md. DRAFT until the owner approves it in the tracker. Fields marked signOff are proposals, not decisions.",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "status": "draft",
  "City": {
    "Name": "Cedar Glade",
    "State": "Texas",
    "County": "Larkin County",
    "Nickname": "The Glade",
    "Motto": "Room to grow",
    "Founded": 1872,
    "Population": "about 1.4 million in the metro",
    "signOff": "Word-bible decision 1. Cedar Glade is already the name in Data/city/city.json."
  },
  "History": [
    { "Year": 1872, "Text": "Cattle drivers stop to water their herds at a cedar grove on Caddo Creek. A trading post opens. People start calling the spot Cedar Glade." },
    { "Year": 1886, "Text": "The railroad arrives. A depot, a cotton gin and a red brick square grow up around the tracks. That square is Redbud Square today." },
    { "Year": 1921, "Text": "The Halloway family builds the first tall office building downtown. The rail yard becomes the busiest in the county." },
    { "Year": 1958, "Text": "The Prairie Star Freeway cuts across the west side. Gas stations, motels and diners line the new frontage roads." },
    { "Year": 1974, "Text": "Cedar Glade Regional Airport opens on old farm land to the south. Trucks and warehouses follow." },
    { "Year": 1985, "Text": "A dam on Caddo Creek fills Lake Cedar. Ranch families on the hill sell lots with lake views." },
    { "Year": 1999, "Text": "The Cedar Glade Grackles get a new ballpark east of downtown. The old warehouses around it sit empty for years." },
    { "Year": 2009, "Text": "Downtown hits bottom. Half the towers are dark. The rail yard closes." },
    { "Year": 2020, "Text": "New jobs pour in. Families move to the open land at Greenfield Edge. Everyone wants to build." },
    { "Year": 2026, "Text": "You arrive with a little cash, a big idea and no name. The city is growing faster than anyone can plan. That is your chance." }
  ],
  "Proposals": [
    { "id": "city_name", "Value": "Cedar Glade", "signOff": "owner", "note": "Glade Parks as the in-world city (a real development). The game title stays Glade Parks Builder." },
    { "id": "rich_list", "Value": "Prairie 100", "signOff": "owner", "note": "Lone Star 100 (busy trade name) and Bluebonnet 100 (collides with the default company)." },
    { "id": "default_company", "Value": "Bluebonnet Development", "signOff": "owner", "note": "Bluebonnet Builders. The player can still type any name." },
    { "id": "newspaper", "Value": "Cedar Glade Courier", "signOff": "owner", "note": "Glade Parks Gazette in Data/market/cycle.json." },
    { "id": "hotel_default", "Value": "Glade Inns", "signOff": "owner", "note": "nothing. Keep it: Glade now points at Cedar Glade." },
    { "id": "music_city", "Value": "Harmony Bluff", "signOff": "owner", "note": "Nashville as the hidden trip city. Hidden in v1; Pine Ridge is the v1 trip." }
  ]
}
world/districts.json:
{
  "_note": "World bible districts. Ids are the plan-4 map roster site-map sources (corner, creek, glade, green, lake are shipped ids in Data/city/city.json and Data/Sites.json; oldtown, airport, stadium are new maps). Display names are proposals for the P1.18 roster and P2.11 map spec. DRAFT for owner sign-off.",
  "formatVersion": 1,
  "Districts": [
    {
      "id": "corner",
      "Name": "Downtown Cedar Glade",
      "Short": "Downtown",
      "Identity": "Old towers, a closed rail yard and streets that empty out at six. The bones are great and the rents are cheap. The first developer to bring people back downtown wins big.",
      "Signature": "Air rights over the old rail yard",
      "Landmark": "The Brass Clock Depot",
      "Mood": "comeback",
      "note": "Roster row 1. Today named Infill Corner in city.json."
    },
    {
      "id": "creek",
      "Name": "Creekside",
      "Short": "Creekside",
      "Identity": "The walkable part of town. Patios, lofts, dog parks and a trail along the creek. Rents are high, lots are tiny and the neighbors watch everything.",
      "Signature": "Creek trail and the trolley line",
      "Landmark": "The Green Trolley barn",
      "Mood": "trendy",
      "note": "Roster row 2, the mixed-use district."
    },
    {
      "id": "oldtown",
      "Name": "Redbud Square",
      "Short": "Old Town",
      "Identity": "The red brick square where the town began. A courthouse, a feed store and a bakery that has been open since your grandma was a kid. Build here and you build with the past.",
      "Signature": "Heritage square and festivals",
      "Landmark": "The old Larkin County Courthouse",
      "Mood": "proud",
      "note": "Roster row 3. New map."
    },
    {
      "id": "glade",
      "Name": "Prairie Star Corridor",
      "Short": "The Corridor",
      "Identity": "Miles of frontage road along the freeway. Gas, burgers, car washes and strip centers. Nobody calls it pretty. Everybody drives past it, and that is the point.",
      "Signature": "Frontage roads and small lots by the exits",
      "Landmark": "The Exit 14 water tower",
      "Mood": "busy",
      "note": "Roster row 4, with the strip map merged in. Replaces the real-place name Glade Parks."
    },
    {
      "id": "green",
      "Name": "Greenfield Edge",
      "Short": "Greenfield",
      "Identity": "Open ranch land at the edge of town, with new families moving in every week. Here you do not build one building. You plan a whole community: streets, schools, parks and shops.",
      "Signature": "A whole community you design",
      "Landmark": "The Okafor windmill",
      "Mood": "growing",
      "note": "Roster row 5, the master-planned suburb."
    },
    {
      "id": "airport",
      "Name": "Kestrel Flats",
      "Short": "Kestrel Flats",
      "Identity": "Flat land, big trucks and planes overhead. Warehouses rise in months, not years. The money is steady, the neighbors are few, and the roads always need fixing.",
      "Signature": "Truck routes and air cargo",
      "Landmark": "The old control tower at Cedar Glade Regional Airport",
      "Mood": "hardworking",
      "note": "Roster row 6. New map."
    },
    {
      "id": "lake",
      "Name": "Lakefront",
      "Short": "Lakefront",
      "Identity": "Lake Cedar, boat docks and ranch houses on the hill with a view. Everyone wants to live here and nobody wants anything new built here. Views are worth money, and people fight for them.",
      "Signature": "Marina, and homes with lake views",
      "Landmark": "The Hillside lookout",
      "Mood": "exclusive",
      "note": "Roster row 7, with the hill map merged in. Hillside is a neighborhood inside it."
    },
    {
      "id": "stadium",
      "Name": "Grackle Yards",
      "Short": "Grackle Yards",
      "Identity": "Old warehouses around the ballpark. Eighty nights a year the streets fill with fans. The other nights are quiet. Turn game days into every day and you own the east side.",
      "Signature": "Game days and spillover crowds",
      "Landmark": "Grackle Field, home of the Cedar Glade Grackles",
      "Mood": "loud",
      "note": "Roster row 8. New map."
    }
  ],
  "Destination": {
    "id": "mtn",
    "Name": "Pine Ridge",
    "Short": "Pine Ridge",
    "Identity": "A mountain ski town a short flight away. Winter is packed and pricey. Summer is quiet and cheap. Smart money buys in July and sells in January.",
    "Signature": "Ski season",
    "Landmark": "The Silver Bell gondola",
    "Mood": "seasonal",
    "note": "Plan-4 v1 destination. Site map source mtn."
  },
  "HiddenDestinations": [
    { "id": "nash", "Name": "Harmony Bluff", "Identity": "A river city full of music halls, guitar shops and rooftop bars.", "note": "Owner choice: music city, fictional. Hidden until its own pass." }
  ]
}

@dialogue/banker_loan.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"
VAR site_name = "Bluebonnet Plaza"

-> banker_loan

=== banker_loan ===
Gil Haverty leans back and straightens his bolo tie. # id: banker_loan.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Morning, {player_name}. Coffee? Tell me about {site_name}. # id: banker_loan.open.02 # speaker: banker
* [Ask plainly for the loan. # id: banker_loan.ask.01 # mem: banker met # rel: banker +2]
    Plain talk. I like that. Let me look at what you brought. # id: banker_loan.ask.02 # speaker: banker
* [Hand over a clean, checked folder. # id: banker_loan.ask.03 # skill_req: finance 2 # rel: banker +6]
    Well now. Somebody did their homework. # id: banker_loan.ask.04 # speaker: banker
* [You know I pay on time. # id: banker_loan.ask.05 # show_if_mem: banker paid_on_time # rel: banker +4 # loan: payment_pct -5]
    I do know that. It counts for plenty around here. # id: banker_loan.ask.06 # speaker: banker
* [Gil, we go way back. Help me out. # id: banker_loan.ask.07 # rel_req: banker 60 # loan: payment_pct -8]
    For you, I will sharpen my pencil. # id: banker_loan.ask.08 # speaker: banker
- Gil taps the folder and thinks for a moment. # id: banker_loan.verdict.01 # speaker: narrator
Here is where I land. The bank can do it at this payment. # id: banker_loan.verdict.02 # speaker: banker
* [Take it. Thank you, Gil. # id: banker_loan.verdict.03 # loan: answer yes # rel: banker +3 # mem: banker met]
    Pleasure. Come see me when the doors open. # id: banker_loan.verdict.04 # speaker: banker
    -> END
* [Ask if the payment can come down a bit. # id: banker_loan.verdict.05 # loan: payment_pct -4 # loan: answer yes # rel: banker -2]
    A little. Do not push your luck, friend. # id: banker_loan.verdict.06 # speaker: banker
    -> END
* [Say you need it by Friday, no matter what. # id: banker_loan.verdict.07 # loan: answer no # rel: banker -8]
    Pressure is not how I do business. The answer is no. # id: banker_loan.verdict.08 # speaker: banker
    -> END
* [Offer to come back after your next lease is signed. # id: banker_loan.verdict.09 # loan: answer later # mem: banker met]
    Smart. Bring me a signed lease and we will talk again. # id: banker_loan.verdict.10 # speaker: banker
    -> END

@dialogue/broker_tip.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"
VAR site_name = "the Creekside lot"

-> broker_tip

=== broker_tip ===
{player_name}, it is Jazmine. Got a minute? I have news. # id: broker_tip.open.01 # speaker: top_broker
There is a lot near {site_name} that is not on the market yet. # id: broker_tip.open.02 # speaker: top_broker
The owner wants a quiet sale. I called you first. Do not make me regret it. # id: broker_tip.open.03 # speaker: top_broker
* [Thank her and ask for the details. # id: broker_tip.ask.01 # broker: priority +1 # rel: top_broker +3]
    Good manners. I like that. # id: broker_tip.details.01 # speaker: top_broker
    Corner lot, flat ground, owner is tired of mowing. Go see it. # id: broker_tip.details.02 # speaker: top_broker
    -> END
* [Tell her you know the area is about to grow. # id: broker_tip.ask.02 # skill_req: market_sense 2 # broker: priority +2 # deal: price_pct -3]
    You have been reading the traffic counts. Nice. # id: broker_tip.sense.01 # speaker: top_broker
    Since you see what I see, I will ask the owner to shave the price. # id: broker_tip.sense.02 # speaker: top_broker
    -> END
* [Ask her to put in a word as a friend. # id: broker_tip.ask.03 # rel_req: top_broker 60 # mem: top_broker helped # deal: price_pct -5]
    For you, sure. We go back a ways now. # id: broker_tip.friend.01 # speaker: top_broker
    I told the owner you are good for it. The price just came down. # id: broker_tip.friend.02 # speaker: top_broker
    -> END
* [Say you are too busy right now. # id: broker_tip.ask.04 # broker: priority -2 # rel: top_broker -4]
    Busy, huh. I will call the next person on my list. # id: broker_tip.busy.01 # speaker: top_broker
    You hear the line click. The tip is gone. # id: broker_tip.busy.02 # speaker: narrator
    -> END

@dialogue/brokers_distressed.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR broker_name = "Lupe"
VAR owner_name = "the owner"
VAR site_name = "the old shop on Longhorn Ln"

-> first_look

=== first_look ===
{player_name}, {broker_name}. Owner has to sell. Taxes are late. # id: brokers_distressed.first_look.01 # speaker: broker
{site_name}. {owner_name} needs a buyer who closes, not one who talks. # id: brokers_distressed.first_look.02 # speaker: broker
Three days. Then I call the next buyer. # id: brokers_distressed.first_look.03 # speaker: broker
* [Say you can close fast and fair. # id: brokers_distressed.first_look.04 # broker: priority +2]
    Fair is the word I needed. I will tell {owner_name}. # id: brokers_distressed.first_look.05 # speaker: broker
    -> END
* [Push for a low price since the owner is stuck. # id: brokers_distressed.first_look.06 # deal: price_pct -8 # broker: priority -2]
    You will get it cheap. You will not get my next call first. # id: brokers_distressed.first_look.07 # speaker: broker
    -> END
* [Pass for now. # id: brokers_distressed.first_look.08 # broker: priority -1]
    Fine. Do not wait on the next one. # id: brokers_distressed.first_look.09 # speaker: broker
    -> END

=== late_answer ===
You went quiet on me. I took the site to other buyers. # id: brokers_distressed.late_answer.01 # speaker: broker
* [Say sorry and promise a same day answer next time. # id: brokers_distressed.late_answer.02 # broker: priority +1]
    Same day. I will hold you to it. # id: brokers_distressed.late_answer.03 # speaker: broker
    -> END
* [Say you were busy. # id: brokers_distressed.late_answer.04 # broker: priority -2]
    Everybody is busy. The fast ones still answer. # id: brokers_distressed.late_answer.05 # speaker: broker
    -> END

@dialogue/brokers_text.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR broker_name = "Odell"
VAR owner_name = "the owner"
VAR site_name = "the site on Pecan Hollow Dr"

-> first_look

=== first_look ===
{player_name}. {broker_name}. Got one before anyone else. # id: brokers_text.first_look.01 # speaker: broker
{site_name}. {owner_name} wants it quiet. You get a few days, then I take it to other buyers. # id: brokers_text.first_look.02 # speaker: broker
* [Say you will look at it today. # id: brokers_text.first_look.03 # broker: priority +2]
    That is why I call you first. # id: brokers_text.first_look.04 # speaker: broker
    -> END
* [Ask what the owner really wants. # id: brokers_text.first_look.05 # skill_req: negotiation 2 # broker: priority +1 # deal: price_pct -3]
    Between us? Speed beats price. Offer clean and fast. # id: brokers_text.first_look.06 # speaker: broker
    -> END
* [Say it is not for you. # id: brokers_text.first_look.07 # broker: priority -1]
    No problem. Thanks for the quick answer. # id: brokers_text.first_look.08 # speaker: broker
    -> END

=== lunch ===
{broker_name} picks the booth in the back and orders for both of you. # id: brokers_text.lunch.01 # speaker: narrator
So. What are you hunting for this year? # id: brokers_text.lunch.02 # speaker: broker
* [Tell the truth about what you need. # id: brokers_text.lunch.03 # broker: priority +2]
    Good. Now I know what to send you. # id: brokers_text.lunch.04 # speaker: broker
    -> END
* [Pick up the check. # id: brokers_text.lunch.05 # cash: personal -200 # broker: priority +1]
    Next one is on me. I mean it. # id: brokers_text.lunch.06 # speaker: broker
    -> END
* [Spend lunch on your phone. # id: brokers_text.lunch.07 # broker: priority -2]
    {broker_name} pays and leaves early. # id: brokers_text.lunch.08 # speaker: narrator
    -> END

=== cut_price ===
I heard you cut your price on {owner_name} after you shook on it. # id: brokers_text.cut_price.01 # speaker: broker
My name was on that deal. # id: brokers_text.cut_price.02 # speaker: broker
* [Say the site had problems nobody told you about. # id: brokers_text.cut_price.03 # skill_req: negotiation 3 # broker: priority +1]
    Maybe. Next time, say so before you shake. # id: brokers_text.cut_price.04 # speaker: broker
    -> END
* [Say sorry and say it will not happen again. # id: brokers_text.cut_price.05 # broker: priority +1]
    That helps. It does not fix it. # id: brokers_text.cut_price.06 # speaker: broker
    -> END
* [Say business is business. # id: brokers_text.cut_price.07 # broker: priority -3]
    Then do your business with someone else. # id: brokers_text.cut_price.08 # speaker: broker
    The texts stop. # id: brokers_text.cut_price.09 # speaker: narrator
    -> END

@dialogue/city_hearing.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"
VAR site_name = "Bluebonnet Plaza"

-> city_hearing

=== city_hearing ===
The council room is full. Folding chairs scrape. Folks hold signs. # id: city_hearing.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Next item, {site_name}. Mr. or Ms. {player_name}, you have the floor. # id: city_hearing.open.02 # speaker: mayor
* [Say it plainly. More cars will come, and here is our plan. # id: city_hearing.open.03 # rep: hearing_truth # city: approval_pct +4]
    The room is quiet. A few heads nod. # id: city_hearing.open.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Say traffic will hardly change. # id: city_hearing.open.05 # rep: hearing_spin # city: approval_pct +6 # city: goodwill -3]
    Some folks in the back groan. # id: city_hearing.open.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Thank the town and talk about the new park. # id: city_hearing.open.07 # skill_req: charisma 2 # city: goodwill +4 # rel: mayor +3]
    The mayor smiles. She loves a good park. # id: city_hearing.open.08 # speaker: narrator
- A council member leans in. How bad is the traffic on Main Street? # id: city_hearing.traffic.01 # speaker: council
The city planner flips a page and waits for your answer. # id: city_hearing.traffic.02 # speaker: planner
* [Admit rush hour will be slower and offer a new turn lane. # id: city_hearing.traffic.03 # city: approval_pct +5 # city: goodwill +3 # rel: mayor +3]
    Thank you for being straight with us. # id: city_hearing.traffic.04 # speaker: council
* [Wave off the question and say our study looks fine. # id: city_hearing.traffic.05 # city: approval_pct -4 # rel: mayor -4]
    I asked a simple question. # id: city_hearing.traffic.06 # speaker: council
* [Say you will pay for a new traffic light. # id: city_hearing.traffic.07 # cash: company -20000 # city: goodwill +5]
    That would help a lot. The planner is writing it down. # id: city_hearing.traffic.08 # speaker: planner
- Mayor Vu raps her gavel. We are ready to talk about the fees and the size of the project. # id: city_hearing.deal.01 # speaker: mayor
* [Ask the city to trim the fees. # id: city_hearing.deal.02 # city: fee_pct -5 # city: goodwill -2]
    The council trades looks. They may give a little. # id: city_hearing.deal.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Offer to pay full fees if you can build a bit taller. # id: city_hearing.deal.04 # city: fee_pct +3 # city: density_pct +10 # rel: mayor +2]
    The mayor nods. A fair trade, she says. # id: city_hearing.deal.05 # speaker: mayor
* [Offer a smaller project to calm the neighbors. # id: city_hearing.deal.06 # city: density_pct -10 # city: approval_pct +8 # city: goodwill +3]
    Several neighbors clap. # id: city_hearing.deal.07 # speaker: narrator
- The council takes a vote. # id: city_hearing.vote.01 # speaker: narrator
* [Stand and give your closing words with care. # id: city_hearing.vote.02 # skill_xp: win_hearing # city: approval_pct +5 # rel: mayor +3]
    Four votes to one. The project moves forward. # id: city_hearing.vote.03 # speaker: mayor
    -> END
* [Say thanks and sit down. # id: city_hearing.vote.04 # city: goodwill +1]
    The vote is close, but the project moves ahead. # id: city_hearing.vote.05 # speaker: mayor
    -> END

@dialogue/contractor_invoice.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"
VAR contractor_name = "Hector Salinas"
VAR site_name = "Bluebonnet Plaza"

-> contractor_invoice

=== contractor_invoice ===
{contractor_name} climbs down from the scaffold and hands you a folded paper. # id: contractor_invoice.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Here is the bill for the last stretch at {site_name}, {player_name}. # id: contractor_invoice.open.02 # speaker: contractor
My crew has to eat, so I would like it paid. # id: contractor_invoice.open.03 # speaker: contractor
* [Pay it today, in full. # id: contractor_invoice.pay.01 # rep: pay_contractor_on_time # mem: @contractor paid_on_time # build: speed_pct +5 # cash: company -18000]
    Now that is how you keep a crew happy. We will work faster. # id: contractor_invoice.pay.02 # speaker: contractor
* [Say you will pay it later, when cash is better. # id: contractor_invoice.pay.03 # rep: stall_contractor # mem: @contractor stalled_payment # build: speed_pct -10 # build: surprise_cost_pct +5]
    Later. Sure. Do not be surprised if my guys slow down. # id: contractor_invoice.pay.04 # speaker: contractor
* [Pay half now and half on Friday. # id: contractor_invoice.pay.05 # rel: @contractor +2 # cash: company -9000]
    Half today is fair. Friday, I will hold you to it. # id: contractor_invoice.pay.06 # speaker: contractor
- Hector rubs his neck. One more thing. We found rotten wood behind the wall. # id: contractor_invoice.extra.01 # speaker: contractor
* [Pay the extra cost to fix it right. # id: contractor_invoice.extra.02 # cash: company -4000 # build: surprise_cost_pct -5]
    Good call. A fix now saves a mess later. # id: contractor_invoice.extra.03 # speaker: contractor
    -> END
* [Split the extra cost with him. # id: contractor_invoice.extra.04 # cash: company -2000 # rel: @contractor +2]
    I can live with that. # id: contractor_invoice.extra.05 # speaker: contractor
    -> END
* [Argue it was in the first price. # id: contractor_invoice.extra.06 # rel: @contractor -4 # build: surprise_cost_pct +5]
    No, it was not. We both know that. # id: contractor_invoice.extra.07 # speaker: contractor
    -> END

@dialogue/encounters/airport.ink:
// P3.21 street encounters for map airport. One screen each: one line, 2 or 3 replies, one press. Ids match Data/encounters/index.json.
// Knot = id with dots as underscores. Numbers are guesses for the owner to tune.

=== enc_airport_01 ===
Imani Vos runs freight. She needs a dock building by spring and will sign early. # id: enc.airport.01.line # speaker: broker
* [Tell her you can build it. # id: enc.airport.01.c1 # broker: priority +2]
    -> END
* [Say spring is too soon. # id: enc.airport.01.c2 # broker: priority -1]
    -> END

=== enc_airport_02 ===
A plane passes so low you count the windows. Twenty two. You feel proud. # id: enc.airport.02.line # speaker: narrator
* [Wave at it. # id: enc.airport.02.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Write the number down. # id: enc.airport.02.c2 # cash: personal -1]
    -> END

=== enc_airport_03 ===
A forklift driver dropped a pallet of rubber ducks across the road. He asks for a hand. # id: enc.airport.03.line # speaker: crew
* [Help pick them up. # id: enc.airport.03.c1 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Keep one and drive off. # id: enc.airport.03.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_airport_04 ===
Yara Patel covers her ears as a plane goes over. "Offices hate this. Warehouses do not care. Which are you?" # id: enc.airport.04.line # speaker: owner
* [Say warehouses. # id: enc.airport.04.c1 # broker: priority +1]
    -> END
* [Say offices with thick glass. # id: enc.airport.04.c2 # cash: company -40 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END

=== enc_airport_05 ===
Andre Pak stares at the farm road. "Potholes deep enough for fish. Someone has to fix it." # id: enc.airport.05.line # speaker: crew
* [Pay to fix your stretch. # id: enc.airport.05.c1 # cash: company -150 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Wait for the county. # id: enc.airport.05.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_airport_06 ===
Oksana Duarte from Icehouse Cold Storage wants a freezer warehouse. "Higher rent. Higher build cost. Cold hands." # id: enc.airport.06.line # speaker: tenant
* [Say yes. # id: enc.airport.06.c1 # broker: priority +2]
    -> END
* [Say you build dry boxes only. # id: enc.airport.06.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_airport_07 ===
Chen Medina shows you the old control tower. "Cafe with a view, or knock it down? It has a lot of stairs." # id: enc.airport.07.line # speaker: owner
* [Make it a cafe. # id: enc.airport.07.c1 # cash: company -100 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Knock it down. # id: enc.airport.07.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_airport_08 ===
Coach Ames stands by the school gate. "A truck stop wants your corner. The Truck Watch says no. So do I." # id: enc.airport.08.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Turn the truck stop down. # id: enc.airport.08.c1 # rel: ten +2 # city: goodwill +1]
    -> END
* [Take the deal. # id: enc.airport.08.c2 # cash: company +100 # neighbor: complaints +2]
    -> END

=== enc_airport_09 ===
Ifeoma Garza holds a clipboard. "Your cargo tenant wants customs approval. Your fence has a hole. Fix it?" # id: enc.airport.09.line # speaker: inspector
* [Fix the fence today. # id: enc.airport.09.c1 # cash: company -30 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Patch it with a pallet. # id: enc.airport.09.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_airport_10 ===
Jamal Rahman opens a lost shipping box on your lot. It is full of rubber ducks. Thousands. # id: enc.airport.10.line # speaker: crew
* [Give them to the school. # id: enc.airport.10.c1 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Sell them at the swap meet. # id: enc.airport.10.c2 # cash: personal +20]
    -> END

// Writes on bike_fixer: helped or rent_break. The handshake is in the opening, not in a reply. Step 2 tests it.

=== chain_breakin_1 ===
Late at night, one light is on at your shops. The front window of Second Wind Cycles is all over the sidewalk. # id: chain_breakin_1.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Sol Ferrer is sweeping glass. She does not stop when she sees you. # id: chain_breakin_1.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Hold this. # id: chain_breakin_1.open.03 # speaker: bike_fixer
It is a dustpan. You are part of the cleanup now. # id: chain_breakin_1.open.04 # speaker: narrator
Cash box is gone. So is the orange bike I built for the holidays raffle. # id: chain_breakin_1.open.05 # speaker: bike_fixer
Glass man or rent. I have one of those in me this month. # id: chain_breakin_1.open.06 # speaker: bike_fixer
One thing. If you see that bike, you tell me first. # id: chain_breakin_1.open.07 # speaker: bike_fixer
Not the police. Not the news. I want one good look at whoever it is. # id: chain_breakin_1.open.08 # speaker: bike_fixer
She holds out a hand black with chain grease. You shake it. Now you match. # id: chain_breakin_1.open.09 # speaker: narrator
* [Pay the glass man yourself. Tonight. # id: chain_breakin_1.pick.01 # cash: company -800 # mem: bike_fixer helped # rel: ten +2]
    The glass man comes at midnight. He charges midnight prices. # id: chain_breakin_1.glass.01 # speaker: narrator
    Sol fixes his squeaky ladder while he is still on it. # id: chain_breakin_1.glass.02 # speaker: narrator
    A shop needs a window. Kids buy with their eyes. I owe you one. # id: chain_breakin_1.glass.03 # speaker: bike_fixer
* [Give her a rent break. One month. She fixes the glass. # id: chain_breakin_1.pick.02 # rep: tenant_rent_break # mem: bike_fixer rent_break]
    A month. Good. Then the glass is mine. I know a man. # id: chain_breakin_1.month.01 # speaker: bike_fixer
    She tapes cardboard over the hole for tonight. She writes OPEN on it. In chain grease. # id: chain_breakin_1.month.02 # speaker: narrator
    Do not tell the other shops. They will all start breaking their own windows. # id: chain_breakin_1.month.03 # speaker: bike_fixer
* [Rent is due on the first. Tell her you are sorry about the glass. # id: chain_breakin_1.pick.03 # rel: bike_fixer -6 # rel: bank +2]
    Sorry does not keep the rain out. But I heard you. # id: chain_breakin_1.due.01 # speaker: bike_fixer
    She takes the dustpan back. You were holding it wrong anyway. # id: chain_breakin_1.due.02 # speaker: narrator
    The rent will be on time. Sol will be up all night with cardboard and tape. # id: chain_breakin_1.due.03 # speaker: narrator
- By morning the shop is open. Sol fixes a kid's flat for free. The kid does the pumping. That is the deal. # id: chain_breakin_1.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
The orange bike is out there somewhere. So is your handshake. # id: chain_breakin_1.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
-> END

=== chain_breakin_2 ===
A winter night in Kestrel Flats. By the night dock at Icehouse Cold Storage, an orange bike leans on the fence. # id: chain_breakin_2.open.01 # speaker: narrator
You know that bike. The raffle tag is still on the handlebars. # id: chain_breakin_2.open.02 # speaker: narrator
A kid in a work vest two sizes too big comes out to unlock it. He sees you and stops. # id: chain_breakin_2.open.03 # speaker: narrator
Jonah. I am 15. The last bus leaves at ten. My shift ends at two. # id: chain_breakin_2.open.04 # speaker: neighbor
The cash box is under my bed. I have not opened it. # id: chain_breakin_2.open.05 # speaker: neighbor
I keep going to bring it back. I get as far as the corner. Eleven times now. # id: chain_breakin_2.open.06 # speaker: neighbor
I oil the chain every week. I did not want her to get it back rusty. # id: chain_breakin_2.open.07 # speaker: neighbor
Your phone buzzes. Channel 6 Glade News: who is the bike bandit. Air time for whoever finds him. # id: chain_breakin_2.open.08 # speaker: narrator
The bike bandit is holding his lunch box with both hands. # id: chain_breakin_2.open.09 # speaker: narrator
* [Keep your word. Call Sol first. Wait with the kid. # id: chain_breakin_2.pick.01 # rep: honor_handshake # mem: bike_fixer honored_deal]
    Sol picks up on the first ring. You can hear a wrench. # id: chain_breakin_2.word.01 # speaker: narrator
    Stay put. Both of you. I am bringing the truck. # id: chain_breakin_2.word.02 # speaker: bike_fixer
    You wait on the curb with the bike bandit. He gives you half his sandwich. # id: chain_breakin_2.word.03 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 buzzes again. You let it buzz. # id: chain_breakin_2.word.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Call the police line. Not Sol. Not the news. # id: chain_breakin_2.pick.02 # rel: bike_fixer -3 # rel: ten +1 # city: goodwill +1]
    The officer on the line is calm. She asks Jonah to wait. He waits. # id: chain_breakin_2.book.01 # speaker: narrator
    He holds the bike up straight the whole time. So it does not get scratched. # id: chain_breakin_2.book.02 # speaker: narrator
    You did it by the book. It is not the book you shook on. # id: chain_breakin_2.book.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Call Channel 6. You, the bike and the bandit, live at six. # id: chain_breakin_2.pick.03 # rep: take_better_offer # mem: bike_fixer broke_deal]
    The Channel 6 van is there in nine minutes. It has never been that fast for weather. # id: chain_breakin_2.live.01 # speaker: narrator
    A bright light comes on. Jonah pulls his hood up. You fix your hair. # id: chain_breakin_2.live.02 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: bike bandit bagged. Developer cracks the case. Story at six. And at ten. # id: chain_breakin_2.live.03 # speaker: narrator
    You are famous until Thursday. Sol finds out from her own TV. # id: chain_breakin_2.live.04 # speaker: narrator
- The orange bike gets a ride home tonight. It is the only one here with nothing to explain. # id: chain_breakin_2.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Sol runs the raffle again when the holidays come. She will remember tonight. So will Jonah. # id: chain_breakin_2.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
-> END

Raffle day at Second Wind Cycles. The line of kids runs out the door and past two more of your shops. # id: chain_breakin_3.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Every kid has a ticket in one hand and a flat tire in the other. # id: chain_breakin_3.open.02 # speaker: narrator
The raffle bike sits in the window with a bow on it. # id: chain_breakin_3.open.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Look at the pump. Jonah is there, in an apron that fits. # id: chain_breakin_3.door.01 # show_if_mem: bike_fixer honored_deal # rel: bike_fixer +2]
    That night Sol looked at him for one whole minute. Then she handed him a broom. # id: chain_breakin_3.kept.01 # speaker: narrator
    He works Saturdays now. He built this year's raffle bike. It is orange. # id: chain_breakin_3.kept.02 # speaker: narrator
    He owed me a window. He has paid for two. # id: chain_breakin_3.kept.03 # speaker: bike_fixer
    Hold this. # id: chain_breakin_3.kept.04 # speaker: bike_fixer

* [Look at the window. Bars. Sol works the line alone. # id: chain_breakin_3.door.02 # show_if_mem: bike_fixer broke_deal # rel: ten -2]
    The clip ran three nights. Your face, the bike, the kid. # id: chain_breakin_3.sold.01 # speaker: narrator
    You shook my hand. Then you sold a boy for a headline. # id: chain_breakin_3.sold.02 # speaker: bike_fixer
    She says it to the tire she is fixing. Her hands never stop. # id: chain_breakin_3.sold.03 # speaker: narrator

// Street chain "Student Driver", step 1 of 4 (writer A). Prairie Star Corridor, day. Starts the chain.
// Writes the Winnie memory: driving_teacher helped (kind) or burned (sour). The fair reply writes none.
// Plan: Docs/story/chains.md section 5.1. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> chain_fender_1

=== chain_fender_1 ===
Red light on the freeway side road. Something taps your bumper. Twice. Gently. # id: chain_fender_1.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Behind you sits a mint green car as long as a boat. The sign on its roof says STUDENT DRIVER. # id: chain_fender_1.open.02 # speaker: narrator
The student has both hands on the wheel and both eyes shut. # id: chain_fender_1.open.03 # speaker: narrator
The teacher rolls her window down, one turn at a time. She counts to three. # id: chain_fender_1.open.04 # speaker: narrator
Winnie Pascoe. Easy Does It Driving School. The car is the Duchess. # id: chain_fender_1.open.05 # speaker: driving_teacher
And that is where we would have stopped. # id: chain_fender_1.open.06 # speaker: driving_teacher
Mirror. Signal. Brake. That was the brake's cousin, Tobias. # id: chain_fender_1.open.07 # speaker: driving_teacher
Tobias, 16, opens one eye. # id: chain_fender_1.open.08 # speaker: narrator
Did we stop? # id: chain_fender_1.open.09 # speaker: neighbor
We did, Tobias. We had help. # id: chain_fender_1.open.10 # speaker: driving_teacher
* [Laugh. Tell the kid everybody hits something once. # id: chain_fender_1.pick.01 # mem: driving_teacher helped]
    Tobias opens the other eye. It is a start. # id: chain_fender_1.kind.01 # speaker: narrator
    Winnie hands you a coupon through the window. One free lesson. # id: chain_fender_1.kind.02 # speaker: narrator
    The stop sign back there. That is where you would have stopped. Use the coupon. # id: chain_fender_1.kind.03 # speaker: driving_teacher
* [Swap names. The school pays for the bumper. # id: chain_fender_1.pick.02 # cash: personal +150 # rel: driving_teacher +2]
    Winnie writes a check on the hood. In pen. She parks every letter between the lines. # id: chain_fender_1.fair.01 # speaker: narrator
    There. Even. Tobias, say thank you to the bumper. # id: chain_fender_1.fair.02 # speaker: driving_teacher
    Thank you, bumper. # id: chain_fender_1.fair.03 # speaker: neighbor
* [Make a scene. You want cash now, from the kid. # id: chain_fender_1.pick.03 # cash: personal +300 # mem: driving_teacher burned # rel: ten -2]
    Tobias counts out his lunch money. Then his bus money. You take all of it. # id: chain_fender_1.sour.01 # speaker: narrator
    Winnie looks at you for three full seconds. # id: chain_fender_1.sour.02 # speaker: narrator
    Noted. # id: chain_fender_1.sour.03 # speaker: driving_teacher
- The light turns green. The Duchess hops one foot and stops. You will see that car again. # id: chain_fender_1.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Green means go, Tobias. It does not mean hop. # id: chain_fender_1.hook.02 # speaker: driving_teacher
-> END

// Street chain "Student Driver", step 2 of 4 (writer A). Creekside, summer. Fires 21 days after step 1. Now it is your fault.
// Writes the Winnie memory: driving_teacher paid_on_time (pay now) or burned (lie). The card reply writes none.
// Plan: Docs/story/chains.md section 5.1. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> chain_fender_2

=== chain_fender_2 ===
Grackle weather in Creekside. You back out of a tiny spot by the Green Trolley barn. Crunch. In your mirror: mint green, and a sign on the roof. # id: chain_fender_2.open.01 # speaker: narrator
The Duchess was parked. Today's lesson was parking. It had been going well. # id: chain_fender_2.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Winnie Pascoe sits in the passenger seat with a sandwich. A new student holds the wheel. # id: chain_fender_2.open.03 # speaker: narrator
She finishes her bite. She counts to three. # id: chain_fender_2.open.04 # speaker: narrator
We have met. Last time it was my turn. # id: chain_fender_2.open.05 # speaker: driving_teacher
And that is where you would have looked. # id: chain_fender_2.open.06 # speaker: driving_teacher
Her tail light is all over the street. The student nods at you. The student has not stopped nodding. # id: chain_fender_2.open.07 # speaker: narrator
Mirror. Signal. Look. Next time, pick any one. # id: chain_fender_2.open.08 # speaker: driving_teacher
* [Own it. Pay for her tail light right now. # id: chain_fender_2.pick.01 # cash: personal -200 # mem: driving_teacher paid_on_time # rel: driving_teacher +4]
    You pay on the spot. Winnie writes a receipt on a sandwich napkin. In pen. # id: chain_fender_2.pay.01 # speaker: narrator
    Same day. I have old students who still owe me from 1989. # id: chain_fender_2.pay.02 # speaker: driving_teacher
    She tapes the light back on herself. The tape lives in the glove box, next to the spare sandwich. # id: chain_fender_2.pay.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Own it. Leave your card and your word. # id: chain_fender_2.pick.02 # rel: driving_teacher +5]
    Winnie reads your card. Then she reads the back. The back is blank. # id: chain_fender_2.card.01 # speaker: narrator
    A card and a word. I will keep both in the glove box. # id: chain_fender_2.card.02 # speaker: driving_teacher
    The student nods. For once it fits. # id: chain_fender_2.card.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Say her car rolled into you. Her student nods at everything. # id: chain_fender_2.pick.03 # cash: personal +100 # mem: driving_teacher burned]
    You say the Duchess rolled into you. You look at the student. The student nods. # id: chain_fender_2.sour.01 # speaker: narrator
    Winnie counts to three. Twice. Then she pays you out of the lesson envelope. # id: chain_fender_2.sour.02 # speaker: narrator
    The Duchess has not rolled since 1994. Noted. # id: chain_fender_2.sour.03 # speaker: driving_teacher
- You get back in. Mirror. Signal. Look. You pull out like it is a test. # id: chain_fender_2.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
There. All three. Somebody taught you once. I will finish the job. # id: chain_fender_2.hook.02 # speaker: driving_teacher
-> END

// Street chain "Student Driver", step 3 of 4 (writer A). Grackle Yards, game night in the holidays season. Fires 30 days after step 2.
// Writes no memory. Moves Winnie and your tenants. Cameo: Rocco Benedetti counts meatballs.
// Plan: Docs/story/chains.md section 5.1. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> chain_fender_3

=== chain_fender_3 ===
Game night at Grackle Yards, with holiday lights on every food truck. A crowd has formed, and not for the game. Somebody is trying to park a mint green car. # id: chain_fender_3.open.01 # speaker: narrator
The Duchess is as long as a boat. The gap between the two food trucks is as long as a canoe. It has been 20 minutes. # id: chain_fender_3.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Rocco Benedetti works the crowd with a tray. # id: chain_fender_3.open.03 # speaker: narrator
Forty meatballs. For parking. Nobody help that kid. # id: chain_fender_3.open.04 # speaker: neighbor
Winnie Pascoe stands on the curb with four cones. Calm as a pond. # id: chain_fender_3.open.05 # speaker: narrator
Left. Left. And that is where we would have gone left. # id: chain_fender_3.open.06 # speaker: driving_teacher
She sees you. She counts to three. # id: chain_fender_3.open.07 # speaker: narrator
I am one cone short. You are about the right height. # id: chain_fender_3.open.08 # speaker: driving_teacher
* [Be the cone. Stand very still. # id: chain_fender_3.pick.01 # rel: driving_teacher +6 # rel: ten +2]
    You stand where the cone goes. You hold very still. A kid in the crowd salutes you. # id: chain_fender_3.cone.01 # speaker: narrator
    The Duchess slides in. It misses you by one meatball. # id: chain_fender_3.cone.02 # speaker: narrator
    Best cone I have had all year. The others are plastic. # id: chain_fender_3.cone.03 # speaker: driving_teacher
* [Park it for the kid. One try. In front of everybody. # id: chain_fender_3.pick.02 # rel: ten +4 # rel: driving_teacher -3]
    You take the wheel. One try. Not a scratch. The crowd goes wild. # id: chain_fender_3.show.01 # speaker: narrator
    The student climbs out and claps for you. Winnie does not. # id: chain_fender_3.show.02 # speaker: narrator
    He learned nothing. You learned to show off. # id: chain_fender_3.show.03 # speaker: driving_teacher
    Sixty meatballs. Do it again. # id: chain_fender_3.show.04 # speaker: neighbor
* [Buy the whole crowd meatballs while they wait. # id: chain_fender_3.pick.03 # cash: personal -60 # rel: ten +5]
    A hundred meatballs. I mean it. Nobody help that kid. # id: chain_fender_3.treat.01 # speaker: neighbor
    The crowd eats. The student keeps trying. Try nine goes in clean. Nobody sees it. They are chewing. # id: chain_fender_3.treat.02 # speaker: narrator
    He did it alone. That is the only way it counts. # id: chain_fender_3.treat.03 # speaker: driving_teacher
- Inside Grackle Field, somebody hits a home run. Out here, nobody looks up. # id: chain_fender_3.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Next week we do the freeway. # id: chain_fender_3.hook.02 # speaker: driving_teacher
I am going to need a bigger tray. # id: chain_fender_3.hook.03 # speaker: neighbor
-> END

// Street chain "Student Driver", step 4 of 4, the payoff (writer A). Any district, a spring day. Fires 30 days after step 3.
// Door memory: driving_teacher burned (written in step 1 or step 2). The "stand next to Winnie" reply is the prize for two decent turns.
// Plan: Docs/story/chains.md section 5.1. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> chain_fender_4

=== chain_fender_4 ===
A spring morning. A mint green car as long as a boat is double parked in front of you. On purpose. Winnie Pascoe stands beside it with a clipboard. # id: chain_fender_4.open.01 # speaker: narrator
She counts to three. You have learned to wait. # id: chain_fender_4.open.02 # speaker: narrator
The tight corner by the Green Trolley barn. Eleven bumps this year. I was in the car for six. # id: chain_fender_4.open.03 # speaker: driving_teacher
The council counts bumps on Thursday. Enough bumps, and the corner gets a four way stop. # id: chain_fender_4.open.04 # speaker: driving_teacher
I need people who were in one. They stand up at the council hearing and say so. # id: chain_fender_4.open.05 # speaker: driving_teacher
You were in one. Creekside. Summer. Her tail light. # id: chain_fender_4.open.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Look at the clipboard. She saved you line one. # id: chain_fender_4.door.01 # hide_if_mem: driving_teacher burned # rel: driving_teacher +2]
    The list runs four pages. Every driver she ever taught is on it. # id: chain_fender_4.list.01 # speaker: narrator
    The bus driver. The tow truck man. The woman who drives your concrete truck. # id: chain_fender_4.list.02 # speaker: narrator
    They all stop for me. Now they stop for you. # id: chain_fender_4.list.03 # speaker: driving_teacher
* [Reach for the clipboard. She holds it to her chest. # id: chain_fender_4.door.02 # show_if_mem: driving_teacher burned # rel: ten -2]
    You are in my notes. You are not on my list. # id: chain_fender_4.cold.01 # speaker: driving_teacher
    A parking officer walks up to your car. He nods to Winnie. She taught him too. He is writing something. # id: chain_fender_4.cold.02 # speaker: narrator
    He is very thorough. I taught him that. # id: chain_fender_4.cold.03 # speaker: driving_teacher
-
* [Stand up Thursday. Tell the truth. One of the bumps was yours. # id: chain_fender_4.pick.01 # rep: hearing_truth # cash: company -1500 # city: goodwill +3]
    Thursday. You stand up. You tell the council you backed into a parked driving school. # id: chain_fender_4.truth.01 # speaker: narrator
    The council counts your bump. Then it mails you a share of the bill for the new stop. # id: chain_fender_4.truth.02 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: council approves four way stop at the trolley barn corner. # id: chain_fender_4.news.01 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: developer confesses. The victim was parked. # id: chain_fender_4.news.02 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: four stop signs on one corner now. Where do I park. # id: chain_fender_4.news.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Say you never saw a bump there. Slow cars are bad for your shops. # id: chain_fender_4.pick.02 # rep: hearing_spin # rel: driving_teacher -6]
    Thursday. You tell the council you never saw a bump at that corner. Not one. # id: chain_fender_4.spin.01 # speaker: narrator
    Winnie sits in the third row. She writes one word on her clipboard. You can guess the word. # id: chain_fender_4.spin.02 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: council puts off four way stop for more study. # id: chain_fender_4.news.04 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: is your corner safe. Developer says yes. The corner could not be reached. # id: chain_fender_4.news.05 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: got bumped at the trolley barn again. Also, where do I park. # id: chain_fender_4.news.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Stand up next to Winnie. Let her do the talking. # id: chain_fender_4.pick.03 # hide_if_mem: driving_teacher burned # rel_req: driving_teacher 62 # rep: hearing_truth # city: goodwill +4 # build: speed_pct +3]
    Thursday. Every seat holds one of her old students. Every one of them parked legally. # id: chain_fender_4.side.01 # speaker: narrator
    I taught half this room to stop. I would like a sign to help with the other half. # id: chain_fender_4.side.02 # speaker: driving_teacher
    The council votes yes before she sits down. The city pays for the stop. Her drivers start getting your trucks there early. # id: chain_fender_4.side.03 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: four way stop passes without one no. Council thanks its driving teacher. # id: chain_fender_4.news.07 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: one woman stops an entire city. Story at six. # id: chain_fender_4.news.08 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: I had Winnie in 1998. I still signal in my own driveway. Where do I park. # id: chain_fender_4.news.09 # speaker: narrator
* [Sign nothing. Wish her luck. # id: chain_fender_4.pick.04 # rel: driving_teacher -2]
    Winnie counts to three. # id: chain_fender_4.luck.01 # speaker: narrator
    Luck is for people who do not signal. # id: chain_fender_4.luck.02 # speaker: driving_teacher
    Thursday, she fills two rows without you. The stop passes by one vote. # id: chain_fender_4.luck.03 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: council approves four way stop at the trolley barn corner, by one vote. # id: chain_fender_4.news.10 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: stop sign squeaks through. So do the brakes. Story at six. # id: chain_fender_4.news.11 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: which developer skipped the hearing. And where do they park. # id: chain_fender_4.news.12 # speaker: narrator
- A week later the Duchess rolls up beside you. The window comes down, one turn at a time. # id: chain_fender_4.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Tobias passed. Third try. He drives the Channel 6 van now. Watch your bumper. # id: chain_fender_4.hook.02 # speaker: driving_teacher
-> END

=== chain_hustle_1 ===
A folding table sits under the Exit 14 water tower. The banner says NAME THIS TOWER. TODAY ONLY. # id: chain_hustle_1.open.01 # speaker: narrator
The man behind it wears a suit one size too big. His business card lists six businesses. # id: chain_hustle_1.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Lyle Tolliver. Lucky Lyle. I know that face. You were on Channel 6. # id: chain_hustle_1.open.03 # speaker: fast_talker
Picture it. {company_name}. Up there. Forty feet tall. # id: chain_hustle_1.open.04 # speaker: fast_talker
Planes will read it. Birds will read it. Today only. # id: chain_hustle_1.open.05 # speaker: fast_talker
He has a clipboard and a paint chart. The chart has one color. It is the color the tower already is. # id: chain_hustle_1.open.06 # speaker: narrator
He does not own the tower. The county does. Nobody has told the clipboard. # id: chain_hustle_1.open.07 # speaker: narrator
* [Buy it. Your name on a water tower. What could go wrong. # id: chain_hustle_1.pick.01 # cash: personal -300 # mem: fast_talker fair_price]
    Sold. You have a good eye and cash on you. My two favorite things. # id: chain_hustle_1.sold.01 # speaker: fast_talker
    He writes a receipt in crayon. It says PAID. Under that, smaller, it says PROBABLY. # id: chain_hustle_1.sold.02 # speaker: narrator
    Paint goes up next week. Or the week after. Technically, soon. # id: chain_hustle_1.sold.03 # speaker: fast_talker
* [Ask to see the deed. # id: chain_hustle_1.pick.02 # rel: fast_talker +3]
    A deed. Of course. A careful buyer. I love a careful buyer. # id: chain_hustle_1.deed.01 # speaker: fast_talker
    He has a deed. It is for a different tower. It is in crayon. # id: chain_hustle_1.deed.02 # speaker: narrator
    Technically, I am selling the idea. # id: chain_hustle_1.deed.03 # speaker: fast_talker
    You give the idea back. He takes it well. He has had practice. # id: chain_hustle_1.deed.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Out talk him. Sell him his own folding table. # id: chain_hustle_1.pick.03 # skill_req: negotiation 2 # cash: personal +100 # rel: fast_talker +6 # miss: Nice try. I sold that same pitch to the man who taught it to you.]
    A man with six businesses needs a real desk, you say. This one. Today only. # id: chain_hustle_1.table.01 # speaker: narrator
    He nods. He nods faster. He pays you for the table he is standing behind. # id: chain_hustle_1.table.02 # speaker: narrator
    Wait. That was mine. That was beautiful. Who are you? # id: chain_hustle_1.table.03 # speaker: fast_talker
* [Call the county about the man selling its tower. # id: chain_hustle_1.pick.04 # mem: fast_talker burned # city: goodwill +2]
    The county says thank you. The county says it will send somebody. # id: chain_hustle_1.county.01 # speaker: narrator
    By the time you hang up, the banner is down and the clipboard is gone. # id: chain_hustle_1.county.02 # speaker: narrator
    No hard feelings. I never forget a face. Technically, that is a promise. # id: chain_hustle_1.county.03 # speaker: fast_talker
- Then he folds the table. Flat, in four seconds. He is gone before the light changes. # id: chain_hustle_1.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
You have a feeling you will see that table again. # id: chain_hustle_1.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
-> END

=== chain_hustle_2 ===
Game night at Grackle Yards. You know that folding table. The new banner says GAME DAY TREASURES. TODAY ONLY. # id: chain_hustle_2.open.01 # speaker: narrator
You! I never forget a face. Look at this. A baseball signed by Gus the Grackle. # id: chain_hustle_2.open.02 # speaker: fast_talker
The name is in marker. A feather is taped to the ball. For proof. # id: chain_hustle_2.open.03 # speaker: narrator
And watches. Tickwel. One L. Technically a different company. # id: chain_hustle_2.open.04 # speaker: fast_talker
A man in a Game Day Merchants vest is coming this way. He has a clipboard too. His looks real. # id: chain_hustle_2.open.05 # speaker: narrator
Lyle puts the cash box in your hands. # id: chain_hustle_2.open.06 # speaker: narrator
Watch the table. Five minutes. I have to move my car. # id: chain_hustle_2.open.07 # speaker: fast_talker
He does not have a car. # id: chain_hustle_2.open.08 # speaker: narrator
* [Sell a watch while he is gone. You are good at this. # id: chain_hustle_2.pick.01 # cash: personal +50 # rel: ten -2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    You sell a Tickwel to a man in a Grackles cap. It ticks. That is all it does. # id: chain_hustle_2.watch.01 # speaker: narrator
    The hands do not move. He finds out in the third inning. # id: chain_hustle_2.watch.02 # speaker: narrator
    The man in the vest writes down your name. He spells it right. That is the bad part. # id: chain_hustle_2.watch.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Tell every customer the truth. One L. # id: chain_hustle_2.pick.02 # rel: ten +3 # rel: fast_talker -2]
    One L, you tell them. Not the real one. The feather is from a pillow. # id: chain_hustle_2.truth.01 # speaker: narrator
    A woman buys the baseball anyway. She says her dog will not know the difference. # id: chain_hustle_2.truth.02 # speaker: narrator
    The man in the vest puts his pen away. Nothing to write. He looks almost sad. # id: chain_hustle_2.truth.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Fold the table. Keep his things safe until he is back. # id: chain_hustle_2.pick.03 # mem: fast_talker helped]
    Lyle folds this table in four seconds. It takes you nine. You pinch a finger. # id: chain_hustle_2.fold.01 # speaker: narrator
    The man in the vest finds a flat table and a shut box. Nothing to write down. # id: chain_hustle_2.fold.02 # speaker: narrator
    You sit on the folded table with the box in your lap. You do not open it. Lyle would have. # id: chain_hustle_2.fold.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Ask where your water tower name is. # id: chain_hustle_2.pick.04 # show_if_mem: fast_talker fair_price # cash: personal +100 # rel: fast_talker -1]
    Lyle was almost gone. He walks back slowly. # id: chain_hustle_2.tower.01 # speaker: narrator
    The tower. Yes. The paint is on order. Technically, the ladder is on order. # id: chain_hustle_2.tower.02 # speaker: fast_talker
    You hold out your hand. He counts some of your money back into it. Not all of it. # id: chain_hustle_2.tower.03 # speaker: narrator
    Call the rest a deposit. On my good name. Now I really must move the car. # id: chain_hustle_2.tower.04 # speaker: fast_talker
- Lyle is back in six minutes, on foot. He says the car is fine. # id: chain_hustle_2.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
He counts the cash box. Twice. He looks at you. He counts it again. # id: chain_hustle_2.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
By the last inning the banner is down. TODAY ONLY is over until tomorrow. # id: chain_hustle_2.hook.03 # speaker: narrator
-> END
