=== chain_hustle_3 ===
A winter day downtown. Lyle Tolliver stands on the corner with no table. His suit fits. # id: chain_hustle_3.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Something is wrong with Lucky Lyle. He looks scared. # id: chain_hustle_3.open.02 # speaker: narrator
I have a real one. An honest deal. I do not know what to do with it. # id: chain_hustle_3.open.03 # speaker: fast_talker
I was outside one of the dark towers. Selling warm air. In jars. Winter special. # id: chain_hustle_3.open.04 # speaker: fast_talker
A man bought a jar. Then he told me a secret. An owner who has to sell. A deal nobody else has seen. # id: chain_hustle_3.open.05 # speaker: fast_talker
It is all true. I checked. I did not even need the word technically. # id: chain_hustle_3.open.06 # speaker: fast_talker
He wants a finder's fee, on a handshake. His hand is out. It is already shaking a little. # id: chain_hustle_3.open.07 # speaker: narrator
* [Shake on it. Pay his fee today, in full. # id: chain_hustle_3.pick.01 # hide_if_mem: fast_talker burned # rep: pay_contractor_on_time # mem: fast_talker paid_on_time # cash: company -2000 # broker: priority +3]
    You pay him on the spot. He holds the check up to the light. # id: chain_hustle_3.paid.01 # speaker: narrator
    It is real. I checked it the way I would check one of mine. # id: chain_hustle_3.paid.02 # speaker: fast_talker
    The tip is real too. You hear about the building before any broker in town. # id: chain_hustle_3.paid.03 # speaker: narrator
    I told the truth and got paid. It felt strange. I may try it twice. # id: chain_hustle_3.paid.04 # speaker: fast_talker
* [Shake on it. Take the tip. Never pay. Who would he tell. # id: chain_hustle_3.pick.02 # hide_if_mem: fast_talker burned # rep: take_better_offer # mem: fast_talker burned # broker: priority +3]
    You shake. You take the address. The fee is coming, you say. Technically, soon. # id: chain_hustle_3.stiff.01 # speaker: narrator
    Lyle knows that word. He taught it to half the town. # id: chain_hustle_3.stiff.02 # speaker: narrator
    The tip is real. For once, the fake thing on this corner was not his. # id: chain_hustle_3.stiff.03 # speaker: narrator
    He does not yell. He takes out a card and writes your name on the back. # id: chain_hustle_3.stiff.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Buy the tip at double. He already sold it once this morning. # id: chain_hustle_3.pick.03 # show_if_mem: fast_talker burned # cash: company -4000 # broker: priority +2]
    For you, double. You called the county on me. I had to buy a whole new banner. # id: chain_hustle_3.double.01 # speaker: fast_talker
    Also, I sold it once already this morning. Technically, he bought the idea. You get the address. # id: chain_hustle_3.double.02 # speaker: fast_talker
    You pay. The address is real. You are second in line for it. # id: chain_hustle_3.double.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Walk away. Nothing Lyle sells is real. # id: chain_hustle_3.pick.04 # rel: fast_talker -3]
    Lyle watches you go. He does not run after you. That is new. # id: chain_hustle_3.walk.01 # speaker: narrator
    It is real this time. # id: chain_hustle_3.walk.02 # speaker: fast_talker
    He says it to a pigeon. The pigeon has heard that before. # id: chain_hustle_3.walk.03 # speaker: narrator
    A week later the building sells to somebody else. It was real. # id: chain_hustle_3.walk.04 # speaker: narrator
- Lyle stays on the corner a while. One honest deal. He looks at his own hand like it did it without him. # id: chain_hustle_3.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
His folding table has the day off. Tables like that never stay folded. # id: chain_hustle_3.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
-> END

=== chain_hustle_4 ===
A summer day. A folding table is set up outside your building. You know that table. # id: chain_hustle_4.open.01 # speaker: narrator
There is a banner. Of course there is a banner. # id: chain_hustle_4.open.02 # speaker: narrator
* [Walk up to the table. Lyle is behind it. There is a line. # id: chain_hustle_4.door.01 # hide_if_mem: fast_talker burned # rel: fast_talker +2]
    The banner says LEASE HERE. TODAY ONLY. # id: chain_hustle_4.line.01 # speaker: narrator
    The line is real. A florist. A dentist. A man with a pizza oven on a trailer. # id: chain_hustle_4.line.02 # speaker: narrator
    I told them the truth. It felt strange. They lined up anyway. # id: chain_hustle_4.line.03 # speaker: fast_talker
    I said the developer is straight with table people. Technically I am the only table person. It still counts. # id: chain_hustle_4.line.04 # speaker: fast_talker
* [Walk up to the table. Three strangers. Each one has a banner. # id: chain_hustle_4.door.02 # show_if_mem: fast_talker burned # rel: ten -1]
    Each one bought the right to name your building. From Lyle. Today only. # id: chain_hustle_4.names.01 # speaker: narrator
    One banner says HAPPY BIRTHDAY DOREEN. # id: chain_hustle_4.names.02 # speaker: narrator
    Doreen is my wife. She is going to love this. It is her building now, right? # id: chain_hustle_4.names.03 # speaker: neighbor
    They all have receipts. In crayon. # id: chain_hustle_4.names.04 # speaker: narrator
    Lyle is not here. His new card is. It lists seven businesses. The new one is naming rights. # id: chain_hustle_4.names.05 # speaker: narrator
-
* [Let him work the line. Pay him for every lease that signs. # id: chain_hustle_4.pick.01 # hide_if_mem: fast_talker burned # rel: ten +5 # broker: priority +2]
    Paid after the work. I have never tried it in that order. # id: chain_hustle_4.work.01 # speaker: fast_talker
    By five the florist has signed. So has the dentist. The pizza man wants to see the roof. # id: chain_hustle_4.work.02 # speaker: narrator
    Lyle describes the roof from memory. He has never been up there. Every word turns out true. # id: chain_hustle_4.work.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Give him a desk. One business. One card. No table. # id: chain_hustle_4.pick.02 # hide_if_mem: fast_talker burned # cash: company -1500 # rel: fast_talker +10 # rel: ten +3]
    A desk. With drawers. He sits down slowly, like it might fold. # id: chain_hustle_4.desk.01 # speaker: narrator
    One business. One card. What do I do with the other five? # id: chain_hustle_4.desk.02 # speaker: fast_talker
    The new card says Lyle Tolliver, Leasing. He reads it four times. # id: chain_hustle_4.desk.03 # speaker: narrator
    It is all true. Every word. I do not know where to put the technically. # id: chain_hustle_4.desk.04 # speaker: fast_talker
* [Give the three of them their money back yourself. # id: chain_hustle_4.pick.03 # show_if_mem: fast_talker burned # cash: company -900 # rel: ten +4]
    You pay back all three. In real money. They check it like it is the other kind. # id: chain_hustle_4.refund.01 # speaker: narrator
    The man with the Doreen banner asks if it can hang for one day anyway. # id: chain_hustle_4.refund.02 # speaker: narrator
    You say yes. For one day your building is named HAPPY BIRTHDAY DOREEN. Doreen brings cake. # id: chain_hustle_4.refund.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Tell them a crayon receipt is a crayon receipt. # id: chain_hustle_4.pick.04 # show_if_mem: fast_talker burned # rel: ten -4 # neighbor: complaints +2]
    A crayon receipt is a crayon receipt, you say. Nobody can argue with that. All three try. # id: chain_hustle_4.crayon.01 # speaker: narrator
    They leave. One banner stays, tied to your door handle. It is the Doreen one. # id: chain_hustle_4.crayon.02 # speaker: narrator
    Doreen hears about it by dinner. Doreen has a very big family. They shop somewhere else now. # id: chain_hustle_4.crayon.03 # speaker: narrator
- The table folds flat in four seconds. It has done that before. # id: chain_hustle_4.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
-> END

// Street chain "Story Hour", step 1 of 4 (writer A). Your site, a spring day. Starts the chain (minFame 10, needs a project).
// Writes the Bernie memory: site_protester helped (shake and sit) or burned (carried off). The plain shake writes none.
// Cameo: Amos Tulley scores once. Plan: Docs/story/chains.md section 5.2. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> chain_protest_1

=== chain_protest_1 ===
A spring morning at your site, and it is too quiet. The whole crew has stopped work to listen to one woman whisper. # id: chain_protest_1.open.01 # speaker: narrator
She stands on a library step stool under the big oak. Her chalkboard says SAVE THE STORY OAK. # id: chain_protest_1.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Save the oak. Save the oak. You may join in. Quietly. # id: chain_protest_1.open.03 # speaker: site_protester
Amos Tulley has moved his lawn chair next to her. # id: chain_protest_1.open.04 # speaker: narrator
Three. Letters too small. # id: chain_protest_1.open.05 # speaker: fence_regular
Bernadette Stroud. Bernie. I read to kids under this tree every Saturday for 31 years. # id: chain_protest_1.open.06 # speaker: site_protester
You are the developer from Channel 6. Your loading dock goes right where I am standing. # id: chain_protest_1.open.07 # speaker: site_protester
I am not against your building. I am against one saw. # id: chain_protest_1.open.08 # speaker: site_protester
Give me until the council votes in the fall. If they will not protect the tree, I fold my stool for good. # id: chain_protest_1.open.09 # speaker: site_protester
She holds out her hand. # id: chain_protest_1.open.10 # speaker: narrator
* [Shake on it. The saw waits for the vote. # id: chain_protest_1.pick.01 # rel: site_protester +5 # build: speed_pct -3]
    Her grip is firm. Librarians carry a lot of books. # id: chain_protest_1.shake.01 # speaker: narrator
    We shook. I will tell the oak. # id: chain_protest_1.shake.02 # speaker: site_protester
    The crew goes back to work. They hammer a little softer than before. # id: chain_protest_1.shake.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Shake on it. Then sit down for one story. # id: chain_protest_1.pick.02 # mem: site_protester helped # rel: ten +2 # build: speed_pct -3]
    You sit down in the dirt. So does the crew. Hard hats off. # id: chain_protest_1.story.01 # speaker: narrator
    She reads the one about a bear who is late for supper. She does every voice. In a whisper. # id: chain_protest_1.story.02 # speaker: narrator
    We shook. And you sat still. Not many developers can do both. # id: chain_protest_1.story.03 # speaker: site_protester
    The foreman asks if there is a second book. There is. # id: chain_protest_1.story.04 # speaker: narrator
* [No deal. Have the crew carry her and the stool to the sidewalk. Gently. # id: chain_protest_1.pick.03 # mem: site_protester burned # neighbor: complaints +2 # build: speed_pct +3]
    Two of the crew lift the stool with her still on it. She rides it to the sidewalk like a parade float. # id: chain_protest_1.carry.01 # speaker: narrator
    I have shushed four mayors. I can shush a bulldozer. # id: chain_protest_1.carry.02 # speaker: site_protester
    From the sidewalk she rings a small bell. Once. The crew gets back to work. Nobody whistles. # id: chain_protest_1.carry.03 # speaker: narrator
- Amos Tulley turns his lawn chair to face the oak. He has found something better than a hole. # id: chain_protest_1.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Same time tomorrow. Bring a friend. Quietly. # id: chain_protest_1.hook.02 # speaker: site_protester
-> END

=== chain_protest_3 ===
One week before the council vote. A big tenant will sign today, for more rent. They want the loading dock where the oak stands. They want the tree gone by Friday. # id: chain_protest_3.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Their man waits in a rental car. The lease is on his knee. The engine is running. # id: chain_protest_3.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Bernie is on her stool under the oak. Somebody hung one string of holiday lights on the lowest branch. # id: chain_protest_3.open.03 # speaker: narrator
She has heard. News travels fast in a whisper. # id: chain_protest_3.open.04 # speaker: narrator
Friday. I heard Friday. # id: chain_protest_3.open.05 # speaker: site_protester
She says it in a normal voice. It lands like a shout. Two of the crew take their hard hats off. # id: chain_protest_3.open.06 # speaker: narrator
That tree has waited 200 years for most things. You cannot wait seven days? # id: chain_protest_3.open.07 # speaker: site_protester
The saw is in the truck. The lease is in the car. The oak is where it has always been. # id: chain_protest_3.open.08 # speaker: narrator
* [Keep the handshake. Wait for the vote. # id: chain_protest_3.pick.01 # hide_if_mem: site_protester burned # rep: honor_handshake # mem: site_protester honored_deal]
    The rental car pulls out. It takes the big rent with it. # id: chain_protest_3.keep.01 # speaker: narrator
    We shook. # id: chain_protest_3.keep.02 # speaker: site_protester
    She is whispering again. That is how you know it is all right. # id: chain_protest_3.keep.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Take the tenant. The oak comes down Friday. # id: chain_protest_3.pick.02 # hide_if_mem: site_protester burned # rep: take_better_offer # mem: site_protester evicted # cash: company +8000]
    You sign on the hood of the rental car. The rent is very good. # id: chain_protest_3.take.01 # speaker: narrator
    We shook. # id: chain_protest_3.take.02 # speaker: site_protester
    Normal voice. She folds her stool. It is the loudest sound on the site. # id: chain_protest_3.take.03 # speaker: narrator
    Story hour is evicted. # id: chain_protest_3.take.04 # speaker: site_protester
* [Cut it Friday. You never shook on anything. # id: chain_protest_3.pick.03 # show_if_mem: site_protester burned # mem: site_protester evicted # cash: company +8000 # neighbor: complaints +3]
    You sign on the hood of the rental car. The rent is very good. # id: chain_protest_3.cut.01 # speaker: narrator
    No. We never shook. I remember. I was being carried at the time. # id: chain_protest_3.cut.02 # speaker: site_protester
    She folds her stool. It is the loudest sound on the site. # id: chain_protest_3.cut.03 # speaker: narrator
    Story hour is evicted. # id: chain_protest_3.cut.04 # speaker: site_protester
* [Redraw the plan. The dock moves. The oak stays. # id: chain_protest_3.pick.04 # cash: company -6000 # build: speed_pct -5 # rel: site_protester +10 # city: goodwill +3]
    You draw the dock on the other side. The hood of the rental car makes a fine desk. # id: chain_protest_3.move.01 # speaker: narrator
    The new dock costs more and takes longer. The tenant's man says he will ask his boss. # id: chain_protest_3.move.02 # speaker: narrator
    You moved a building for a tree. I did not know they moved. # id: chain_protest_3.move.03 # speaker: site_protester
    She is whispering again. On the chalkboard she adds two words. THANK YOU. Small letters. # id: chain_protest_3.move.04 # speaker: narrator
- Fence Line: so is the oak thing settled. Asking because of parking. # id: chain_protest_3.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Settled or not, Bernie knows where she will be on Saturday mornings. # id: chain_protest_3.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
-> END

Saturday morning in spring. Ten o'clock. You walk to the edge of your site. Here, one woman on a step stool once whispered a whole crew to a stop. # id: chain_protest_4.open.01 # speaker: narrator

    Six kids sit in the gravel. Behind them, trucks back up to your dock. Beep. Beep. Beep. # id: chain_protest_4.stump.01 # speaker: narrator

    Brock Delacroix is parked across the street. There is a tree in a pot in the back of his truck. It has a sign. # id: chain_protest_4.stump.03 # speaker: narrator
    My truck has more trees than your site. Cute. # id: chain_protest_4.stump.04 # speaker: rival
- We start at ten. You are on time. That is something. # id: chain_protest_4.ten.01 # speaker: site_protester

    Shh. Whisper the bear. # id: chain_protest_4.read.02 # speaker: site_protester
    You whisper the bear. A hundred kids lean in. Two council members in the back row lean in too. # id: chain_protest_4.read.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Build a little free library box under the oak. # id: chain_protest_4.pick.02 # hide_if_mem: site_protester evicted # cash: company -500 # rel: ten +5 # city: goodwill +3]
    Your crew builds it by lunch. A box on a post, with a door and a roof. # id: chain_protest_4.box.01 # speaker: narrator
    It is the smallest thing you have ever built. It is full in one hour. # id: chain_protest_4.box.02 # speaker: narrator
    I expect returns on time. I know where you work. # id: chain_protest_4.box.03 # speaker: site_protester
* [Plant a new oak. Tell her it will be ready in 80 years. # id: chain_protest_4.pick.03 # show_if_mem: site_protester evicted # cash: company -300 # rel: site_protester +8]
    The new oak is as tall as the six kids. It has nine leaves. You counted. # id: chain_protest_4.plant.01 # speaker: narrator
    Eighty years. Then I will need a taller stool. # id: chain_protest_4.plant.02 # speaker: site_protester
    She whispers it. It is the first whisper you have had from her since the saw. # id: chain_protest_4.plant.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Walk past. A stump makes a fine bench. # id: chain_protest_4.pick.04 # show_if_mem: site_protester evicted # rel: ten -3]
    You walk past. Six kids watch you go. One of them waves. Kids will wave at anybody. # id: chain_protest_4.past.01 # speaker: narrator
    And that, children, is the developer. # id: chain_protest_4.past.02 # speaker: site_protester
    Normal voice. All six kids turn around and look. # id: chain_protest_4.past.03 # speaker: narrator
- Fence Line: story hour is Saturdays at ten. Bring your own chair. Where do I park. # id: chain_protest_4.hook.01 # speaker: narrator

// Street chain chain.tourist, step 1 of 3 (writer C). The Wrong Map. Redbud Square, a spring day. Gate: maxHeat 30.
// Writes: lost_mapmaker helped or burned. Reads nothing. The small book comes back in step 3.
// Plan: Docs/story/chains.md section 5.5. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> chain_tourist_1

=== chain_tourist_1 ===
A man in a tan vest stands in the middle of Redbud Square. He turns a paper map around and around. # id: chain_tourist_1.open.01 # speaker: narrator
The vest has nine pockets. The map has one coffee ring, from 1974. # id: chain_tourist_1.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Pardon me. Is this Varney Street? # id: chain_tourist_1.open.03 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
It is not. There is no Varney Street. Your phone has never heard of it. # id: chain_tourist_1.open.04 # speaker: narrator
He taps the map. There it is, in neat blue ink. Varney St. # id: chain_tourist_1.open.05 # speaker: narrator
Osgood Varney. I drew this map. The county promised me one street for it. # id: chain_tourist_1.open.06 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
I am not lost. I know exactly where I am. It is the town that moved. # id: chain_tourist_1.open.07 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
I turned left where the drive in was. The drive in is a bank now. I do not think it shows films. # id: chain_tourist_1.open.08 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
* [Walk him to the map room at the old courthouse yourself. # id: chain_tourist_1.pick.01 # mem: lost_mapmaker helped]
    You walk him over. He sets the pace. It is a good pace. # id: chain_tourist_1.walk.01 # speaker: narrator
    The map room has every county map since 1886. He checks them all. Varney Street is on none of them. # id: chain_tourist_1.walk.02 # speaker: narrator
    Then they are all wrong in the same way. That is very interesting. # id: chain_tourist_1.walk.03 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    He hands you a pencil from pocket two. It has no eraser. # id: chain_tourist_1.walk.04 # speaker: narrator
    A gift. I have never needed that end. # id: chain_tourist_1.walk.05 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
* [Tell him the truth. There is no Varney Street. # id: chain_tourist_1.pick.02 # rel: lost_mapmaker +3]
    He looks at you. Then at the map. Then at the whole square. # id: chain_tourist_1.truth.01 # speaker: narrator
    Not yet. # id: chain_tourist_1.truth.02 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    Thank you for not pointing. Most people point somewhere, to be polite. # id: chain_tourist_1.truth.03 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    So far I have been pointed at the lake, the airport and a car wash. # id: chain_tourist_1.truth.04 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
* [Charge him for directions. Point at the freeway. # id: chain_tourist_1.pick.03 # cash: personal +5 # mem: lost_mapmaker burned]
    He pays in exact change, from pocket six. # id: chain_tourist_1.fee.01 # speaker: narrator
    A fee for directions. In my day they were free and wrong. # id: chain_tourist_1.fee.02 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    He looks where you pointed. Then at the map. Then at you. # id: chain_tourist_1.fee.03 # speaker: narrator
    That is the freeway. I drew the freeway. My street is not on it. # id: chain_tourist_1.fee.04 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    You pocket the money. He folds the map, slowly, along the old lines. # id: chain_tourist_1.fee.05 # speaker: narrator
- He takes a small book from pocket four and writes two words in it. He does not show you which two. # id: chain_tourist_1.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Then he walks off across the square, counting his steps out loud. # id: chain_tourist_1.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
-> END

// Street chain chain.tourist, step 2 of 3 (writer C). The Wrong Map. Lakefront, a summer day. Fires 30 days after step 1.
// Writes: lost_mapmaker burned (sour reply only). Reads nothing. Here the player learns what he is looking for.
// Cameo: Margaret Thistlewood and her fishing pole, sour branch only.
// Plan: Docs/story/chains.md section 5.5. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> chain_tourist_2

=== chain_tourist_2 ===
A man stands ankle deep in Lake Cedar, in his socks. His shoes hang around his neck. He holds a paper map over his head. # id: chain_tourist_2.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Tan vest. Nine pockets. You know that vest. # id: chain_tourist_2.open.02 # speaker: narrator
According to this, I am in a pecan orchard. # id: chain_tourist_2.open.03 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
The lake came in 1985. His map is from 1974. Row four, third tree is somewhere near his left sock. # id: chain_tourist_2.open.04 # speaker: narrator
The county promised me a street for drawing this map. Varney Street. They never built it. # id: chain_tourist_2.open.05 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
I have been walking on paper for 50 years. # id: chain_tourist_2.open.06 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
Every line I drew starts at the orchard gate. The gate is under there. So I start here. # id: chain_tourist_2.open.07 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
He holds out a ball of red string. The other end is tied to his belt. # id: chain_tourist_2.open.08 # speaker: narrator
* [Take the string. Wade in. # id: chain_tourist_2.pick.01 # cash: personal -40 # rel: lost_mapmaker +8]
    The lake is warm. Your shoes were new. # id: chain_tourist_2.wade.01 # speaker: narrator
    Left. More left. Stop. You are standing on the gate. # id: chain_tourist_2.wade.02 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    You feel it under your foot. An iron latch. Nobody has opened it since 1985. # id: chain_tourist_2.wade.03 # speaker: narrator
    Good. Now I know where everything else is. # id: chain_tourist_2.wade.04 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    A fish looks at your ankle and thinks better of it. # id: chain_tourist_2.wade.05 # speaker: narrator
* [Hold the string from the dock. Dry. # id: chain_tourist_2.pick.02 # rel: lost_mapmaker +4]
    You stay on the dock. He walks out until the string goes tight. # id: chain_tourist_2.dock.01 # speaker: narrator
    A little slack, please. Less. That is not less. # id: chain_tourist_2.dock.02 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    A duck swims through the string. Twice. He measures around the duck. # id: chain_tourist_2.dock.03 # speaker: narrator
    Thank you. A dry helper is still a helper. # id: chain_tourist_2.dock.04 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
* [Tell the Hillside Homeowners League a stranger is measuring their lake. # id: chain_tourist_2.pick.03 # mem: lost_mapmaker burned # city: goodwill +1]
    Margaret Thistlewood is on the dock in four minutes, with her fishing pole. # id: chain_tourist_2.league.01 # speaker: narrator
    Margaret Thistlewood, Hillside. Sir, this lake has been measured. It is the right size. # id: chain_tourist_2.league.02 # speaker: neighbor
    Madam, I was here before the lake. I have it in writing. # id: chain_tourist_2.league.03 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    She holds the fishing pole up next to him. He is not taller than the trees. He still has to go. # id: chain_tourist_2.league.04 # speaker: narrator
    You made a telephone call. Sound carries on a lake. It never carried in the orchard. # id: chain_tourist_2.league.05 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
- He rolls the red string back into a ball and puts it in pocket seven. # id: chain_tourist_2.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Then he turns the map a quarter turn and looks toward the far edge of town. # id: chain_tourist_2.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
Varney Street is not in the lake. He has plenty of string left. # id: chain_tourist_2.hook.03 # speaker: narrator
-> END

VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

=== chain_tourist_3 ===
After dark at Greenfield Edge, four little flags stand in an empty field. A lantern swings between them. # id: chain_tourist_3.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Behind the lantern is a man with nine pockets. # id: chain_tourist_3.open.02 # speaker: narrator
* [Walk toward the lantern. He waves it. He has been waiting to show somebody. # id: chain_tourist_3.door.01 # hide_if_mem: lost_mapmaker burned # rel: lost_mapmaker +2]
    There you are. Mind your feet. You are standing in the middle of the road. # id: chain_tourist_3.found.01 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    He opens the small book to page one. Two words. Not yet. He crosses them out. # id: chain_tourist_3.found.02 # speaker: narrator
    Sixty feet wide. A quarter mile long. It runs between two fences. # id: chain_tourist_3.found.03 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    The county drew it in 1974 and forgot it. I did not. # id: chain_tourist_3.found.04 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    Red string runs from flag to flag. Nobody owns this ground but the county. # id: chain_tourist_3.found.05 # speaker: narrator
    And it runs along good dirt. Both sides. # id: chain_tourist_3.found.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Walk toward the lantern. He folds the map when he sees you. # id: chain_tourist_3.door.02 # show_if_mem: lost_mapmaker burned # rel: lost_mapmaker +1]
    Good evening. I found it. I thought you should know that I found it. # id: chain_tourist_3.late.01 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    Sixty feet wide. A quarter mile long. The county forgot it. I did not. # id: chain_tourist_3.late.02 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    I have already shown someone. A loud young man in a tall truck bought me pie. # id: chain_tourist_3.late.03 # speaker: lost_mapmaker
    He asked very good questions. He wrote the answers on his hand. # id: chain_tourist_3.late.04 # speaker: lost_mapmaker

// Street chain chain.wedding, step 1 of 4 (writer C). Hard Hat Wedding. Lakefront, a spring day. Gate: minHonor -19.
// Writes no memory. The free reply is worth 8 with Cricket, which the shop reply in step 4 counts.
// Plan: Docs/story/chains.md section 5.6. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> chain_wedding_1

=== chain_wedding_1 ===
A bride, a groom and nine people in matching yellow stand at a fence on the Lakefront. They are all looking at weeds. # id: chain_wedding_1.open.01 # speaker: narrator
A woman with a headset, two phones and a clipboard walks straight at you. # id: chain_wedding_1.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Cricket Mayhew. Mayhew Weddings. Mayhew, not mayhem. People get that wrong. # id: chain_wedding_1.open.03 # speaker: wedding_planner
The bluebonnet field got mowed this morning. The photos are at noon. The bride has seen the field. # id: chain_wedding_1.open.04 # speaker: wedding_planner
Behind the fence, on the empty lot by the marina, the weeds are in bloom. Yellow. They match the dresses. # id: chain_wedding_1.open.05 # speaker: narrator
I asked around. Everybody says you know everybody. Also that you are not scary. I asked that part twice. # id: chain_wedding_1.open.06 # speaker: wedding_planner
One call from you opens that gate. I have a bride, a groom and eleven minutes. # id: chain_wedding_1.open.07 # speaker: wedding_planner
* [Make the call. Hold the gate. Carry the train over the mud. # id: chain_wedding_1.pick.01 # rel: wedding_planner +8]
    The owner picks up on the second ring. The gate is open in four minutes. # id: chain_wedding_1.gate.01 # speaker: narrator
    You hold the gate with one foot and the train with both hands. # id: chain_wedding_1.gate.02 # speaker: narrator
    The bride is Nora. She looks at the weeds for a long time. # id: chain_wedding_1.gate.03 # speaker: narrator
    They are prettier than the bluebonnets. Nobody tell the bluebonnets. # id: chain_wedding_1.gate.04 # speaker: neighbor
    You get mud to the knee. You are in two of the photos, holding a dress. # id: chain_wedding_1.gate.05 # speaker: narrator
* [Make the call. Charge a small finder's fee. # id: chain_wedding_1.pick.02 # cash: personal +100 # rel: wedding_planner -2]
    The gate is open in four minutes. Your fee takes five. # id: chain_wedding_1.fee.01 # speaker: narrator
    A fee. For a gate. To a field of weeds. Fine. It goes on the list. # id: chain_wedding_1.fee.02 # speaker: wedding_planner
    She pays from an envelope marked EMERGENCIES. It is a thick envelope. # id: chain_wedding_1.fee.03 # speaker: narrator
    The bridesmaids carry the train themselves. One of them watches you the whole time. # id: chain_wedding_1.fee.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Sorry. You are late for the bank. # id: chain_wedding_1.pick.03 # rel: wedding_planner -4 # rel: bank +2]
    You are on time at the bank, for once. The bank notices. # id: chain_wedding_1.bank.01 # speaker: narrator
    In your mirror, nine people in yellow are lifting a groom over a fence. # id: chain_wedding_1.bank.02 # speaker: narrator
    His name is Gideon. You know that because they are all yelling it. # id: chain_wedding_1.bank.03 # speaker: narrator
    Cricket does not wave. She writes something on the clipboard. Then she underlines it. # id: chain_wedding_1.bank.04 # speaker: narrator
- Both of her phones ring at once. She answers both. # id: chain_wedding_1.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Next is the cake, the band and the weather. It is fine. It is all fine. # id: chain_wedding_1.hook.02 # speaker: wedding_planner
-> END

// Writes no memory. The free reply is worth 8 with Cricket, which the shop reply in step 4 counts.
// Cameo: Brock drives past twice, free reply only. No line for him here. His one "Cute." is in step 4.
// Plan: Docs/story/chains.md section 5.6. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

=== chain_wedding_2 ===
A van sits on the freeway side road with its hood up and steam pouring out. The side says SUNUP KOLACHES. # id: chain_wedding_2.open.01 # speaker: narrator
A woman is fanning the back doors with a clipboard. Headset. Two phones. You know her. # id: chain_wedding_2.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Cricket Mayhew. Mayhew, not mayhem. Oh. It is you. Good. # id: chain_wedding_2.open.03 # speaker: wedding_planner
The van is cooked, the tasting is in one hour and the tower is going soft. # id: chain_wedding_2.open.04 # speaker: wedding_planner
Inside is a tower of 300 kolaches. It is taller than the groom. It has started to lean. # id: chain_wedding_2.open.05 # speaker: narrator
It is grackle weather. Three grackles on the wire are watching the tower. # id: chain_wedding_2.open.06 # speaker: narrator
Nora and Gideon pick their wedding kolache today. There are nine kinds. Gideon has notes on all nine. # id: chain_wedding_2.open.07 # speaker: wedding_planner
Your car has cold air. I can hear it from here. It sounds beautiful. # id: chain_wedding_2.open.08 # speaker: wedding_planner
* [Load the tower in your back seat. Drive like it is glass. # id: chain_wedding_2.pick.01 # rel: wedding_planner +8 # rel: ten +2]
    The tower rides in your back seat with a seat belt on. Cricket holds the top. # id: chain_wedding_2.glass.01 # speaker: narrator
    You take every bump at two miles an hour. # id: chain_wedding_2.glass.02 # speaker: narrator
    Brock passes you. He goes around the block and passes you again. # id: chain_wedding_2.glass.03 # speaker: narrator
    Slower. That was a pebble. I felt that pebble. # id: chain_wedding_2.glass.04 # speaker: wedding_planner
    The tower gets there standing. Sunup Kolaches hears who drove it. # id: chain_wedding_2.glass.05 # speaker: narrator
* [Rent her your cold air by the mile. # id: chain_wedding_2.pick.02 # cash: personal +150 # rel: wedding_planner -3]
    By the mile. Bless your heart. Van, steam, meter. It goes on the list. # id: chain_wedding_2.meter.01 # speaker: wedding_planner
    It is four miles. You take the long way. It is six. # id: chain_wedding_2.meter.02 # speaker: narrator
    She pays from an envelope marked EMERGENCIES. She counts it twice. # id: chain_wedding_2.meter.03 # speaker: narrator
    The tower gets there standing. Cricket says thank you, out of habit. # id: chain_wedding_2.meter.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Buy a dozen off the top. They are going soft anyway. # id: chain_wedding_2.pick.03 # cash: personal -12 # rel: wedding_planner -4]
    You take twelve off the top. Now it is a tower of 288. # id: chain_wedding_2.dozen.01 # speaker: narrator
    That was the apricot row. Gideon had two pages on the apricot row. # id: chain_wedding_2.dozen.02 # speaker: wedding_planner
    They are very good. They are a little warm. # id: chain_wedding_2.dozen.03 # speaker: narrator
    Cricket waves down a tow truck, a bread truck and a man on a riding mower. The mower stops. # id: chain_wedding_2.dozen.04 # speaker: narrator
    The tower gets to the tasting at four miles an hour, with grass on it. # id: chain_wedding_2.dozen.05 # speaker: narrator
- Both of her phones ring at once. She answers both. # id: chain_wedding_2.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Next is the ballroom, the band and the weather. The ballroom is the easy one. It is fine. It is all fine. # id: chain_wedding_2.hook.02 # speaker: wedding_planner
-> END

After dark, a flashlight is walking around your site downtown. It has a hard hat on over a headset. # id: chain_wedding_3.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Cricket Mayhew. Mayhew, not mayhem. Do not be mad. Your night guard is holding my other phone. # id: chain_wedding_3.open.02 # speaker: wedding_planner
The ballroom pipe burst, the dance floor is a pond and the band is standing on chairs. # id: chain_wedding_3.open.03 # speaker: wedding_planner
140 guests come tomorrow at four. Nora does not know yet. Gideon knows. Gideon is lying down. # id: chain_wedding_3.open.04 # speaker: wedding_planner
She points the flashlight up at your half built top floor. # id: chain_wedding_3.open.05 # speaker: narrator
It has a roof. Mostly. It has a view. It is perfect. # id: chain_wedding_3.open.06 # speaker: wedding_planner
The sign on your fence says HARD HATS PAST THIS POINT. She is well past that point. # id: chain_wedding_3.open.07 # speaker: narrator
One night. 140 chairs. I will sweep it myself. # id: chain_wedding_3.open.08 # speaker: wedding_planner
* [Yes. No charge. Your crew strings the work lights. # id: chain_wedding_3.pick.01 # mem: wedding_planner helped # rel: ten +4 # build: speed_pct -3]
    Your crew stays late. Nobody has to ask them twice. # id: chain_wedding_3.lights.01 # speaker: narrator
    The lift holds two tons. How big is this cake? # id: chain_wedding_3.lights.02 # speaker: crew
    By midnight the work lights hang in rows. The concrete mixer has a bow on it. # id: chain_wedding_3.lights.03 # speaker: narrator
    You lose a day of work. The top floor has never looked better. # id: chain_wedding_3.lights.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Yes. For a fair fee, and everyone wears a hard hat. # id: chain_wedding_3.pick.02 # mem: wedding_planner helped # cash: company +3000]
    A fee and 140 hard hats. Done. Done. Where do I get 140 hard hats. Done. # id: chain_wedding_3.fee.01 # speaker: wedding_planner
    She pays from an envelope marked EMERGENCIES. This is what it was for. # id: chain_wedding_3.fee.02 # speaker: narrator
    By midnight nine bridesmaids are tying yellow ribbon on hard hats. # id: chain_wedding_3.fee.03 # speaker: narrator
    Your contractor counts the hats twice. He wants them all back. # id: chain_wedding_3.fee.04 # speaker: narrator
* [No. If one guest trips on one board, it is your name on Channel 6. # id: chain_wedding_3.pick.03 # rel: wedding_planner -6 # rel: bank +2]
    The bank that paid for this building would agree with you. # id: chain_wedding_3.no.01 # speaker: narrator
    No. Right. No is an answer. I have a list of answers and no is on it. # id: chain_wedding_3.no.02 # speaker: wedding_planner
    She takes off the hard hat and hangs it on your fence, neatly. # id: chain_wedding_3.no.03 # speaker: narrator
    She walks off into the dark. A block away, a very tall truck slows down next to her flashlight. # id: chain_wedding_3.no.04 # speaker: narrator

Tomorrow. Four o'clock. 140 guests. It is fine. It is all fine. # id: chain_wedding_3.hook.02 # speaker: wedding_planner

The front page of the Cedar Glade Courier is taped to a shop window. It is a wedding photo, and you know the bride. # id: chain_wedding_4.open.01 # speaker: narrator
A woman with a headset and two phones is looking at it too. You know her as well. # id: chain_wedding_4.open.02 # speaker: narrator
* [Look closer. The bride is in a hard hat. That is your building. # id: chain_wedding_4.door.01 # show_if_mem: wedding_planner helped # rel: ten +2]
    140 guests in hard hats. The first dance was on plywood. # id: chain_wedding_4.hat.01 # speaker: narrator
    The groom's grandmother rode the work lift. Then she asked to go again. # id: chain_wedding_4.hat.02 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: couple marries on top floor of half built building. # id: chain_wedding_4.news.01 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: bride in a hard hat. Is your wedding safe. Story at six. # id: chain_wedding_4.news.02 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: lovely wedding. 140 guests. Where did they all park. # id: chain_wedding_4.news.03 # speaker: narrator
    Cricket Mayhew. Hard hat weddings. That is what I do now. Nine booked, four waiting, one wants a crane. # id: chain_wedding_4.hat.03 # speaker: wedding_planner
    Every florist, baker and tuxedo shop I know wants to be near that roof. # id: chain_wedding_4.hat.04 # speaker: wedding_planner
* [Look closer. The bride is standing in the bed of a lifted truck. # id: chain_wedding_4.door.02 # hide_if_mem: wedding_planner helped # rel: ten +1]
    The wedding happened in a motel parking lot. The truck was the stage. # id: chain_wedding_4.truck.01 # speaker: narrator
    The horn played the wedding march. It only knows the first half. # id: chain_wedding_4.truck.02 # speaker: narrator
    Cricket Mayhew. He was driving by. He had a truck, a speaker and a speech. I had a pond. # id: chain_wedding_4.truck.03 # speaker: wedding_planner
    A very tall truck rolls up beside you. It still has ribbon on the mirrors. # id: chain_wedding_4.truck.04 # speaker: narrator
    I gave the toast. Nobody asked me to. 140 guests. They all know my name now. Cute. # id: chain_wedding_4.truck.05 # speaker: rival
- Cricket looks at the photo. Then at you. Both phones are quiet. That never happens. # id: chain_wedding_4.window.01 # speaker: narrator
* [Lease her the small shop by the door. Mayhew Weddings. # id: chain_wedding_4.pick.01 # show_if_mem: wedding_planner helped # rel_req: wedding_planner 70 # rel: ten +6 # broker: priority +3]
    A shop. With a door. And a sign. I have worked out of a van for nine years. # id: chain_wedding_4.shop.01 # speaker: wedding_planner
    She signs the clipboard. Then the lease. Then the clipboard again. # id: chain_wedding_4.shop.02 # speaker: narrator
    By Friday the florist, the baker and the tuxedo shop have all called. They want the space next door. # id: chain_wedding_4.shop.03 # speaker: narrator
    The sign goes up. MAYHEW WEDDINGS. Under it, smaller: NOT MAYHEM. # id: chain_wedding_4.shop.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Open the roof for weddings. Charge for it. # id: chain_wedding_4.pick.02 # show_if_mem: wedding_planner helped # cash: company +2000 # rel: ten +2]
    You put a price on the roof. Cricket books four dates before you finish the sentence. # id: chain_wedding_4.roof.01 # speaker: narrator
    Hard hats are extra. The lift ride is free for grandmothers. # id: chain_wedding_4.roof.02 # speaker: narrator
    Your tenants like a Saturday crowd in good shoes. # id: chain_wedding_4.roof.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Send the couple a gift. Dinner for two. # id: chain_wedding_4.pick.03 # cash: personal -100 # rel: wedding_planner +5]
    You send Nora and Gideon dinner for two at Casa Cielito. # id: chain_wedding_4.gift.01 # speaker: narrator
    A thank you card comes back in two days. Gideon wrote it. It has notes. # id: chain_wedding_4.gift.02 # speaker: narrator
    Dinner for two. I heard. I hear everything. It was the right table. # id: chain_wedding_4.gift.03 # speaker: wedding_planner
* [Tell Cricket. Next time, you say yes. # id: chain_wedding_4.pick.04 # hide_if_mem: wedding_planner helped # rel: wedding_planner +4]
    Next time. She writes it on the clipboard. Then she takes a photo of it with both phones. # id: chain_wedding_4.next.01 # speaker: narrator
    I have a wedding in June. The barn has a goat problem. I will call you. # id: chain_wedding_4.next.02 # speaker: wedding_planner
    The tall truck pulls away. The ribbon stays on the mirrors. # id: chain_wedding_4.next.03 # speaker: narrator
- Both of her phones ring at once. She answers both. # id: chain_wedding_4.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
It is fine. It is all fine. # id: chain_wedding_4.hook.02 # speaker: wedding_planner

@dialogue/encounters/city.ink:
// P3.21 street encounters for map city. One screen each: one line, 2 or 3 replies, one press. Ids match Data/encounters/index.json.
// Knot = id with dots as underscores. Numbers are guesses for the owner to tune.

=== enc_city_01 ===
You find a lucky penny face up. Then a dollar. Then nothing else ever again. # id: enc.city.01.line # speaker: narrator
* [Keep it. # id: enc.city.01.c1 # cash: personal +1]
    -> END
* [Leave it for someone else. # id: enc.city.01.c2 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_02 ===
Nadia Crowe from the paper asks what you think of the city in three words. # id: enc.city.02.line # speaker: reporter
* [Say growing, proud, ready. # id: enc.city.02.c1 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Say no comment. # id: enc.city.02.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_03 ===
A kid sells lemonade on the corner. Fifty cents. It is mostly ice. # id: enc.city.03.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Buy one. # id: enc.city.03.c1 # cash: personal -1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Buy the whole jug. # id: enc.city.03.c2 # cash: personal -10 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Pat your pockets. Just lint. Tell him the sign looks great. # id: enc.city.03.c3 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_04 ===
Your car radio picks up a station that only plays a cow. Mooing. On air. At noon. # id: enc.city.04.line # speaker: narrator
* [Keep listening. # id: enc.city.04.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Change it. # id: enc.city.04.c2 # cash: personal -1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_05 ===
Your banker is at the same coffee shop. She says hello and asks how the year is going. # id: enc.city.05.line # speaker: banker
* [Tell her straight how it is. # id: enc.city.05.c1 # rel: banker +3]
    -> END
* [Say everything is perfect. # id: enc.city.05.c2 # rel: banker -1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_06 ===
You pass go. Nobody pays you two hundred. You check twice. # id: enc.city.06.line # speaker: narrator
* [Shrug. # id: enc.city.06.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Collect it yourself from your own wallet. # id: enc.city.06.c2 # cash: personal -200 # cash: company +200]
    -> END

=== enc_city_07 ===
A painter asks if you know anyone hiring. He has his own brushes. # id: enc.city.07.line # speaker: contractor
* [Give him a card. # id: enc.city.07.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Say you will ask around. # id: enc.city.07.c2 # broker: priority +1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_08 ===
Brock Delacroix pulls up at the light and grins. "Nice car. Shame about your last deal." # id: enc.city.08.line # speaker: rival
* [Smile and say nothing. # id: enc.city.08.c1 # rel: rival +1]
    -> END
* [Tell him to watch the road. # id: enc.city.08.c2 # rel: rival -2]
    -> END

=== enc_city_09 ===
A pigeon lands on your hood and refuses to leave for two blocks. # id: enc.city.09.line # speaker: narrator
* [Name it. # id: enc.city.09.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Wash the car after. # id: enc.city.09.c2 # cash: personal -12]
    -> END

=== enc_city_10 ===
A street sign has your name on it. Spelled wrong. The city says it is a coincidence. # id: enc.city.10.line # speaker: narrator
* [Ask them to fix it. # id: enc.city.10.c1 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END
* [Take a photo and frame it. # id: enc.city.10.c2 # cash: personal -25]
    -> END

=== enc_city_11 ===
Carmen Pham walks a cat on a leash past your office. The cat looks at you like it owns the block. # id: enc.city.11.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Nod to the cat. # id: enc.city.11.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Ask the cat for rent. # id: enc.city.11.c2 # cash: personal +1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_12 ===
Mayor Rosalind Vu stops you on the steps. "People say you keep your word. I need a builder like that." # id: enc.city.12.line # speaker: mayor
* [Offer to help. # id: enc.city.12.c1 # rel: mayor +2 # city: goodwill +1]
    -> END
* [Say you are busy this year. # id: enc.city.12.c2 # rel: mayor -1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_13 ===
Vikram Nakamura slides a card across a diner table. "I hear you play rough. I like rough. Call me." # id: enc.city.13.line # speaker: investor
* [Take the card. # id: enc.city.13.c1 # rel: inv +2]
    -> END
* [Leave it on the table. # id: enc.city.13.c2 # rel: inv -1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_14 ===
Gil Haverty from the bank spots you in line for coffee. "Rates may move next quarter. Come see me." # id: enc.city.14.line # speaker: banker
* [Book a time. # id: enc.city.14.c1 # rel: banker +1]
    -> END
* [Say you will call. # id: enc.city.14.c2 # rel: banker -1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_15 ===
Sofia Zielinski the inspector buys you a soda. "You run clean jobs. Keep it that way and I keep it quick." # id: enc.city.15.line # speaker: inspector
* [Thank her. # id: enc.city.15.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Ask if quick can mean quicker. # id: enc.city.15.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_16 ===
A man in a sandwich board yells that the end is near. Tariq Sokolov asks if your lofts have parking. # id: enc.city.16.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Give him a flyer. # id: enc.city.16.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Say the end has no parking. # id: enc.city.16.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_17 ===
Malik Greer from your old crew waves from a cherry picker. "Need hands next job? I am free in June." # id: enc.city.17.line # speaker: crew
* [Save him a spot. # id: enc.city.17.c1 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Say you are full. # id: enc.city.17.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_18 ===
Every streetlight on your street blinks at once. Then again. Rania Coleman on her porch says it does this every full moon. # id: enc.city.18.line # speaker: narrator
* [Wave at the lights. # id: enc.city.18.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Call the city. # id: enc.city.18.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_19 ===
Jazmine Treviño catches you at a red light. "I have a buyer who wants what you have. Want me to bring them?" # id: enc.city.19.line # speaker: top_broker
* [Say bring them. # id: enc.city.19.c1 # broker: priority +2]
    -> END
* [Say not for sale. # id: enc.city.19.c2 # rel: top_broker -1]
    -> END

=== enc_city_20 ===
Zainab Eze stops you to say your sign is upside down. It is not. She is standing on her head. # id: enc.city.20.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Stand on your head too. # id: enc.city.20.c1 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Keep walking. # id: enc.city.20.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

@dialogue/encounters/corner.ink:
// P3.21 street encounters for map corner. One screen each: one line, 2 or 3 replies, one press. Ids match Data/encounters/index.json.
// Knot = id with dots as underscores. Numbers are guesses for the owner to tune.

=== enc_corner_01 ===
Celeste Halloway waves you over by the rail yard. "I would sell you the air over track three. Just the air. Interested?" # id: enc.corner.01.line # speaker: owner
* [Say you want to talk price soon. # id: enc.corner.01.c1 # broker: priority +2]
    -> END
* [Say sky is not for sale in your book. # id: enc.corner.01.c2 # rel: top_broker -1]
    -> END

=== enc_corner_02 ===
Theo Banerjee is counting dark windows on your block out loud. He reaches forty and asks when yours will glow. # id: enc.corner.02.line # speaker: narrator
* [Promise lights by next year. # id: enc.corner.02.c1 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Tell him to count slower. # id: enc.corner.02.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END
* [Count with him. # id: enc.corner.02.c3 # cash: personal -5]
    -> END

=== enc_corner_03 ===
The Brass Clock Depot clock froze at 6:02. A repair crew says a small gift gets it ticking again. # id: enc.corner.03.line # speaker: crew
* [Chip in for the fix. # id: enc.corner.03.c1 # cash: personal -200 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Leave it. It is right twice a day. # id: enc.corner.03.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_corner_11 ===
Celeste Halloway calls back weeks later. "You meant it about the air. Lunch on the thirtieth floor?" # id: enc.corner.11.line # speaker: owner
* [Go to lunch. # id: enc.corner.11.c1 # rel: top_broker +3 # broker: priority +2]
    -> END
* [Send your regrets. # id: enc.corner.11.c2 # rel: top_broker -2]
    -> END

=== enc_corner_04 ===
Rosa Medina runs a taco truck. "Let five of us park on your empty lot at noon? Small rent, big crowd." # id: enc.corner.04.line # speaker: owner
* [Say yes. Noon is theirs. # id: enc.corner.04.c1 # cash: company +40 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Say no. Keep the lot clean. # id: enc.corner.04.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_corner_05 ===
Dmitri Kowalski points up at a dark tower. "Cheap. The elevators are older than your parents." # id: enc.corner.05.line # speaker: broker
* [Ask him to send the papers. # id: enc.corner.05.c1 # broker: priority +1]
    -> END
* [Pass. Old elevators eat money. # id: enc.corner.05.c2 # rel: top_broker -1]
    -> END

=== enc_corner_06 ===
Abdul Fischer lowers his camera. "Your deck will block the best train photo in town. I have shot it for 30 years." # id: enc.corner.06.line # speaker: neighbor

// P3.21 street encounters for map creek. One screen each: one line, 2 or 3 replies, one press. Ids match Data/encounters/index.json.
// Knot = id with dots as underscores. Numbers are guesses for the owner to tune.

=== enc_creek_01 ===
Marisol Quint is picking trash out of the creek with a grabber. She hands you a spare. # id: enc.creek.01.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Help for ten minutes. # id: enc.creek.01.c1 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Thank her and drive on. # id: enc.creek.01.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_creek_02 ===
The trolley bell rings three times for you. Nobody knows why. The driver just nods. # id: enc.creek.02.line # speaker: narrator
* [Nod back. # id: enc.creek.02.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Ring your car horn three times. # id: enc.creek.02.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_creek_03 ===
Darnell Pike, a trail runner and part time broker, says a bike shop wants a corner by the trolley stop. # id: enc.creek.03.line # speaker: broker
* [Ask him to send it over. # id: enc.creek.03.c1 # broker: priority +2]
    -> END
* [Say you are full up. # id: enc.creek.03.c2 # broker: priority -1]
    -> END

=== enc_creek_04 ===
Beatriz Ochoa wants cafe tables on your sidewalk. The fire marshal is watching from across the street. # id: enc.creek.04.line # speaker: owner
* [Allow two tables and a clear path. # id: enc.creek.04.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Say no tables. # id: enc.creek.04.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_creek_05 ===
Isaac Reyes blocks your crew. "You need parking. We hate garages. Find a middle path or find a new street." # id: enc.creek.05.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Hide the garage behind shops. # id: enc.creek.05.c1 # cash: company -300 # neighbor: complaints -1]
    -> END
* [Build it plain and fast. # id: enc.creek.05.c2 # neighbor: complaints +2]
    -> END

=== enc_creek_06 ===
Lorraine Okafor offers a tiny lot on a handshake. "Break it and the whole street hears. Keep it and so do they." # id: enc.creek.06.line # speaker: mentor
* [Shake her hand. # id: enc.creek.06.c1 # rep: honor_handshake # rel: mentor +2]
    -> END
* [Ask for it in writing. # id: enc.creek.06.c2 # rel: mentor -1]
    -> END

=== enc_creek_07 ===
Nia Thibodeaux holds a crying baby at midnight. A rooftop bar plays the same song for the fourth time. # id: enc.creek.07.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Call the bar and ask for quiet. # id: enc.creek.07.c1 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Hum along. # id: enc.creek.07.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_creek_08 ===
Kenji Navarro shouts over the rain. "Caddo Creek is up a foot. Your low lot is next. Sandbags?" # id: enc.creek.08.line # speaker: crew
* [Pay for sandbags now. # id: enc.creek.08.c1 # cash: company -250 # city: goodwill +1]
    -> END
* [Wait and see. # id: enc.creek.08.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_creek_09 ===
Farah Moreau stares at your blank wall like it owes her money. "Free mural. A heron. A big one." # id: enc.creek.09.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Let her paint the heron. # id: enc.creek.09.c1 # city: goodwill +1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Sell the wall for an ad instead. # id: enc.creek.09.c2 # cash: company +60 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_creek_10 ===
Liam Cho and the shop next door both chain bikes to your one bike rack. Now they chain each other. # id: enc.creek.10.line # speaker: tenant
* [Buy a second rack. # id: enc.creek.10.c1 # cash: company -20 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Let them sort it out. # id: enc.creek.10.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

// P3.21 street encounters for map glade. One screen each: one line, 2 or 3 replies, one press. Ids match Data/encounters/index.json.
// Knot = id with dots as underscores. Numbers are guesses for the owner to tune.

=== enc_glade_01 ===
Ruben Cask owns a pad site on the frontage road. He wants out before the road work starts. # id: enc.glade.01.line # speaker: owner
* [Say you will look at it. # id: enc.glade.01.c1 # broker: priority +2]
    -> END
* [Pass. # id: enc.glade.01.c2 # rel: top_broker -1]
    -> END

=== enc_glade_02 ===
A truck driver lost on the frontage road asks the way to the highway ramp. # id: enc.glade.02.line # speaker: crew
* [Point the way. # id: enc.glade.02.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Lead him there. # id: enc.glade.02.c2 # cash: personal -10 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END

=== enc_glade_03 ===
A giant inflatable tube man at the car wash bows to you. Then again. Then again. # id: enc.glade.03.line # speaker: narrator
* [Bow back. # id: enc.glade.03.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Honk. # id: enc.glade.03.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_glade_04 ===
Quinn Barrera brings two car wash owners to your last pad. They will not look at each other. # id: enc.glade.04.line # speaker: broker
* [Pick the one who pays more. # id: enc.glade.04.c1 # cash: company +40 # rel: top_broker +1]
    -> END
* [Tell them to wash each other. # id: enc.glade.04.c2 # rel: top_broker -1]
    -> END

=== enc_glade_05 ===
Wanda Okonkwo owns the big empty store by the exit. "Gym, church or self storage. Help me choose." # id: enc.glade.05.line # speaker: owner
* [Say gym. People come every day. # id: enc.glade.05.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Say storage. It pays and stays quiet. # id: enc.glade.05.c2 # broker: priority +1]
    -> END

=== enc_glade_06 ===
Rashid Haddad from city hall squints up at the Exit 14 water tower. "Who will paint it? Your name could go on it." # id: enc.glade.06.line # speaker: council
* [Pay for the paint. # id: enc.glade.06.c1 # cash: company -150 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Leave it rusty. # id: enc.glade.06.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_glade_07 ===
Zeke Walker parks his truck on your empty lot every night. Tonight he left a thank you note on a fry box. # id: enc.glade.07.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Let him stay. # id: enc.glade.07.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Put up a no parking sign. # id: enc.glade.07.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_glade_08 ===
Hana Iyer shows you a photo of your drive thru line on the frontage road. "We need a turn lane. You pay." # id: enc.glade.08.line # speaker: planner
* [Pay for the lane. # id: enc.glade.08.c1 # cash: company -200 # city: goodwill +1]
    -> END
* [Push back at the hearing. # id: enc.glade.08.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_glade_09 ===
Bilal Tran tours every pad for the second time. He asks where the bathroom is. He does not make an offer. # id: enc.glade.09.line # speaker: buyer

// P3.21 street encounters for map green. One screen each: one line, 2 or 3 replies, one press. Ids match Data/encounters/index.json.
// Knot = id with dots as underscores. Numbers are guesses for the owner to tune.

=== enc_green_01 ===
Paige Whitlow from the homeowners board wants to know if your plan has a dog park. # id: enc.green.01.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Say yes, a big one. # id: enc.green.01.c1 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Say no promises. # id: enc.green.01.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_green_02 ===
Gil Ferraro farms the last open land next to the new homes. He will sell, but only to someone he trusts. # id: enc.green.02.line # speaker: owner
* [Shake his hand and visit next week. # id: enc.green.02.c1 # rep: fair_buyout]
    -> END
* [Offer cash today. # id: enc.green.02.c2 # rep: lowball_buyout]
    -> END

=== enc_green_03 ===
Every sprinkler on the street turns on as you drive by. You are now very clean. # id: enc.green.03.line # speaker: narrator
* [Laugh it off. # id: enc.green.03.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Report the timer. # id: enc.green.03.c2 # city: goodwill +1]
    -> END

=== enc_green_04 ===
Darius Obi from a home builder wants 200 lots now. "Cash this month. Price is fair. Mostly." # id: enc.green.04.line # speaker: buyer
* [Sell him the first 50. # id: enc.green.04.c1 # cash: company +200 # broker: priority +1]
    -> END
* [Wait for a better price. # id: enc.green.04.c2 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END

=== enc_green_05 ===
Esperanza Lam runs the Fence Line poll. "Pond or park? The families want to know what you think." # id: enc.green.05.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Say park. # id: enc.green.05.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Say pond. # id: enc.green.05.c2 # city: goodwill +1]
    -> END

=== enc_green_06 ===
Cole Jansen moves his cattle across your new road. "Every Tuesday since my grandpa. Cows do not read maps." # id: enc.green.06.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Put up a cow crossing sign. # id: enc.green.06.c1 # cash: company -10 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Ask him to try Wednesday. # id: enc.green.06.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_green_07 ===
Valeria Osei hands you a paint chip. "New rule. Fences only in this beige." An old rancher laughs behind her. # id: enc.green.07.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Back the beige. # id: enc.green.07.c1 # neighbor: complaints -1]
    -> END
* [Say paint is a free country. # id: enc.green.07.c2 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END

=== enc_green_08 ===
Doctor Naveen Castillo wants to open a clinic. "Families drive an hour now. I need cheap rent for a year." # id: enc.green.08.line # speaker: tenant
* [Give her a year of low rent. # id: enc.green.08.c1 # rel: ten +2 # city: goodwill +1]
    -> END
* [Offer normal rent. # id: enc.green.08.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_green_09 ===
June Albrecht taps the stop sign. "Still no new road. You said spring. It is not spring." # id: enc.green.09.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Say sorry and give a date. # id: enc.green.09.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Blame the county. # id: enc.green.09.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_green_10 ===
Kalani Ramos walks out of the model home with mud to the knees. "Nice house. Is the road a lake?" # id: enc.green.10.line # speaker: buyer
* [Lay gravel this week. # id: enc.green.10.c1 # cash: company -60 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Say it adds charm. # id: enc.green.10.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

// P3.21 street encounters for map lake. One screen each: one line, 2 or 3 replies, one press. Ids match Data/encounters/index.json.
// Knot = id with dots as underscores. Numbers are guesses for the owner to tune.

=== enc_lake_01 ===
Wendell Shore wants to know if your new homes will block his view of the marina. # id: enc.lake.01.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Promise to keep the view. # id: enc.lake.01.c1 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Say views are not a right. # id: enc.lake.01.c2 # neighbor: complaints +2]
    -> END

=== enc_lake_02 ===
Lucia Brandt owns the old bait shop by the marina. She is tired and wants a fair number. # id: enc.lake.02.line # speaker: owner
* [Make a fair offer. # id: enc.lake.02.c1 # rep: fair_buyout]
    -> END
* [Wait for her to drop the price. # id: enc.lake.02.c2 # rep: lowball_buyout]
    -> END

=== enc_lake_03 ===
A duck walks into the street and stops traffic. Nobody honks. The duck takes its time. # id: enc.lake.03.line # speaker: narrator
* [Wait for the duck. # id: enc.lake.03.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Take a photo for the office. # id: enc.lake.03.c2 # cash: personal -1]
    -> END

=== enc_lake_04 ===
A dock party gets loud. Maya Ledesma from the Homeowners League says she already called the Courier. # id: enc.lake.04.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Shut the party down. # id: enc.lake.04.c1 # neighbor: complaints -1]
    -> END
* [Invite her to the party. # id: enc.lake.04.c2 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END

=== enc_lake_05 ===
Gabriel Hoang has sold bait here for 40 years. "Your boardwalk plan has no room for me." # id: enc.lake.05.line # speaker: tenant
* [Keep a spot for him. # id: enc.lake.05.c1 # rel: ten +2 # city: goodwill +1]
    -> END
* [Offer to help him move. # id: enc.lake.05.c2 # cash: company -50 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_lake_06 ===
Grace Shah taps her rotten dock. "Fix this and my view rights are yours." # id: enc.lake.06.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Fix her dock. # id: enc.lake.06.c1 # cash: company -90 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Say the view is not worth it. # id: enc.lake.06.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_lake_07 ===
Omar Flores hauls his boat on a trailer. "Where do we park these in winter? Nobody has space." # id: enc.lake.07.line # speaker: buyer
* [Plan boat storage. # id: enc.lake.07.c1 # broker: priority +1]
    -> END
* [Say not your problem. # id: enc.lake.07.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_lake_08 ===
Lakshmi Nguyen and six other moms ask for a swim beach. It would cost you two lots. # id: enc.lake.08.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Give up the two lots. # id: enc.lake.08.c1 # city: goodwill +2 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Keep the lots. # id: enc.lake.08.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_lake_09 ===
Joaquin Zamora looks down your hillside lot. "Steep. Costs more to build. The view costs more too." # id: enc.lake.09.line # speaker: crew
* [Build it anyway. # id: enc.lake.09.c1 # broker: priority +1]
    -> END
* [Sell the slope to someone braver. # id: enc.lake.09.c2 # cash: company +50]
    -> END

=== enc_lake_10 ===
Ruth Valdez swears a catfish the size of a canoe lives under your dock. She has a blurry photo. # id: enc.lake.10.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Name the dock after the fish. # id: enc.lake.10.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Ask for a clearer photo. # id: enc.lake.10.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

@dialogue/encounters/mtn.ink:
// P3.21 street encounters for map mtn. One screen each: one line, 2 or 3 replies, one press. Ids match Data/encounters/index.json.
// Knot = id with dots as underscores. Numbers are guesses for the owner to tune.

=== enc_mtn_01 ===
Ingrid Holm rents ski cabins. She'll sell three of them to someone who keeps them open in winter. # id: enc.mtn.01.line # speaker: owner
* [Promise to keep them open. # id: enc.mtn.01.c1 # rep: honor_handshake]
    -> END
* [Say you want them for summer homes. # id: enc.mtn.01.c2 # rel: ten -2]
    -> END

=== enc_mtn_02 ===
A snowplow driver gives you a thumbs up for no reason. Your day is better. # id: enc.mtn.02.line # speaker: narrator
* [Thumbs up back. # id: enc.mtn.02.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Buy him a hot drink. # id: enc.mtn.02.c2 # cash: personal -6 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END

=== enc_mtn_03 ===
The chair lift stops with you on it. The crew asks if you want a free pass for your trouble. # id: enc.mtn.03.line # speaker: crew
* [Take the pass. # id: enc.mtn.03.c1 # cash: personal +40]
    -> END
* [Say it was the best view in town. # id: enc.mtn.03.c2 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END

=== enc_mtn_04 ===
Sun-hee Delgado teaches skiing and sleeps in her car. "We cannot afford to live here. We need worker housing." # id: enc.mtn.04.line # speaker: tenant
* [Add worker rooms to your plan. # id: enc.mtn.04.c1 # cash: company -150 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Say the market sets rent. # id: enc.mtn.04.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_mtn_05 ===
The pass is closed after a storm. Rafael Brennan says your lodge guests are stuck for two days. # id: enc.mtn.05.line # speaker: crew
* [Feed them free. # id: enc.mtn.05.c1 # cash: company -120 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Charge for meals. # id: enc.mtn.05.c2 # cash: company +60 # rel: ten -2]
    -> END

=== enc_mtn_06 ===
A bear opens your condo dumpster. Kai Lindqvist filmed it. It has 40,000 views. # id: enc.mtn.06.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Buy bear proof bins. # id: enc.mtn.06.c1 # cash: company -40 # neighbor: complaints -1]
    -> END
* [Post it again. # id: enc.mtn.06.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_mtn_07 ===
Xiomara Cruz wants your shop for her ski store. "Winter only. Summer is yours to figure out." # id: enc.mtn.07.line # speaker: tenant
* [Sign her for winter. # id: enc.mtn.07.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Ask for a full year. # id: enc.mtn.07.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_mtn_08 ===
Thanh Alvarado rolls up on a muddy bike. "Give us trails and your summer gets busy." # id: enc.mtn.08.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Mark a trail. # id: enc.mtn.08.c1 # cash: company -30 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Keep summer quiet. # id: enc.mtn.08.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_mtn_09 ===
Miguel Usman pats a snow machine. "Costs a lot. Saves a dry winter. Or sits there humming." # id: enc.mtn.09.line # speaker: contractor
* [Buy the machine. # id: enc.mtn.09.c1 # cash: company -300 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Hope for snow. # id: enc.mtn.09.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_mtn_10 ===
Leon Suarez is a famous singer's assistant. He needs one more room for New Year. Every room is full. # id: enc.mtn.10.line # speaker: buyer
* [Give up your own room. # id: enc.mtn.10.c1 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Say no room means no room. # id: enc.mtn.10.c2 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END

@dialogue/encounters/oldtown.ink:
// P3.21 street encounters for map oldtown. One screen each: one line, 2 or 3 replies, one press. Ids match Data/encounters/index.json.
// Knot = id with dots as underscores. Numbers are guesses for the owner to tune.

=== enc_oldtown_01 ===
Hattie Lark runs the square's oldest shop. "Keep the brick and I'll tell every friend I have." # id: enc.oldtown.01.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Promise to keep the brick. # id: enc.oldtown.01.c1 # rep: hearing_truth]
    -> END
* [Say brick costs too much. # id: enc.oldtown.01.c2 # rel: ten -2]
    -> END

=== enc_oldtown_02 ===
A brass band marches past your car, stops, and plays one long note right at you. # id: enc.oldtown.02.line # speaker: narrator
* [Clap. # id: enc.oldtown.02.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Tip the tuba. # id: enc.oldtown.02.c2 # cash: personal -20]
    -> END

=== enc_oldtown_03 ===
Council member Vern Ashby asks if you will sponsor the festival lemonade stand. # id: enc.oldtown.03.line # speaker: council
* [Sponsor it. # id: enc.oldtown.03.c1 # cash: personal -150 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Say maybe next year. # id: enc.oldtown.03.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_oldtown_04 ===
Rosa Delgado dusts flour off her lease. "It is up next month. Raise my rent and the square loses its bread." # id: enc.oldtown.04.line # speaker: tenant
* [Keep her rent the same. # id: enc.oldtown.04.c1 # rel: ten +2 # city: goodwill +1]
    -> END
* [Raise it a little. # id: enc.oldtown.04.c2 # cash: company +50 # rel: ten -2]
    -> END

=== enc_oldtown_05 ===
Earlene Pruitt wants to sell her land to you. Her cousin Walt yells from the porch, "Over my dead feed sack." # id: enc.oldtown.05.line # speaker: owner
* [Make a fair offer anyway. # id: enc.oldtown.05.c1 # rep: fair_buyout]
    -> END
* [Wait until the cousins agree. # id: enc.oldtown.05.c2 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END

=== enc_oldtown_06 ===
Tomas Ibarra scrapes old paint and finds a ghost sign. "Pecan Soda, five cents." It is from 1910. # id: enc.oldtown.06.line # speaker: crew
* [Save the sign. # id: enc.oldtown.06.c1 # cash: company -80 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Paint over it. # id: enc.oldtown.06.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_oldtown_07 ===
Delia Kaur from the county holds a bucket. "The courthouse roof leaks on the judge. Can you chip in?" # id: enc.oldtown.07.line # speaker: council
* [Chip in. # id: enc.oldtown.07.c1 # cash: personal -100 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Say the county has a budget. # id: enc.oldtown.07.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_oldtown_08 ===
Walt Pruitt holds up a ruler. "Your window trim is one inch too modern. One inch." # id: enc.oldtown.08.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Thank him for the inch. # id: enc.oldtown.08.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Measure his porch back. # id: enc.oldtown.08.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_oldtown_09 ===
Marisol Villanueva peeks in your empty corner shop. "A small market would fit here. I would open by spring." # id: enc.oldtown.09.line # speaker: tenant
* [Offer a first year deal. # id: enc.oldtown.09.c1 # cash: company -30 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Ask for full rent. # id: enc.oldtown.09.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_oldtown_10 ===
Mateo Abara digs up a time capsule from 1936. Inside: a comb, a nickel and a note that says "Hello future." # id: enc.oldtown.10.line # speaker: crew
* [Call the Courier for a photo. # id: enc.oldtown.10.c1 # city: goodwill +1]
    -> END
* [Write back and bury it again. # id: enc.oldtown.10.c2 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END

@dialogue/encounters/stadium.ink:
// P3.21 street encounters for map stadium. One screen each: one line, 2 or 3 replies, one press. Ids match Data/encounters/index.json.
// Knot = id with dots as underscores. Numbers are guesses for the owner to tune.

=== enc_stadium_01 ===
Game day. A mascot in a grackle suit high fives your side mirror. # id: enc.stadium.01.line # speaker: narrator
* [High five back. # id: enc.stadium.01.c1 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Buy a foam finger. # id: enc.stadium.01.c2 # cash: personal -15]
    -> END

=== enc_stadium_02 ===
Otis Rambeau runs a sports bar with a lease ending soon. He wants a bigger spot near the gates. # id: enc.stadium.02.line # speaker: owner
* [Offer him space in your next project. # id: enc.stadium.02.c1 # broker: priority +2]
    -> END
* [Say you only build offices. # id: enc.stadium.02.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_stadium_03 ===
A family can't find parking before the game. They ask if they can use your empty lot. # id: enc.stadium.03.line # speaker: neighbor
* [Let them park free. # id: enc.stadium.03.c1 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Charge them ten. # id: enc.stadium.03.c2 # cash: personal +10 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_stadium_04 ===
Mira Bell from the team wants a store in your building. "We pay less. But fans come every day." # id: enc.stadium.04.line # speaker: tenant
* [Take the team store. # id: enc.stadium.04.c1 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Hold out for full rent. # id: enc.stadium.04.c2 # cash: company +40 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_stadium_05 ===
A big concert fills the arena on a Tuesday. Pablo Tan waves cars into your lot with a glow stick he found. # id: enc.stadium.05.line # speaker: crew
* [Pay him for the night. # id: enc.stadium.05.c1 # cash: personal -20 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Close the gate. # id: enc.stadium.05.c2 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> END

=== enc_stadium_06 ===
Rocco Benedetti counts his till. "Twelve losses in a row. Game day sales are gone. Can you help?" # id: enc.stadium.06.line # speaker: tenant
* [Cut his rent for a month. # id: enc.stadium.06.c1 # cash: company -80 # rel: ten +2]
    -> END
* [Say the team will turn it around. # id: enc.stadium.06.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_stadium_07 ===
Samir Kim shows you an old warehouse by the park. "Lofts. Fans would live next to the stadium." # id: enc.stadium.07.line # speaker: owner
* [Ask for a tour. # id: enc.stadium.07.c1 # broker: priority +1]
    -> END
* [Pass. # id: enc.stadium.07.c2 # rel: top_broker -1]
    -> END

=== enc_stadium_08 ===
A flock of grackles moves onto your parking lot. Priya Whitfield shows you her car. It is not white anymore. # id: enc.stadium.08.line # speaker: crew
* [Pay for her car wash. # id: enc.stadium.08.c1 # cash: personal -15 # rel: ten +1]
    -> END
* [Call it good luck. # id: enc.stadium.08.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END

=== enc_stadium_09 ===
Big Earl Tibbs grabs you outside Grackle Talk 98. "Say something nice on air or I keep roasting you." # id: enc.stadium.09.line # speaker: reporter
* [Go on air. # id: enc.stadium.09.c1 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Walk past. # id: enc.stadium.09.c2 # city: goodwill -1]
    -> END

=== enc_stadium_10 ===
Gus the Grackle wants to cut your ribbon. He cannot hold scissors. He has wings. # id: enc.stadium.10.line # speaker: crew
* [Let him try. # id: enc.stadium.10.c1 # city: goodwill +2]
    -> END
* [Cut it yourself. # id: enc.stadium.10.c2 # rel: ten -1]
    -> END
