@dialogue/forced_decisions.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"
VAR contractor_name = "Hank Dobbs"
VAR neighbor_name = "Mrs. Alvarado"
VAR site_name = "the Creekside lot"

-> fd_water_main

// browser line 1911: water main broke. random a: 20000..60000 (middle 40000)
=== fd_water_main ===
Boss, we have a problem. The water main broke under the lot. # id: forced_decisions.water.01 # speaker: contractor
My plumber quotes forty thousand dollars to fix it today. # id: forced_decisions.water.02 # speaker: contractor
Emergencies cost more. A second bid helps if you have time. # id: forced_decisions.water.03 # speaker: contractor
* [Pay the quote. # id: forced_decisions.water.04 # cash: company -40000]
    Done. Water is running again by supper. # id: forced_decisions.water.05 # speaker: contractor
    -> END
* [Wait for a second bid. # id: forced_decisions.water.06 # cash: company -32000 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    Second bid saved you some money. The stores lost a day of sales. # id: forced_decisions.water.07 # speaker: contractor
    -> END
* [Try for a better deal. # id: forced_decisions.water.08 # skill_req: negotiation 2 # cash: company -24000 # skill_xp: close_deal]
    You talked the plumber down. The repair cost a lot less. # id: forced_decisions.water.09 # speaker: contractor
    -> END

// browser line 1920: film crew wants to shoot here. fixed 40000 (no negotiation branch in the browser)
=== fd_film_crew ===
Hi there. I run the crew for a movie shoot in town. # id: forced_decisions.film.01 # speaker: crew
We want two days of filming on your lot. We pay forty thousand dollars. # id: forced_decisions.film.02 # speaker: crew
We will block part of the parking, though. # id: forced_decisions.film.03 # speaker: crew
* [Let them film. # id: forced_decisions.film.04 # cash: company +40000 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    Cameras rolling! Fewer shoppers for a bit, but nice money. # id: forced_decisions.film.05 # speaker: crew
    -> END
* [Decline. # id: forced_decisions.film.06 # rel: ten +1]
    No worries. We will find another lot. # id: forced_decisions.film.07 # speaker: crew
    Your tenants are glad the lot stays open. # id: forced_decisions.film.08 # speaker: narrator
    -> END

// browser line 2129: neighbors complain about late-night noise. sound wall 45000
=== fd_noise_wall ===
Excuse me, {player_name}. I am {neighbor_name}, from the street behind your place. # id: forced_decisions.noise.01 # speaker: neighbor
The patio noise runs late every night. We cannot sleep. # id: forced_decisions.noise.02 # speaker: neighbor
We want a sound wall. It will cost forty five thousand dollars. # id: forced_decisions.noise.03 # speaker: neighbor
* [Build the wall. # id: forced_decisions.noise.04 # cash: company -45000 # neighbor: complaints -2]
    Thank you. Good neighbors make the next city approval easier. # id: forced_decisions.noise.05 # speaker: neighbor
    -> END
* [Ignore them. # id: forced_decisions.noise.06 # neighbor: complaints +2 # city: goodwill -3]
    Then we will talk to city hall. Bad reviews will pile up too. # id: forced_decisions.noise.07 # speaker: neighbor
    -> END
* [Offer quiet hours instead. # id: forced_decisions.noise.08 # skill_req: negotiation 2 # neighbor: complaints -1 # skill_xp: close_deal]
    Patios close at ten. No wall, no cost. We can live with that. # id: forced_decisions.noise.09 # speaker: neighbor
    -> END

// browser line 2407: sinkhole in parking lot. random a: 30000..60000 (middle 45000)
=== fd_sinkhole ===
A drain pipe failed and a sinkhole opened in your parking lot. # id: forced_decisions.sink.01 # speaker: inspector
I checked it this morning. The fix is quoted at forty five thousand dollars. # id: forced_decisions.sink.02 # speaker: inspector
Old pipes fail. A repair reserve is part of owning. # id: forced_decisions.sink.03 # speaker: inspector
* [Fix it now. # id: forced_decisions.sink.04 # cash: company -45000]
    Good call. The crew starts today. # id: forced_decisions.sink.05 # speaker: inspector
    -> END
* [Fence it off for now. # id: forced_decisions.sink.06 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    A fenced hole looks bad and costs you stalls. Fewer visitors. # id: forced_decisions.sink.07 # speaker: inspector
    -> END
* [Try for a better deal. # id: forced_decisions.sink.08 # skill_req: negotiation 2 # cash: company -24750 # skill_xp: close_deal]
    It was the city storm drain. The city shares the cost. # id: forced_decisions.sink.09 # speaker: inspector
    -> END

// browser line 2413: billboard on freeway frontage. fixed 70000, win 120000
=== fd_billboard ===
{player_name}, Jazmine Treviño says hello. I have a sign company on the line. # id: forced_decisions.bill.01 # speaker: broker
They want one billboard on your freeway frontage. # id: forced_decisions.bill.02 # speaker: broker
They pay seventy thousand dollars. Some folks think it is an eyesore. # id: forced_decisions.bill.03 # speaker: broker
* [Allow the sign. # id: forced_decisions.bill.04 # cash: company +70000 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    Billboard goes up. Some visitors will find it ugly. # id: forced_decisions.bill.05 # speaker: broker
    -> END
* [No billboard. # id: forced_decisions.bill.06 # rel: @broker +1]
    Fair enough. I will tell them no. # id: forced_decisions.bill.07 # speaker: broker
    -> END
* [Try for a better deal. # id: forced_decisions.bill.08 # skill_req: negotiation 2 # cash: company +120000 # skill_xp: close_deal]
    They agreed to pay more and to advertise your own shops on it. # id: forced_decisions.bill.09 # speaker: broker
    -> END

// browser line 3849: feeup24, council raises impact fees by 1 point
// browser speak-against odds are 25 percent plus goodwill over 250, capped 10 to 65 percent; shown here as a mild goodwill cost
=== fd_impact_fees ===
Mayor Vu here. The council wants to raise impact fees. # id: forced_decisions.fees.01 # speaker: mayor
New buildings would pay one more point of their cost to the city. # id: forced_decisions.fees.02 # speaker: mayor
Growth is straining our roads and schools. # id: forced_decisions.fees.03 # speaker: mayor
* [Accept it. # id: forced_decisions.fees.04 # city: fee_pct +1 # city: goodwill +2]
    Thank you. The council will remember you helped. # id: forced_decisions.fees.05 # speaker: mayor
    -> END
* [Speak against it. # id: forced_decisions.fees.06 # city: goodwill -1]
    You make your case in the meeting. It could go either way. # id: forced_decisions.fees.07 # speaker: mayor
    -> END
* [Meet in the middle. # id: forced_decisions.fees.08 # skill_req: negotiation 2 # city: goodwill +1 # skill_xp: win_hearing]
    Fees rise by half a point. Fair enough. # id: forced_decisions.fees.09 # speaker: mayor
    -> END

@dialogue/handshake_test.ink:
// Handshake deal tested by a better offer. The player is SELLING here (a pad site), which is how the
// reputation tags read: "Honored a handshake deal when a better offer came" (reputation.json).
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"
VAR buyer_name = "Earlene Pruitt"
VAR site_name = "the pad site on Creekside Road"

-> handshake_test

=== handshake_test ===
Last week you shook hands with {buyer_name}. She is buying {site_name} from you. # id: handshake_test.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Nothing is signed yet. Then your phone buzzes. # id: handshake_test.open.02 # speaker: narrator
{player_name}, I have a buyer who will pay a lot more for that pad. Today. # id: handshake_test.open.03 # speaker: top_broker
Your call. I just need an answer by tonight. # id: handshake_test.open.04 # speaker: top_broker
* [Keep your word. {buyer_name} gets it at the price you shook on. # id: handshake_test.choice.01 # rep: honor_handshake # mem: @buyer honored_deal # deal: close]
    You call {buyer_name} and tell her the deal stands. # id: handshake_test.honor.01 # speaker: narrator
    Folks do not do that much anymore. I will not forget it. # id: handshake_test.honor.02 # speaker: buyer
    -> END
* [Take the better offer and call off the handshake. # id: handshake_test.choice.02 # rep: take_better_offer # mem: @buyer broke_deal # deal: price_pct +8 # deal: close]
    You call {buyer_name} and say the deal is off. # id: handshake_test.break.01 # speaker: narrator
    I thought a handshake meant something. Do not call me again. # id: handshake_test.break.02 # speaker: buyer
    The extra money is nice. Word gets around town, though. # id: handshake_test.break.03 # speaker: narrator
    -> END
* [Tell {buyer_name} about the offer and ask her to come up a little. # id: handshake_test.choice.03 # rel: @buyer -2 # deal: price_pct +3 # deal: close]
    Well, that is honest of you, at least. I can come up a bit. Not all the way. # id: handshake_test.middle.01 # speaker: buyer
    You settle on a price in between and sign it that afternoon. # id: handshake_test.middle.02 # speaker: narrator
    -> END
* [Tell the broker no, and ask her to keep that buyer in mind for your next site. # id: handshake_test.choice.04 # rep: honor_handshake # broker: priority +1 # deal: close]
    Fair enough. I will send that buyer your way next time. # id: handshake_test.later.01 # speaker: top_broker
    -> END

@dialogue/hearing.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> hearing

=== hearing ===
The hearing room is cold and quiet. The city lawyer opens a thick folder. # id: hearing.open.01 # speaker: narrator
{company_name} is here because of what folks have seen these last months. # id: hearing.open.02 # speaker: council
The inspector lists every complaint, one by one. # id: hearing.open.03 # speaker: narrator
Your permits stay frozen until this is done. How do you want to answer? # id: hearing.open.04 # speaker: council
* [Fight it. Bring your lawyer and say you did nothing wrong. # id: hearing.fight.01 # rel: mayor -2]
    Your lawyer stands. This could take a while, and it could go either way. # id: hearing.fight.02 # speaker: narrator
    -> END
* [Settle. Pay the fine and promise to do better. # id: hearing.settle.01 # rel: mayor +1]
    The lawyer writes down a number. Folks will hear that you paid. # id: hearing.settle.02 # speaker: narrator
    -> END
* [Take a deal. Tell them who else was in on it. # id: hearing.deal.01 # rel: rival -5 # mem: rival burned]
    The room goes still. The case gets smaller, but people will remember. # id: hearing.deal.02 # speaker: narrator
    -> END

@dialogue/intros.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> intro_mentor

=== intro_mentor ===
Name is Lorraine Okafor. I built half of Creekside on handshakes. # id: intros.mentor.01 # speaker: mentor
Retired now, but I still read every plan in town. # id: intros.mentor.02 # speaker: mentor
First thing I ask about any deal: what does it do for the neighbors? # id: intros.mentor.03 # speaker: mentor
* [Say the neighbors always come first. # id: intros.mentor.pick.01 # rel: mentor +6 # mem: mentor met]
    Good answer. Come by the ranch and I will tell you the rest. # id: intros.mentor.reply.01 # speaker: mentor
    -> END
* [Say you want to learn the business first. # id: intros.mentor.pick.02 # rel: mentor +3 # mem: mentor met]
    Honest, at least. We start with listening. # id: intros.mentor.reply.02 # speaker: mentor
    -> END
* [Say profit is what matters most. # id: intros.mentor.pick.03 # rel: mentor -4 # mem: mentor met]
    Hm. Profit is fine. But folks remember how you earned it. # id: intros.mentor.reply.03 # speaker: mentor
    -> END

=== intro_rival ===
Brock Delacroix, Delacroix Ventures. You have probably seen my truck. # id: intros.rival.01 # speaker: rival
I bid on every lot you look at, and I grin when I win. # id: intros.rival.02 # speaker: rival
Nothing personal, {player_name}. Just business. # id: intros.rival.03 # speaker: rival
* [Shake his hand and smile back. # id: intros.rival.pick.01 # rel: rival +4 # mem: rival met]
    Ha! A friendly one. That will not last long. # id: intros.rival.reply.01 # speaker: rival
    -> END
* [Tell him to keep his eyes on the road. # id: intros.rival.pick.02 # rel: rival -3 # mem: rival met]
    Big talk. Let us see you back it up. # id: intros.rival.reply.02 # speaker: rival
    -> END
* [Ask what he does when he loses. # id: intros.rival.pick.03 # rel: rival +1 # mem: rival met]
    Loses? I will tell you when it happens. # id: intros.rival.reply.03 # speaker: rival
    -> END

=== intro_mayor ===
I am Mayor Rosalind Vu. I count the traffic complaints at every meeting. # id: intros.mayor.01 # speaker: mayor
And I love a ribbon cutting with a new park in it. # id: intros.mayor.02 # speaker: mayor
Build something this town is proud of, and my door stays open. # id: intros.mayor.03 # speaker: mayor
* [Promise a park in your plans. # id: intros.mayor.pick.01 # rel: mayor +6 # mem: mayor met]
    Now that is what I like to hear. # id: intros.mayor.reply.01 # speaker: mayor
    -> END
* [Say you will keep traffic low. # id: intros.mayor.pick.02 # rel: mayor +4 # mem: mayor met]
    Good. Put that in writing at the hearing. # id: intros.mayor.reply.02 # speaker: mayor
    -> END
* [Say you just need the permits fast. # id: intros.mayor.pick.03 # rel: mayor -3 # mem: mayor met]
    Fast is not how we do it here. Plan on a few meetings. # id: intros.mayor.reply.03 # speaker: mayor
    -> END

=== intro_banker ===
Gil Haverty, Prairie Lantern Savings. Pleased to meet you. # id: intros.banker.01 # speaker: banker
I trust a good track record more than a good pitch. # id: intros.banker.02 # speaker: banker
Pay on time and finish what you start, and we will get along fine. # id: intros.banker.03 # speaker: banker
* [Promise to pay on time, always. # id: intros.banker.pick.01 # rel: banker +5 # mem: banker met]
    That is the kind of promise I like to see kept. # id: intros.banker.reply.01 # speaker: banker
    -> END
* [Say you have big plans and need big money. # id: intros.banker.pick.02 # rel: banker -3 # mem: banker met]
    Big plans are fine. Let us see small ones finished first. # id: intros.banker.reply.02 # speaker: banker
    -> END
* [Ask what he looks for in a builder. # id: intros.banker.pick.03 # rel: banker +3 # mem: banker met]
    Honesty, mostly. The numbers come after. # id: intros.banker.reply.03 # speaker: banker
    -> END

=== intro_top_broker ===
Jazmine Treviño, Treviño Commercial. I know every off-market deal in three counties. # id: intros.broker.01 # speaker: top_broker
I call the people I like first. So be likable, {player_name}. # id: intros.broker.02 # speaker: top_broker
Now, are you buying or just looking? # id: intros.broker.03 # speaker: top_broker
* [Say you are buying, and soon. # id: intros.broker.pick.01 # rel: top_broker +5 # mem: top_broker met # broker: priority +1]
    Music to my ears. Keep your phone on. # id: intros.broker.reply.01 # speaker: top_broker
    -> END
* [Say you are just looking around. # id: intros.broker.pick.02 # rel: top_broker +1 # mem: top_broker met]
    Looking is free. Buying is better. We will talk. # id: intros.broker.reply.02 # speaker: top_broker
    -> END
* [Ask her to call you before anyone else. # id: intros.broker.pick.03 # rel: top_broker -3 # mem: top_broker met]
    Slow down, hotshot. First calls get earned. # id: intros.broker.reply.03 # speaker: top_broker
    -> END

@dialogue/neighbor_buyout.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"
VAR neighbor_name = "Walt Pruitt"
VAR site_name = "Bluebonnet Plaza"

-> neighbor_buyout

=== neighbor_buyout ===
{neighbor_name} waves from a porch swing. The lot next door is his. # id: neighbor_buyout.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Come on up, {player_name}. I hear you want my lot for {site_name}. # id: neighbor_buyout.open.02 # speaker: neighbor
That dirt has been in my family a long time. # id: neighbor_buyout.open.03 # speaker: neighbor
* [Make a fair offer, right up front. # id: neighbor_buyout.open.04 # mem: @neighbor met # deal: price_pct +8]
    He studies you a long moment. # id: neighbor_buyout.open.05 # speaker: narrator
    -> fair
* [Open low and say that is all it is worth. # id: neighbor_buyout.open.06 # mem: @neighbor met # deal: price_pct -15]
    His smile fades. # id: neighbor_buyout.open.07 # speaker: narrator
    -> lowball
* [Ask what he would want, then think about it. # id: neighbor_buyout.open.08 # mem: @neighbor met # neighbor: parcel offered]
    Nobody ever asks me that. Come back when you have a number. # id: neighbor_buyout.open.09 # speaker: neighbor
    -> END

= fair
That is more than I figured. What about my pecan tree? # id: neighbor_buyout.fair.01 # speaker: neighbor
* [Promise to keep the tree and close the deal. # id: neighbor_buyout.fair.02 # rep: fair_buyout # mem: @neighbor fair_price # neighbor: parcel sold # deal: close]
    Then we have a deal. Come back with a pie when the place opens. # id: neighbor_buyout.fair.03 # speaker: neighbor
    -> END
* [Shake on it right now. # id: neighbor_buyout.fair.04 # rep: fair_buyout # mem: @neighbor fair_price # neighbor: parcel sold # deal: handshake]
    A handshake is good enough for me. # id: neighbor_buyout.fair.05 # speaker: neighbor
    -> END

= lowball
That is an insult. My cousin got twice that down the road. # id: neighbor_buyout.lowball.01 # speaker: neighbor
* [Say it is the best you will do, and hint the city may not like his junk pile. # id: neighbor_buyout.lowball.02 # rep: lowball_buyout # mem: @neighbor lowballed # neighbor: parcel refused # neighbor: complaints +1]
    You get off my porch. I will see you at city hall. # id: neighbor_buyout.lowball.03 # speaker: neighbor
    -> END
* [Back off and say sorry for the rough start. # id: neighbor_buyout.lowball.04 # mem: @neighbor met # neighbor: parcel offered # deal: price_pct +5]
    Hmph. Maybe. Bring a better number. # id: neighbor_buyout.lowball.05 # speaker: neighbor
    -> END

@dialogue/rival_bid.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"
VAR site_name = "the Creekside lot"

-> rival_bid

=== rival_bid ===
Well, howdy, {player_name}. Heard you like {site_name}. # id: rival_bid.open.01 # speaker: rival
Funny. So do I. I just put in a bid on it. # id: rival_bid.open.02 # speaker: rival
Bring your checkbook, {company_name}. You will need it. # id: rival_bid.open.03 # speaker: rival
* [Raise your bid five percent. # id: rival_bid.bid.01 # rival: bid_pct +5 # cash: company -10000]
    Five percent? Cute. That just got me excited. # id: rival_bid.raise.01 # speaker: rival
    You paid a little extra to stay in the race. # id: rival_bid.raise.02 # speaker: narrator
    -> END
* [Offer to split the lot with him. # id: rival_bid.bid.02 # rival: site shared # rel: rival +5]
    Split it? Huh. I did not see that coming. # id: rival_bid.split.01 # speaker: rival
    Fine. Half a lot beats a fight. Send me the map. # id: rival_bid.split.02 # speaker: rival
    -> END
* [Tell him the owner likes you better. # id: rival_bid.bid.03 # skill_req: negotiation 3 # deal: price_pct -4 # rival: site won]
    You called the owner first, did you? Smart. # id: rival_bid.trick.01 # speaker: rival
    The owner dropped the price a little for a buyer who keeps promises. # id: rival_bid.trick.02 # speaker: narrator
    Enjoy it, {player_name}. I will get the next one. # id: rival_bid.trick.03 # speaker: rival
    -> END
* [Let him have it and look elsewhere. # id: rival_bid.bid.04 # rival: site lost # rel: rival -5]
    Ha! Thanks for the lot. Easiest win this year. # id: rival_bid.lose.01 # speaker: rival
    There are other sites in town. You tip your hat and walk. # id: rival_bid.lose.02 # speaker: narrator
    -> END

@dialogue/story/ch1_booth.ink:
// Story ch1, scene 1 (writer A). Plays when mission m1_meet_mentor is done, right after cs_meet_mentor.
// All three Pearl replies end in the same handshake (pie now, the tab when Gil says bankable). ch4_tab depends on it.
// Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 6, ch1. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch1_booth

=== ch1_booth ===
The back booth of the Honeycomb Diner. Your whole plan fits on one napkin. # id: ch1_booth.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Lorraine Okafor turns the napkin around. Then she turns it back. # id: ch1_booth.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Two shops, a driveway and a lake. # id: ch1_booth.open.03 # speaker: mentor
The lake is syrup. # id: ch1_booth.open.04 # speaker: narrator
I ask one thing about every deal, {player_name}. # id: ch1_booth.open.05 # speaker: mentor
What does it do for the neighbors? # id: ch1_booth.open.06 # speaker: mentor
* [They get fresh bread and a place to park. # id: ch1_booth.pick.01 # rel: mentor +4]
    Bread and parking. I have paid for worse ideas. # id: ch1_booth.answer.01 # speaker: mentor
    Most of them were mine. # id: ch1_booth.answer.02 # speaker: mentor
* [They get to watch me get rich. # id: ch1_booth.pick.02 # rel: mentor -3 # rel: rival +2]
    There's a fellow in a tall truck who says that. # id: ch1_booth.answer.03 # speaker: mentor
    He says it louder. It's still not an answer. # id: ch1_booth.answer.04 # speaker: mentor
* [I do not know yet. Ask me when it is built. # id: ch1_booth.pick.03 # rel: mentor +2 # rel: office_manager +2]
    Honest. And free. I like both. # id: ch1_booth.answer.05 # speaker: mentor
    In the next booth, somebody says, "Hm." It sounds like a good grade. # id: ch1_booth.answer.06 # speaker: narrator
- A red pen lands on your paperwork. It did not come from Lorraine. # id: ch1_booth.pearl.01 # speaker: narrator
You spelled Corridor wrong. Twice. Scoot over. # id: ch1_booth.pearl.02 # speaker: office_manager
Pearl Tackett. 74. Retired Larkin County clerk. She scoots in beside you. # id: ch1_booth.pearl.03 # speaker: narrator
Wrong form. Wrong box. Here you signed where the city signs. # id: ch1_booth.pearl.04 # speaker: office_manager
And this one is a kids' menu, hon. You did finish the maze. # id: ch1_booth.pearl.05 # speaker: office_manager
She fixes all of it before your coffee gets cold. # id: ch1_booth.pearl.06 # speaker: narrator
You need an office manager. I need a reason to leave the house. # id: ch1_booth.pearl.07 # speaker: office_manager
My price is pie now. The rest goes on a tab. # id: ch1_booth.pearl.08 # speaker: office_manager
You pay the tab the day Gil Haverty calls you bankable. # id: ch1_booth.pearl.09 # speaker: office_manager
Take it. I have seen your spelling. # id: ch1_booth.pearl.10 # speaker: mentor
* [Shake on it. # id: ch1_booth.pick.04 # deal: handshake # rel: office_manager +6]
    Good grip. Pie is at three. Don't be late to your own office. # id: ch1_booth.deal.01 # speaker: office_manager
* [Shake, and give her a title: Head of Head Office. # id: ch1_booth.pick.05 # deal: handshake # rel: office_manager +8 # cash: personal -15]
    Head of Head Office. I'll need cards. # id: ch1_booth.deal.02 # speaker: office_manager
    You buy her first slice to seal it. Pecan. # id: ch1_booth.deal.03 # speaker: narrator
    Pie, received. Credited. The rest is on the tab. # id: ch1_booth.deal.04 # speaker: office_manager
* [Say you work alone. # id: ch1_booth.pick.06 # deal: handshake # rel: office_manager -3]
    That was not a question, hon. # id: ch1_booth.deal.05 # speaker: office_manager
    She shakes your hand anyway. You notice you are letting her. # id: ch1_booth.deal.06 # speaker: narrator
- The diner phone rings. Pearl gets there before the waitress. # id: ch1_booth.phone.01 # speaker: narrator
{company_name}, head office. Please hold. # id: ch1_booth.phone.02 # speaker: office_manager
She presses the phone to her sweater. # id: ch1_booth.phone.03 # speaker: narrator
It's a man about a dumpster. Sit up straight, hon. # id: ch1_booth.phone.04 # speaker: office_manager
Lorraine stands and tips her hat. Still no handshake. # id: ch1_booth.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
A napkin, a clerk and a phone. Folks have started with less. # id: ch1_booth.hook.02 # speaker: mentor
Go lay it out. And mind the kid on your lot. # id: ch1_booth.hook.03 # speaker: mentor
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch1_shovel.ink:
// Story ch1, chapter close (writer A). Plays when mission m1_start is done, just before cs_groundbreaking.
// Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 6, ch1. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch1_shovel

=== ch1_shovel ===
Shovel day. The crowd is four people and one camera. # id: ch1_shovel.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Pearl hands you the gold shovel. It is her snow shovel, spray painted. # id: ch1_shovel.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Nobody knows why a Texan owns a snow shovel. Pearl is not saying. # id: ch1_shovel.open.03 # speaker: narrator
Hold it low, hon. The gold is still wet. # id: ch1_shovel.open.04 # speaker: office_manager
One of the four sits in a lawn chair by the fence. # id: ch1_shovel.open.05 # speaker: narrator
Amos Tulley. Retired. I watch holes. # id: ch1_shovel.open.06 # speaker: fence_regular
There is no hole yet. He likes a good seat. # id: ch1_shovel.open.07 # speaker: narrator
It is August. The dirt is baked hard as a brick. # id: ch1_shovel.open.08 # speaker: narrator
You swing. The shovel bounces. # id: ch1_shovel.open.09 # speaker: narrator
You swing harder. The shovel bends. # id: ch1_shovel.open.10 # speaker: narrator
Channel 6 Glade News: the groundbreaking of the year. # id: ch1_shovel.open.11 # speaker: narrator
You hold your sandwich up for the camera. Nobody asked you to. # id: ch1_shovel.open.12 # speaker: narrator
A big shiny grackle drops off the water tower. # id: ch1_shovel.open.13 # speaker: narrator
That's Gerald. He's robbed this lot since the hat store. # id: ch1_shovel.open.14 # speaker: fence_regular
Gerald takes the sandwich. # id: ch1_shovel.open.15 # speaker: narrator
Gerald does not give it back. # id: ch1_shovel.open.16 # speaker: narrator
Channel 6 Glade News calls him Gus. He is not Gus. # id: ch1_shovel.open.17 # speaker: narrator
A microphone lands under your chin. You are live. # id: ch1_shovel.open.18 # speaker: narrator
* ["The neighbors are going to love it." # id: ch1_shovel.pick.01 # rel: mentor +2 # rel: ten +2]
    Somewhere in Creekside, a hat tips. # id: ch1_shovel.mic.01 # speaker: narrator
    Good. Short. Nobody can misquote short. # id: ch1_shovel.mic.02 # speaker: office_manager
* ["Brock Delacroix should watch his back." # id: ch1_shovel.pick.02 # rel: rival -3]
    Out on the freeway, a very tall truck honks. Twice. # id: ch1_shovel.mic.03 # speaker: narrator
    He heard that, hon. He hears anything with his name in it. # id: ch1_shovel.mic.04 # speaker: office_manager
* ["The shovel was defective." # id: ch1_shovel.pick.03 # rel: office_manager -2 # rel: fence_regular +3]
    That shovel is older than you, hon. And it showed up on time. # id: ch1_shovel.mic.05 # speaker: office_manager
    Blaming the tool. A classic. I respect it. # id: ch1_shovel.mic.06 # speaker: fence_regular
- Amos writes on a card and holds it up. # id: ch1_shovel.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Four. Nice hole. Crooked. # id: ch1_shovel.hook.02 # speaker: fence_regular
Your phone buzzes. It is Jazmine Treviño. # id: ch1_shovel.hook.03 # speaker: narrator
Bad news. Nobody will lease on the Triple Flop. # id: ch1_shovel.hook.04 # speaker: top_broker
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch1_stand.ink:
// Story ch1, scene 2, the big choice (writer A). Plays when mission m1_place is done.
// Writes the Pip memory: kid_partner helped, fair_price or lowballed (door memory: kid_partner lowballed).
// Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 6, ch1. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch1_stand

=== ch1_stand ===
Your tablet shows two shops and one driveway. # id: ch1_stand.open.01 # speaker: narrator
The driveway runs right over a lemonade stand. # id: ch1_stand.open.02 # speaker: narrator
The stand has a kid in it. He has a cash box and a clipboard. # id: ch1_stand.open.03 # speaker: narrator
Pip Delgado. 12. Lemonade and day old pastries, all summer. # id: ch1_stand.open.04 # speaker: kid_partner
I was here first. That makes me your first tenant. I want it in writing. # id: ch1_stand.open.05 # speaker: kid_partner
He holds out the clipboard. It is a lease. It is in marker. It has a late fee. # id: ch1_stand.open.06 # speaker: narrator
You know this lot is cursed, right? Folks call it the Triple Flop. # id: ch1_stand.open.07 # speaker: kid_partner
First a tanning place. In Texas. The sun is free here. # id: ch1_stand.open.08 # speaker: kid_partner
Then phone repair. Then a store that only sold hats. # id: ch1_stand.open.09 # speaker: kid_partner
He looks you over, boots to hair. # id: ch1_stand.open.10 # speaker: narrator
You do not have a hat. # id: ch1_stand.open.11 # speaker: kid_partner
This stand pays my mom's flour bill. So what's your offer? # id: ch1_stand.open.12 # speaker: kid_partner
The lot took nearly all your cash. # id: ch1_stand.open.13 # speaker: narrator
Moving the driveway costs real money and a late start. # id: ch1_stand.open.14 # speaker: narrator
Moving the kid costs a twenty. # id: ch1_stand.open.15 # speaker: narrator
* [Redraw the driveway around the stand. Make him Site Lemonade Officer. # id: ch1_stand.pick.01 # rep: fair_buyout # mem: kid_partner helped # cash: company -15000 # build: speed_pct -10 # rel: baker +8]
    Site Lemonade Officer. Does it come with a vest? # id: ch1_stand.spare.01 # speaker: kid_partner
    It does now. You hand over your own. It hangs to his knees. # id: ch1_stand.spare.02 # speaker: narrator
    Deal. First cup is free. After that you pay like everybody. # id: ch1_stand.spare.03 # speaker: kid_partner
    The new driveway eats cash you do not have. Shovel day slips. # id: ch1_stand.spare.04 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: new developer redraws plans around a lemonade stand. # id: ch1_stand.news.01 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: boy, 12, stops bulldozer with clipboard. Story at six. # id: ch1_stand.news.02 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: the new place has lemonade. Where do I park. # id: ch1_stand.news.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Buy him a cart with wheels so he can sell from the sidewalk. # id: ch1_stand.pick.02 # mem: kid_partner fair_price # cash: company -4000 # rel: baker +3]
    Pip walks a full circle around the idea. # id: ch1_stand.cart.01 # speaker: narrator
    Wheels. I'd own something with wheels. # id: ch1_stand.cart.02 # speaker: kid_partner
    The sidewalk is city land. So you're not my landlord. You're my neighbor. # id: ch1_stand.cart.03 # speaker: kid_partner
    Neighbors pay full price too. # id: ch1_stand.cart.04 # speaker: kid_partner
    The cart is not free. It costs a lot less than a new driveway. # id: ch1_stand.cart.05 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: lemonade stand moves to the sidewalk, on new wheels. # id: ch1_stand.news.04 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: lemonade stand now mobile. Is any corner safe. # id: ch1_stand.news.05 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: a lemonade cart took my spot. Where do I park. # id: ch1_stand.news.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Hand him a twenty for the plywood. The stand goes by Friday. # id: ch1_stand.pick.03 # rep: lowball_buyout # mem: kid_partner lowballed # build: speed_pct +5 # rel: baker -8]
    Pip holds the twenty up to the sun. He checks both sides. # id: ch1_stand.ruin.01 # speaker: narrator
    It's real. It's also twenty. # id: ch1_stand.ruin.02 # speaker: kid_partner
    I'll remember this. Not in a mean way. In a pricing way. # id: ch1_stand.ruin.03 # speaker: kid_partner
    He folds the stand flat by himself. It takes four minutes. # id: ch1_stand.ruin.04 # speaker: narrator
    You start on time, with your cash still in your pocket. # id: ch1_stand.ruin.05 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: new developer's first move, closes a lemonade stand. # id: ch1_stand.news.07 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: lemonade stand flattened. Town in shock. Weather next. # id: ch1_stand.news.08 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: who ran off the lemonade kid. Also, where do I park. # id: ch1_stand.news.09 # speaker: narrator
- The layout is locked in. The dirt is waiting. # id: ch1_stand.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Now press Start building. # id: ch1_stand.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch2_corner.ink:
// Story ch2, scene 2, the big choice (writer A). Plays when mission m2_open is done, right after cs_grand_opening.
// Writes the Rosa memory: baker honored_deal (kept) or baker broke_deal (door memory for ch7 and the beam).
// Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 6, ch2. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch2_corner

=== ch2_corner ===
Cedar Glade Courier: new center opens. Ribbon still missing. # id: ch2_corner.open.01 # speaker: narrator
The morning after ribbon day. Rosa's window is steamed up by six. # id: ch2_corner.open.02 # speaker: narrator
A woman walks your sidewalk with a tape measure. She measures the curb. Twice. # id: ch2_corner.open.03 # speaker: narrator
Marisol Villanueva. Villanueva Markets. Don't mind me. I'm counting. # id: ch2_corner.open.04 # speaker: grocer
I may want a small market spot one day. First I watch the landlord. # id: ch2_corner.open.05 # speaker: grocer
Then your phone rings. Cluckwell Chicken. # id: ch2_corner.open.06 # speaker: narrator
They want the corner. Rosa's corner. They'll pay much more for it. # id: ch2_corner.open.07 # speaker: narrator
One signature and you are 90% leased this week. # id: ch2_corner.open.08 # speaker: narrator
Their man ends the call with a cluck. It is company policy. # id: ch2_corner.open.09 # speaker: narrator
Rosa has heard. Bakers hear everything by six. # id: ch2_corner.open.10 # speaker: narrator
I already bought the ovens. # id: ch2_corner.open.11 # speaker: baker
You promised. I heard you. # id: ch2_corner.open.12 # speaker: kid_partner
He is holding the clipboard. He wrote it down. With the date. # id: ch2_corner.open.13 # speaker: narrator
* [Keep the handshake. Rosa keeps the corner. # id: ch2_corner.pick.01 # rep: honor_handshake # mem: baker honored_deal # lease: rent_pct -8 # rel: grocer +6 # rel: bank -2]
    You call Cluckwell back and say no. Their man clucks, sadly. # id: ch2_corner.spare.01 # speaker: narrator
    The far bays stay dark a while longer. That is the price. # id: ch2_corner.spare.02 # speaker: narrator
    I know what that call was worth. Thank you. # id: ch2_corner.spare.03 # speaker: baker
    I had a speech ready. It was a really good speech. # id: ch2_corner.spare.04 # speaker: kid_partner
    I lost nothing today. I learned whether your word is good. Cheap lesson. # id: ch2_corner.spare.05 # speaker: grocer
    Cedar Glade Courier: developer turns down chicken chain, keeps bakery on the corner. # id: ch2_corner.news.01 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: chicken snubbed. Bread wins. A town holds its breath. # id: ch2_corner.news.02 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: so no drive through chicken. Fine. Where do I park for bread. # id: ch2_corner.news.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Sell Cluckwell on the far end with its own drive lane. Both stay. # id: ch2_corner.pick.02 # skill_req: negotiation 2 # rep: honor_handshake # mem: baker honored_deal # cash: company -30000 # lease: sign]
    You call Cluckwell back and sell them the far end. With its own drive lane. # id: ch2_corner.both.01 # speaker: narrator
    The drive lane is on your dime. Their man clucks. Then he signs. # id: ch2_corner.both.02 # speaker: narrator
    My corner and a full center. Who taught you that? # id: ch2_corner.both.03 # speaker: baker
    I did. It's on page two. # id: ch2_corner.both.04 # speaker: kid_partner
    I lost nothing today. I learned whether your word is good. Cheap lesson. # id: ch2_corner.both.05 # speaker: grocer
    Cedar Glade Courier: bakery keeps the corner, chicken chain signs for the far end. # id: ch2_corner.news.04 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: bread and chicken, side by side. Can it last. # id: ch2_corner.news.05 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: the chicken line is in my way. Where do I park. # id: ch2_corner.news.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Move Rosa to the back bay. Sign Cluckwell for the corner. # id: ch2_corner.pick.03 # rep: take_better_offer # mem: baker broke_deal # lease: rent_pct +15 # lease: sign # rel: grocer -6 # rel: kid_partner -10]
    You sign Cluckwell for the corner. 90% leased, just like that. # id: ch2_corner.ruin.01 # speaker: narrator
    You promised me the corner. I heard you. Pip heard you. # id: ch2_corner.ruin.02 # speaker: baker
    The back bay has no window. # id: ch2_corner.ruin.03 # speaker: baker
    Pip tears a page off his clipboard and hands it to you. # id: ch2_corner.ruin.04 # speaker: narrator
    That's your promise. Keep it. I have a copy. # id: ch2_corner.ruin.05 # speaker: kid_partner
    Marisol rolls up her tape measure. She says nothing. She leaves. # id: ch2_corner.ruin.06 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: bakery moved to back bay as chicken chain takes the corner. # id: ch2_corner.news.07 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: chicken beats bread in corner showdown. Feathers fly. # id: ch2_corner.news.08 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: I can smell bread but I cannot find it. Where do I park. # id: ch2_corner.news.09 # speaker: narrator
- Your phone rings again. Gil Haverty, Prairie Lantern Savings. # id: ch2_corner.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Fill the rest. Then come see me. # id: ch2_corner.hook.02 # speaker: banker
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch2_flags.ink:
// Story ch2, chapter close (writer A). Plays when mission m2_full is done.
// Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 6, ch2. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch2_flags

=== ch2_flags ===
90% leased. Pearl writes it on a napkin and tapes it to the booth. # id: ch2_flags.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Over at the bakery, Pip is building the Corridor out of pastry boxes. # id: ch2_flags.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Your center is on it now. It is a kolache box with windows drawn on. # id: ch2_flags.open.03 # speaker: narrator
The water tower is a paper cup. # id: ch2_flags.open.04 # speaker: narrator
Then a truck door slams across the street. # id: ch2_flags.open.05 # speaker: narrator
A crew walks the empty field, planting orange flags. # id: ch2_flags.open.06 # speaker: narrator
A lifted truck idles beside them. The window comes down. # id: ch2_flags.open.07 # speaker: narrator
Brock Delacroix looks at your whole center. It takes him one second. # id: ch2_flags.open.08 # speaker: narrator
Cute. # id: ch2_flags.open.09 # speaker: rival
* [Wave. # id: ch2_flags.pick.01 # rel: rival +2]
    Brock waves back before he can stop himself. # id: ch2_flags.wave.01 # speaker: narrator
    That wasn't a wave. I was checking the wind. # id: ch2_flags.wave.02 # speaker: rival
* [Count his flags out loud. # id: ch2_flags.pick.02 # rel: rival -2 # rel: office_manager +2]
    You count 31 flags. Out loud. Slowly. # id: ch2_flags.count.01 # speaker: narrator
    32. You missed one. It's behind the truck. # id: ch2_flags.count.02 # speaker: rival
    32. Noted, hon. # id: ch2_flags.count.03 # speaker: office_manager
* [Ask Pearl to pull his permit file. # id: ch2_flags.pick.03 # rel: office_manager +3 # city: goodwill +1]
    Pearl is already dialing. The clerk's office still answers her on the first ring. # id: ch2_flags.file.01 # speaker: narrator
    31 years, hon. I know which drawer. # id: ch2_flags.file.02 # speaker: office_manager
- Brock's window goes up. The truck stays. # id: ch2_flags.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
By pie time, Pearl has his file. She reads it standing up. # id: ch2_flags.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
Bigger than yours. Same ramp. Hearing is Thursday. # id: ch2_flags.hook.03 # speaker: office_manager
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch2_line.ink:
// Story ch2, scene 1 (writer A). Plays when chapter 2 opens. Leads into mission m2_first_lease.
// Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 6, ch2. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch2_line

=== ch2_line ===
Your shops have walls now. They also have For Lease signs. # id: ch2_line.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Nobody calls. Nobody wants to be shop number four on the Triple Flop. # id: ch2_line.open.02 # speaker: narrator
So you buy a rope, four posts and a sign. Line starts here. # id: ch2_line.open.03 # speaker: narrator
Pearl brings her bingo club. 11 ladies and a man named Dub. # id: ch2_line.open.04 # speaker: narrator
A work truck slows down. The driver leans out. # id: ch2_line.open.05 # speaker: narrator
Ma'am, what's the line for? # id: ch2_line.open.06 # speaker: neighbor
No idea, hon. I am holding a spot. # id: ch2_line.open.07 # speaker: office_manager
He parks. He gets in line. # id: ch2_line.open.08 # speaker: narrator
By noon the line bends around the lot. # id: ch2_line.open.09 # speaker: narrator
A fellow near the back is selling his spot. He does not know what for. # id: ch2_line.open.10 # speaker: narrator
A dusty ranch truck rolls past. Lorraine does not even stop. # id: ch2_line.open.11 # speaker: narrator
You built a line. Now build a reason. # id: ch2_line.open.12 # speaker: mentor
A woman walks the line with flour on one sleeve, counting heads. # id: ch2_line.open.13 # speaker: narrator
42 people. For nothing. Imagine if you had bread. # id: ch2_line.open.14 # speaker: baker
* [Wave Rosa over. Pip already told her about you. # id: ch2_line.door.01 # hide_if_mem: kid_partner lowballed # rel: baker +5]
    You're the one from the stand. Pip says you're all right. # id: ch2_line.warm.01 # speaker: baker
    He also says you don't own a hat. # id: ch2_line.warm.02 # speaker: baker
* [Wave Rosa over. She heard about the stand. # id: ch2_line.door.02 # show_if_mem: kid_partner lowballed # rel: baker -5 # lease: free_months +2]
    You're the one who gave my son a twenty. # id: ch2_line.cold.01 # speaker: baker
    He framed it. It hangs over my register. It is not a thank you. # id: ch2_line.cold.02 # speaker: baker
    I'll hear you out. It will cost you two free months. # id: ch2_line.cold.03 # speaker: baker
- Rosa Delgado. Delgado Family Bakery. I need a corner with a window. # id: ch2_line.corner.01 # speaker: baker
People buy bread they can see. # id: ch2_line.corner.02 # speaker: baker
* [Promise her the corner. Shake on it. # id: ch2_line.pick.01 # deal: handshake # rel: baker +6]
    The corner with the window. I heard you. So did 42 people. # id: ch2_line.shake.01 # speaker: baker
* [Promise the corner and the first month free. # id: ch2_line.pick.02 # deal: handshake # lease: free_months +1 # rel: baker +8]
    A free month buys a lot of flour. Thank you. I mean it. # id: ch2_line.shake.02 # speaker: baker
* [Promise the corner at full rent, not a dollar less. # id: ch2_line.pick.03 # deal: handshake # lease: rent_pct +5 # rel: baker -2]
    Full rent. Fine. Then that window had better be big. # id: ch2_line.shake.03 # speaker: baker
- Rosa shakes your hand. Now you have flour on it. # id: ch2_line.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
She loads three trays into your kolache truck and opens the side door. # id: ch2_line.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
Pastries go down the whole line. The line finally has a reason. # id: ch2_line.hook.03 # speaker: narrator
Pearl clicks her clicker. # id: ch2_line.hook.04 # speaker: narrator
63 served, hon. Dub went through twice. # id: ch2_line.hook.05 # speaker: office_manager
Nobody has said Triple Flop all day. # id: ch2_line.hook.06 # speaker: narrator
Now sign her lease. # id: ch2_line.hook.07 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch3_bankable.ink:
// Story ch3, chapter close (writer A). Plays when mission m3_income is done.
// The bank only says yes at this payment or no: Gil names no rates or terms here.
// Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 6, ch3. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch3_bankable

=== ch3_bankable ===
Prairie Lantern Savings. Gil's desk. # id: ch3_bankable.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Bolo tie. One sharp pencil. A folder with your name on it, getting thick. # id: ch3_bankable.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Gil reads the last page. Then he reads it again, out of habit. # id: ch3_bankable.open.03 # speaker: narrator
A good track record beats a good pitch. # id: ch3_bankable.open.04 # speaker: banker
You have one now. You are bankable. # id: ch3_bankable.open.05 # speaker: banker
He says it like a man reading a thermometer. # id: ch3_bankable.open.06 # speaker: narrator
From Gil, that is a parade. # id: ch3_bankable.open.07 # speaker: narrator
* [Buy the whole booth a round of pie. # id: ch3_bankable.pick.01 # cash: personal -40 # rel: office_manager +3 # rel: mentor +2]
    You call the Honeycomb from the bank lobby. Pie for the whole booth. # id: ch3_bankable.pie.01 # speaker: narrator
    Lorraine gets pecan. She tips her hat to the pie. # id: ch3_bankable.pie.02 # speaker: narrator
* [Tell Gil the pitch was pretty good too. # id: ch3_bankable.pick.02 # rel: banker -1 # rel: rival +1]
    The pitch was a napkin, {player_name}. It had syrup on it. # id: ch3_bankable.pitch.01 # speaker: banker
    I said yes to the record. The napkin is in a drawer. # id: ch3_bankable.pitch.02 # speaker: banker
* [Promise Gil the same homework every time. # id: ch3_bankable.pick.03 # rel: banker +4]
    Then I'll keep sharpening the same pencil. # id: ch3_bankable.work.01 # speaker: banker
    Gil almost smiles. The bolo tie moves a little. # id: ch3_bankable.work.02 # speaker: narrator
- Back at the booth, you say the word out loud. Bankable. # id: ch3_bankable.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Pearl looks up from her pie. # id: ch3_bankable.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
The diner phone rings. She gets there first. # id: ch3_bankable.hook.03 # speaker: narrator
{company_name}, head office. Please hold. # id: ch3_bankable.hook.04 # speaker: office_manager
It's the bank, hon. He says you left before the important part. # id: ch3_bankable.hook.05 # speaker: office_manager
I held one thing back. I wanted you sitting down. # id: ch3_bankable.hook.06 # speaker: banker
It is time you paid yourself. # id: ch3_bankable.hook.07 # speaker: banker
Pearl hangs up for you. Then she slides a folded paper across the table. # id: ch3_bankable.hook.08 # speaker: narrator
On payday, we talk. # id: ch3_bankable.hook.09 # speaker: office_manager
Outside, the truck coughs. The jingle plays slow. # id: ch3_bankable.hook.10 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch3_count.ink:
// Story ch3, scene 1 (writer A). Plays when mission m3_rival is done, after cs_rival_challenge.
// Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 6, ch3. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch3_count

=== ch3_count ===
Two lawn chairs by the Exit 14 ramp. # id: ch3_count.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Pearl counts cars with a clicker. Amos watches the hole across the street. # id: ch3_count.open.02 # speaker: narrator
She counts. I watch. We do not talk about it. # id: ch3_count.open.03 # speaker: fence_regular
That one is Brock's hole. Three. Big. No heart. # id: ch3_count.open.04 # speaker: fence_regular
Pearl clicks twice and hands you a page. # id: ch3_count.open.05 # speaker: narrator
Here's the honest count, hon. You won't like it. # id: ch3_count.open.06 # speaker: office_manager
Build your next row of shops and that ramp jams. Right by the car wash. # id: ch3_count.open.07 # speaker: office_manager
I counted three times. Same answer. Numbers are stubborn that way. # id: ch3_count.open.08 # speaker: office_manager
A man jogs over from the car wash, still holding a sponge. # id: ch3_count.open.09 # speaker: narrator
Danny Okoro. That's my wash. I count cars too. For fun. # id: ch3_count.open.10 # speaker: car_wash_owner
I had 212 cars Saturday. You close that ramp, I have 12. # id: ch3_count.open.11 # speaker: car_wash_owner
And those 12 are my cousins. They don't pay. # id: ch3_count.open.12 # speaker: car_wash_owner
You need something the council can see. You know a kid with boxes. # id: ch3_count.open.13 # speaker: narrator
* [Ask Pip for a scale model. He does it for a kolache. # id: ch3_count.door.01 # hide_if_mem: kid_partner lowballed # rel: kid_partner +3]
    One kolache. Sausage. And my name goes on the model. # id: ch3_count.warm.01 # speaker: kid_partner
    Small. On the bottom. Like the pros do. # id: ch3_count.warm.02 # speaker: kid_partner
* [Ask Pip for a scale model. He sends an invoice. Line 3 says "Lowball tax." # id: ch3_count.door.02 # show_if_mem: kid_partner lowballed # cash: company -500 # rel: kid_partner +1]
    Line 1, boxes. Line 2, glue. Line 3, lowball tax. # id: ch3_count.cold.01 # speaker: kid_partner
    It's a pricing thing. I told you. # id: ch3_count.cold.02 # speaker: kid_partner
- The model is pastry boxes, stuck together with frosting. It is, somehow, correct. # id: ch3_count.model.01 # speaker: narrator
The hearing is Thursday. What do you carry into that room? # id: ch3_count.model.02 # speaker: narrator
* [Bring Danny to speak for himself. # id: ch3_count.pick.01 # city: approval_pct +5 # rel: car_wash_owner +4]
    Me? At a microphone? Okay. I'll wear the good shirt. # id: ch3_count.danny.01 # speaker: car_wash_owner
    It's this shirt. But clean. # id: ch3_count.danny.02 # speaker: car_wash_owner
* [Give the Courier a copy of the count first. # id: ch3_count.pick.02 # rel: reporter +5 # city: goodwill +2]
    Della Marsh at the Courier reads it. She calls back in four minutes. # id: ch3_count.press.01 # speaker: narrator
    The bad number, to a reporter, on purpose. Bold, hon. Or honest. # id: ch3_count.press.02 # speaker: office_manager
* [Bring the model and a smile. # id: ch3_count.pick.03 # city: approval_pct -3 # rel: rival +2]
    A smile is not a traffic study, hon. # id: ch3_count.smile.01 # speaker: office_manager
    Brock is bringing one too. His has more teeth. # id: ch3_count.smile.02 # speaker: office_manager
- You drive back through downtown. # id: ch3_count.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
The Brass Clock Depot says 4:10. It always says 4:10. # id: ch3_count.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
Back at the booth, a notice from Mayor Vu is waiting. Pearl has already stamped it. # id: ch3_count.hook.03 # speaker: narrator
The council votes Thursday. Bring the traffic study. # id: ch3_count.hook.04 # speaker: mayor
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch3_hearing.ink:
// Story ch3, scene 2, the big choice (writer A). The talk for mission m3_hearing. It takes the place of the
// generic council hearing talk for this one hearing; cs_hearing_result (the vote) plays right after it.
// Writes the Danny memory: car_wash_owner helped (truth) or car_wash_owner burned (door memory for ch9).
// Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 6, ch3. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch3_hearing

=== ch3_hearing ===
Thursday. The council hearing. Every seat is taken. # id: ch3_hearing.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Brock goes first. He has a video. It has music and a drone. # id: ch3_hearing.open.02 # speaker: narrator
He also has 40 fans in matching shirts. BROCK YES. # id: ch3_hearing.open.03 # speaker: narrator
Mayor Vu points at one of them. # id: ch3_hearing.open.04 # speaker: narrator
Sir, where do you live? # id: ch3_hearing.open.05 # speaker: mayor
The service department, ma'am. # id: ch3_hearing.open.06 # speaker: crew
They all work at the family car lot. One is still holding a tire. # id: ch3_hearing.open.07 # speaker: narrator
Your turn. Your model is pastry boxes. One tower still says Sunup Kolaches. # id: ch3_hearing.open.08 # speaker: narrator

@dialogue/story/ch4_car_lot.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch4_car_lot

// ch4, Treat yourself. Plays when the player reaches the car lot for mission m4_car, before the shop opens.
// Never names the car the player buys. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
=== ch4_car_lot ===
Saturday. The kolache truck dies on Exit 14. One last jingle, very slow. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.01 # speaker: narrator
The only lot close enough to push it to is Delacroix Motors. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Family rule: every Delacroix sells cars on Saturday. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.03 # speaker: narrator
So the salesman walking over has a name tag. It says: Hi, I am Brock. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.04 # speaker: narrator
Welcome to Delacroix Motors. I have to say that. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.05 # speaker: rival
I also have to smile. This is the smile. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.06 # speaker: rival
He walks you to a lifted truck. The Ridgeback Trailmaster. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.07 # speaker: narrator
It has 9 cup holders. You have had 9 good ideas, total. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.08 # speaker: rival
The office door opens. Miss Odette Delacroix, 78, owner. Brock stands up straight. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.09 # speaker: narrator
If the deal is not sweet, it is not Odette. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.10 # speaker: car_lot_owner
She rides along on your test drive. So does Brock. Nobody invited Brock. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.11 # speaker: narrator
Turn signal. Good. Parking. C minus. My late husband parked like that. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.12 # speaker: car_lot_owner
C minus? Grandma. Look at that back tire. That's a D. # id: ch4_car_lot.open.13 # speaker: rival
* [Park it again, slower. # id: ch4_car_lot.grade.01 # rel: car_lot_owner +5]
    B. Do not let it go to your head. # id: ch4_car_lot.grade.02 # speaker: car_lot_owner
    You never gave me a B. # id: ch4_car_lot.grade.03 # speaker: rival
    You never parked it again. # id: ch4_car_lot.grade.04 # speaker: car_lot_owner
* [Tell her the lines are crooked. # id: ch4_car_lot.grade.05 # rel: car_lot_owner -3 # rel: rival +3]
    I painted those lines myself. In 1989. # id: ch4_car_lot.grade.06 # speaker: car_lot_owner
    Brock laughs so hard his name tag falls off. # id: ch4_car_lot.grade.07 # speaker: narrator
* [Ask her for a parking lesson. # id: ch4_car_lot.grade.08 # rel: car_lot_owner +8 # rel: rival -2]
    Finally. A student. Brock, get the cones. # id: ch4_car_lot.grade.09 # speaker: car_lot_owner
    Brock groans. Then he gets the cones. # id: ch4_car_lot.grade.10 # speaker: narrator
-
Miss Odette studies the top of your head. # id: ch4_car_lot.hat.01 # speaker: narrator
A developer with no hat. Hm. # id: ch4_car_lot.hat.02 # speaker: car_lot_owner
While everyone is busy, Gerald leaves with the hood badge off Brock's truck. # id: ch4_car_lot.hat.03 # speaker: narrator
Back at the lot, Pip Delgado waits by the dead truck. He has a jar of quarters. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.01 # speaker: narrator
How much for the truck? I'm asking as a buyer. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.02 # speaker: kid_partner
Mom needs a pastry truck. This one already smells right. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.03 # speaker: kid_partner
* [Sell it to Pip for his jar of quarters. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.04 # cash: personal +37 # rel: kid_partner +6]
    Deal. I want a receipt. I'll write it. You sign it. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.05 # speaker: kid_partner
    Fair price for a dead truck. B plus. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.06 # speaker: car_lot_owner
    -> horn_thanks
* [Give it to him. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.07 # rel: kid_partner +10 # rel: baker +4]
    Free? What's the catch? I'm checking under it anyway. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.08 # speaker: kid_partner
    Bad business. Good manners. A minus. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.09 # speaker: car_lot_owner
    -> horn_thanks
* [Sell it to the scrap man for more. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.10 # cash: personal +400 # rel: kid_partner -8]
    The scrap man pays more. Pip watches the tow truck hook up. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.11 # speaker: narrator
    Fine. That's business. I'll buy it off him by Monday. I'm writing down what it costs me. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.12 # speaker: kid_partner
    A in math. See me after class. # id: ch4_car_lot.truck.13 # speaker: car_lot_owner
    -> horn_reminder

= horn_thanks
Pip Delgado. Owner of one dead truck. Put that on a card. # id: ch4_car_lot.horn.01 # speaker: kid_partner
He holds up the speaker off the roof. Wires hang from it. # id: ch4_car_lot.horn.02 # speaker: narrator
Whatever you drive off in, this goes in the horn. It is a thank you. # id: ch4_car_lot.horn.03 # speaker: kid_partner
-> hook

= horn_reminder
Come Monday I'm Pip Delgado, owner of one dead truck. No thanks to you. # id: ch4_car_lot.horn.04 # speaker: kid_partner
He holds up the speaker off the roof. He got to it before the tow truck did. # id: ch4_car_lot.horn.05 # speaker: narrator
Whatever you drive off in, this goes in the horn. It is a reminder. # id: ch4_car_lot.horn.06 # speaker: kid_partner
-> hook

= hook
He already talked to the service department. The jingle still will not turn off. # id: ch4_car_lot.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
A car that sings about kolaches. Cute. # id: ch4_car_lot.hook.02 # speaker: rival
Your phone buzzes. Jazmine. Brock reads it over your shoulder. # id: ch4_car_lot.hook.03 # speaker: narrator
Ski town. July. Old lodge. Owner has to sell. You first, for now. # id: ch4_car_lot.hook.04 # speaker: top_broker
I love skiing. # id: ch4_car_lot.hook.05 # speaker: rival
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch4_tab.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch4_tab

// ch4, Treat yourself. Plays when mission m4_pay is done. The big choice is Pearl's tab (door memory: office_manager broke_deal).
// Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
=== ch4_tab ===
Payday at the Honeycomb Diner. Your first real paycheck sits on the table. # id: ch4_tab.open.01 # speaker: narrator
You have checked it 9 times. It is still real. # id: ch4_tab.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Lorraine Okafor stops at the booth. She does not sit. # id: ch4_tab.open.03 # speaker: narrator
You paid yourself, {player_name}. About time. # id: ch4_tab.open.04 # speaker: mentor
A developer who never takes a paycheck makes bad choices at midnight. # id: ch4_tab.open.05 # speaker: mentor
She tips her hat to Pearl on her way out. # id: ch4_tab.open.06 # speaker: narrator
Pip Delgado slides into her spot. He is looking at the check. # id: ch4_tab.open.07 # speaker: narrator
Is that a real paycheck? Can I hold it? # id: ch4_tab.open.08 # speaker: kid_partner
* [Let him hold it. # id: ch4_tab.hold.01 # rel: kid_partner +2]
    It's real. I checked the back. You should frame it. # id: ch4_tab.hold.02 # speaker: kid_partner
* [Tell him to earn his own. # id: ch4_tab.hold.03 # rel: kid_partner -1]
    I'm working on it. I have a five year plan. It's on a napkin. # id: ch4_tab.hold.04 # speaker: kid_partner
-
Across the table, Pearl Tackett clicks her red pen. Once. # id: ch4_tab.tab.01 # speaker: narrator
Hon, it's payday. We talk on payday. # id: ch4_tab.tab.02 # speaker: office_manager
She unfolds the paper from last week. Then she keeps unfolding it. # id: ch4_tab.tab.03 # speaker: narrator
It runs off the table and into Pip's lap. # id: ch4_tab.tab.04 # speaker: narrator
My tab. Every hour since the napkin. In red pen. # id: ch4_tab.tab.05 # speaker: office_manager
Line 12. "Fixed the spelling of Corridor. Twice." She billed you for that. # id: ch4_tab.tab.06 # speaker: kid_partner
Line 30. Pie, received. Credited. # id: ch4_tab.tab.07 # speaker: office_manager
I am not asking a favor, hon. We shook on it. # id: ch4_tab.tab.08 # speaker: office_manager
Pie now, pay when you are bankable. Gil said the word. # id: ch4_tab.tab.09 # speaker: office_manager
The tab is fair. It also costs about one flashy ride. # id: ch4_tab.tab.10 # speaker: narrator
* [Pay the whole tab today. The flashy ride can wait. # id: ch4_tab.pick.01 # rep: honor_handshake # mem: office_manager honored_deal # cash: company -45000 # build: surprise_cost_pct -5]
    You write the check. Your hand only shakes a little. # id: ch4_tab.spare.01 # speaker: narrator
    Pearl reads it twice. She caps the pen. # id: ch4_tab.spare.02 # speaker: narrator
    Good. Now, you spelled payroll wrong. # id: ch4_tab.spare.03 # speaker: office_manager
    I want a tab too. My advice isn't free. # id: ch4_tab.spare.04 # speaker: kid_partner
    Get in line, hon. I'll make you a folder. # id: ch4_tab.spare.05 # speaker: office_manager
    She makes you one too. The label says Surprises. She plans to keep it thin. # id: ch4_tab.spare.06 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: {company_name} pays its office manager in full. # id: ch4_tab.news.01 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: the payday of the year. # id: ch4_tab.news.02 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: who keeps parking a kolache truck by the diner door. # id: ch4_tab.news.03 # speaker: narrator
    -> close
* [Pay half now and half next year. # id: ch4_tab.pick.02 # mem: office_manager stalled_payment # cash: company -22000]
    You write a check for half. You promise the rest next year. # id: ch4_tab.half.01 # speaker: narrator
    Pearl looks at the check. Then at you. Then at the check. # id: ch4_tab.half.02 # speaker: narrator
    I will add a line for interest. In red. # id: ch4_tab.half.03 # speaker: office_manager
    She adds it while you watch. She does not hurry. # id: ch4_tab.half.04 # speaker: narrator
    That's a lot of red. # id: ch4_tab.half.05 # speaker: kid_partner
    It's my best color, hon. # id: ch4_tab.half.06 # speaker: office_manager
    Cedar Glade Courier: {company_name} pays half a tab. The rest is due next year. # id: ch4_tab.news.04 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: red pen trouble on the Corridor. Is your tab next. # id: ch4_tab.news.05 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: does half a tab get you half a parking spot. # id: ch4_tab.news.06 # speaker: narrator
    -> close
* [Say the deal was pie, and pie was paid. # id: ch4_tab.pick.03 # rep: take_better_offer # mem: office_manager broke_deal # build: surprise_cost_pct +10 # rel: mentor -6]
    Pearl looks at you for a long moment. # id: ch4_tab.ruin.01 # speaker: narrator
    She caps the pen and picks up her purse. # id: ch4_tab.ruin.02 # speaker: narrator
    Then I will go where the pie is better. # id: ch4_tab.ruin.03 # speaker: office_manager
    She leaves the tab on the table. She takes the clicker. # id: ch4_tab.ruin.04 # speaker: narrator
    She did all the permits. Who reads the fine print now? Not me. I have school. # id: ch4_tab.ruin.05 # speaker: kid_partner
    Next morning a phone rings across the street. # id: ch4_tab.ruin.06 # speaker: narrator
    Delacroix Ventures, head office. Please hold. # id: ch4_tab.ruin.07 # speaker: office_manager
    You keep the cash. You lose Pearl. # id: ch4_tab.ruin.08 # speaker: narrator
    By supper, Lorraine has heard all about it. # id: ch4_tab.ruin.09 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: Delacroix Ventures hires a new office manager. # id: ch4_tab.news.07 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: the walkout of the year. # id: ch4_tab.news.08 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: the good booth at the diner is open. Parking is still bad. # id: ch4_tab.news.09 # speaker: narrator
    -> close

= close
Out in the lot, the truck coughs. The jingle plays, slow and sad. # id: ch4_tab.close.01 # speaker: narrator
Now go buy a car. The truck does not sound good. # id: ch4_tab.close.02 # speaker: kid_partner
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch5_gondola.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch5_gondola

// ch5, Plant a second flag. Plays when mission m5_trip is done, after cs_flight. ch7 reads this choice through Brock's relationship score.
// Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
=== ch5_gondola ===
Pine Ridge in July. Quiet streets. Cheap everything. # id: ch5_gondola.open.01 # speaker: narrator
One gondola goes up to the Silver Bell Lodge. You get in. # id: ch5_gondola.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Brock Delacroix is already inside. He is in full ski gear. # id: ch5_gondola.open.03 # speaker: narrator
My guy said dress for the market. It's a ski market. # id: ch5_gondola.open.04 # speaker: rival
Don't look at the boots. # id: ch5_gondola.open.05 # speaker: rival
You look at the boots. They are very orange. # id: ch5_gondola.open.06 # speaker: narrator
Halfway up, the gondola stops. It swings. Then it does nothing. # id: ch5_gondola.open.07 # speaker: narrator
A speaker says it will be a short delay. # id: ch5_gondola.open.08 # speaker: narrator
It is not short. It is an hour. # id: ch5_gondola.open.09 # speaker: narrator
I'm fine. I'm great. Quit moving around. # id: ch5_gondola.open.10 # speaker: rival
Brock is holding the bench with both gloves. # id: ch5_gondola.open.11 # speaker: narrator
I'm not scared of heights. I'm scared of this height. # id: ch5_gondola.open.12 # speaker: rival
A mountain jay lands on the window ledge. It eyes your sandwich. # id: ch5_gondola.open.13 # speaker: narrator
It is not Gerald. Gerald is at home, robbing someone you know. # id: ch5_gondola.open.14 # speaker: narrator
By minute 40, Brock has run out of things to brag about. # id: ch5_gondola.open.15 # speaker: narrator
You know that thing I say. All hat, no cattle. # id: ch5_gondola.open.16 # speaker: rival
My dad calls me all hat too. # id: ch5_gondola.open.17 # speaker: rival
Every Saturday. Right there on the lot. # id: ch5_gondola.open.18 # speaker: rival
The cabin is quiet. Even the jay looks away. # id: ch5_gondola.open.19 # speaker: narrator
* [Promise it stays in the cabin. # id: ch5_gondola.pick.01 # rel: rival +8]
    Brock nods. He lets go of the bench with one hand. # id: ch5_gondola.keep.01 # speaker: narrator
    Good. Okay. This does not make us friends. # id: ch5_gondola.keep.02 # speaker: rival
    It makes us two people who got stuck. That's all. # id: ch5_gondola.keep.03 # speaker: rival
* [Trade him a secret. You practice your handshake in the mirror. # id: ch5_gondola.pick.02 # rel: rival +10]
    In the mirror? Who shakes back? # id: ch5_gondola.trade.01 # speaker: rival
    You show him. He takes it very seriously. # id: ch5_gondola.trade.02 # speaker: narrator
    Firm. Too much eye contact. B minus. # id: ch5_gondola.trade.03 # speaker: rival
* [Laugh until the cabin swings. # id: ch5_gondola.pick.03 # rel: rival -6]
    The cabin swings. Brock grabs the bench with both hands again. # id: ch5_gondola.laugh.01 # speaker: narrator
    Stop. Stop laughing. You're rocking it. # id: ch5_gondola.laugh.02 # speaker: rival
    I take it back. My dad says I'm great. # id: ch5_gondola.laugh.03 # speaker: rival
-
The gondola jerks. Then it moves. # id: ch5_gondola.moves.01 # speaker: narrator
Brock breathes out for the first time in an hour. # id: ch5_gondola.moves.02 # speaker: narrator
Tell anyone and I will outbid you on everything, forever. # id: ch5_gondola.moves.03 # speaker: rival
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch5_lodge.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch5_lodge

// ch5, Plant a second flag. The talk for mission m5_deal. The big choice is Nettie's question (door memory: lodge_owner lowballed).
// All three big replies close the deal so the mission counts. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
=== ch5_lodge ===
The Silver Bell Lodge. Log walls. A stone fireplace. A woman with a pen. # id: ch5_lodge.open.01 # speaker: narrator
You are the second Texan this week. The other one is wearing skis in my lobby. # id: ch5_lodge.open.02 # speaker: lodge_owner
Brock waves from the fireplace. He cannot get the skis off. # id: ch5_lodge.open.03 # speaker: narrator
Nettie Pruitt. I am 81. I ran this lodge before there was a gondola. # id: ch5_lodge.open.04 # speaker: lodge_owner
Cedar Glade, you said? I left 40 years ago. My nephew Walt never did. # id: ch5_lodge.open.05 # speaker: lodge_owner
There are 6 buckets on the lobby floor. Each one has a name tag. # id: ch5_lodge.open.06 # speaker: narrator
Mind Harold. He fills up fastest. # id: ch5_lodge.open.07 # speaker: lodge_owner
* [Carry Harold out and empty him. # id: ch5_lodge.bucket.01 # rel: lodge_owner +3]
    Harold is heavier than he looks. You get most of him to the porch. # id: ch5_lodge.bucket.02 # speaker: narrator
    Strong back. Wet shoes. I have hired worse. # id: ch5_lodge.bucket.03 # speaker: lodge_owner
* [Ask who named the buckets. # id: ch5_lodge.bucket.04 # rel: lodge_owner +2]
    I did. After my brothers. # id: ch5_lodge.bucket.05 # speaker: lodge_owner
    They were no help in the rain either. # id: ch5_lodge.bucket.06 # speaker: lodge_owner
-
I need a new roof before the first snow. I cannot pay for one. # id: ch5_lodge.roof.01 # speaker: lodge_owner
So I sell. I would rather stay. Nobody ever writes that part down. # id: ch5_lodge.roof.02 # speaker: lodge_owner
She names her price. It is low. It is a July price. # id: ch5_lodge.roof.03 # speaker: narrator
Folks fly in every July with a checkbook and a smile. # id: ch5_lodge.roof.04 # speaker: lodge_owner
Think how that feels when it lands in your town. # id: ch5_lodge.roof.05 # speaker: lodge_owner
Your phone buzzes. Jazmine. # id: ch5_lodge.text.01 # speaker: narrator
Pine Ridge voted last night. Second gondola line. # id: ch5_lodge.text.02 # speaker: top_broker
It ends at her front door. She has not heard. You did not get this from me. # id: ch5_lodge.text.03 # speaker: top_broker
Nettie sets down the pen. She looks right at you. # id: ch5_lodge.ask.01 # speaker: narrator
Anything I should know before I sign? # id: ch5_lodge.ask.02 # speaker: lodge_owner
* [Tell her about the new line. Pay what the lodge is really worth. # id: ch5_lodge.pick.01 # rep: fair_buyout # mem: lodge_owner fair_price # deal: price_pct +40 # deal: close # rel: neighbor_leader +6]
    You hand her your phone. She reads the text twice. # id: ch5_lodge.fair.01 # speaker: narrator
    Well. Then my price was wrong. And you said so. # id: ch5_lodge.fair.02 # speaker: lodge_owner
    I have met honest buyers before. None of them flew in. # id: ch5_lodge.fair.03 # speaker: lodge_owner
    You pay the real price. It is a lot more. She signs. # id: ch5_lodge.fair.04 # speaker: narrator
    Harold stays with the roof. Be kind to him. # id: ch5_lodge.fair.05 # speaker: lodge_owner
    You told her. On purpose. With your own mouth. # id: ch5_lodge.fair.06 # speaker: rival
    Brock laughs at you all the way to the airport. # id: ch5_lodge.fair.07 # speaker: narrator
    That night she phones her nephew Walt. # id: ch5_lodge.fair.08 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: {company_name} buys a Pine Ridge lodge at full price. # id: ch5_lodge.news.01 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: Texan pays extra on purpose. The shock of the year. # id: ch5_lodge.news.02 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: does a gondola have parking. Asking for July. # id: ch5_lodge.news.03 # speaker: narrator
    -> flag
* [Tell her, and make her a partner. She keeps her room and a share. # id: ch5_lodge.pick.02 # rep: fair_buyout # mem: lodge_owner helped # deal: price_pct +10 # deal: close # rel: neighbor_leader +8]
    You hand her your phone. Then you slide the papers back. # id: ch5_lodge.partner.01 # speaker: narrator
    New deal. She keeps her room, and a share of the lodge. # id: ch5_lodge.partner.02 # speaker: narrator
    A partner. At 81. My sister will be furious. Good. # id: ch5_lodge.partner.03 # speaker: lodge_owner
    I keep the room over the kitchen. And I keep naming the buckets. # id: ch5_lodge.partner.04 # speaker: lodge_owner
    She's going to boss you around for 20 years. # id: ch5_lodge.partner.05 # speaker: rival
    Make it 30. # id: ch5_lodge.partner.06 # speaker: lodge_owner
    Brock laughs at you all the way to the airport. # id: ch5_lodge.partner.07 # speaker: narrator
    That night she phones her nephew Walt. # id: ch5_lodge.partner.08 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: {company_name} and Nettie Pruitt are partners in Pine Ridge. # id: ch5_lodge.news.04 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: the partnership of the year. One of them is 81. # id: ch5_lodge.news.05 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: the lodge has 6 buckets and no parking. We checked. # id: ch5_lodge.news.06 # speaker: narrator
    -> flag
* ["Not a thing." Buy at her price. # id: ch5_lodge.pick.03 # rep: lowball_buyout # mem: lodge_owner lowballed # deal: price_pct -5 # deal: close # rel: neighbor_leader -10]
    You say it with a smile. Not a thing. # id: ch5_lodge.lie.01 # speaker: narrator
    Nettie looks at you a moment longer than you like. # id: ch5_lodge.lie.02 # speaker: narrator
    I have been lied to by better dressed people than you. # id: ch5_lodge.lie.03 # speaker: lodge_owner
    So I suppose you are honest. # id: ch5_lodge.lie.04 # speaker: lodge_owner
    She signs. It is the best deal of your life. # id: ch5_lodge.lie.05 # speaker: narrator
    That price? For that view? I feel sick. Nice work. # id: ch5_lodge.lie.06 # speaker: rival
    That night she phones her nephew Walt. She has a feeling. # id: ch5_lodge.lie.07 # speaker: narrator
    In January the new line opens. Nettie learns what she sold. # id: ch5_lodge.lie.08 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: {company_name} buys a Pine Ridge lodge. The price was low. # id: ch5_lodge.news.07 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: the steal of the year. Can you do it too. Tonight at ten. # id: ch5_lodge.news.08 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: nice lodge. Where do I park. # id: ch5_lodge.news.09 # speaker: narrator
    -> flag

= flag
You own land in two cities. Only one of them has a gondola. # id: ch5_lodge.flag.01 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch5_windmill.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch5_windmill

// ch5, Plant a second flag. Chapter close, plays when mission m5_flag is done. Plants the ch8 promise: every reply ends with it made.
// Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
=== ch5_windmill ===
Home. Greenfield Edge. Grass to the sky, and one old windmill. # id: ch5_windmill.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Your horn plays the jingle at the gate. Three cows look up. None of them are yours. # id: ch5_windmill.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Lorraine Okafor waits under the windmill. She heard you coming. Everyone did. # id: ch5_windmill.open.03 # speaker: narrator
I have watched you since the water tower lot, {player_name}. # id: ch5_windmill.open.04 # speaker: mentor
You made some good calls. You made some loud ones. # id: ch5_windmill.open.05 # speaker: mentor
This is Okafor land. To that fence, and past it. # id: ch5_windmill.open.06 # speaker: mentor
I will sell it to you. A whole community. Streets, shops, front porches. # id: ch5_windmill.open.07 # speaker: mentor
No stack of papers today. Your word. Two conditions. # id: ch5_windmill.open.08 # speaker: mentor
But first, my question. What does it do for the neighbors? # id: ch5_windmill.open.09 # speaker: mentor
She does not wait for your answer. She brought her own. # id: ch5_windmill.open.10 # speaker: narrator
School first. Park first. Before the first house sells. # id: ch5_windmill.open.11 # speaker: mentor
I told June Albrecht your word is good. I told every rancher out here. # id: ch5_windmill.open.12 # speaker: mentor
Do not make a liar of me. Say it out loud. # id: ch5_windmill.open.13 # speaker: mentor
* [Say it out loud. School first. Park first. # id: ch5_windmill.pick.01 # deal: handshake # rel: mentor +6]
    Louder. The cows did not hear you. # id: ch5_windmill.loud.01 # speaker: mentor
    You say it louder. One cow nods. Probably at a fly. # id: ch5_windmill.loud.02 # speaker: narrator
* [Say it, then ask why she never shakes your hand. # id: ch5_windmill.pick.02 # deal: handshake # rel: mentor +8]
    You say it. Then you ask. She almost smiles. # id: ch5_windmill.hand.01 # speaker: narrator
    You get the hand when the job is done. Until then you get the hat. # id: ch5_windmill.hand.02 # speaker: mentor
* [Say it, then ask for the creek pasture too. # id: ch5_windmill.pick.03 # deal: handshake # rel: mentor -3]
    You say it. Then you point at the creek pasture. # id: ch5_windmill.creek.01 # speaker: narrator
    You asked for dessert before grace. No. # id: ch5_windmill.creek.02 # speaker: mentor
    The promise stands. The pasture stays mine. # id: ch5_windmill.creek.03 # speaker: mentor
-
She tips her hat. She does not shake. # id: ch5_windmill.hat.01 # speaker: narrator
That is a handshake you owe me. # id: ch5_windmill.hat.02 # speaker: mentor
She drives off. The windmill creaks. Your phone rings. # id: ch5_windmill.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Earlene Pruitt, Redbud Square. Aunt Nettie says you buy tired buildings. # id: ch5_windmill.hook.02 # speaker: square_cousin
I have a picture house to sell. Bring a flashlight. The last crew says it is haunted. # id: ch5_windmill.hook.03 # speaker: square_cousin
-> END
