@dialogue/story/ch6_paint.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch6_paint

// ch6, Fix one up. Chapter close, plays when mission m6_fix is done. Door on Pearl (ch4): she settles it, or Mayor Vu does.
// Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
=== ch6_paint ===
The Ruby is almost done. It needs paint. # id: ch6_paint.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Heritage rule 41: the new paint must match the old paint. # id: ch6_paint.open.02 # speaker: narrator
It was Barn Red. I was there. # id: ch6_paint.open.03 # speaker: neighbor_leader
It was Brick Red, Walt. I painted it. # id: ch6_paint.open.04 # speaker: square_cousin
You painted the trim. # id: ch6_paint.open.05 # speaker: neighbor_leader
The trim is the part people look at! # id: ch6_paint.open.06 # speaker: square_cousin
The Heritage Society meets to settle it. The meeting runs two hours. # id: ch6_paint.open.07 # speaker: narrator
At minute 90, somebody orders sandwiches. They argue about those too. # id: ch6_paint.open.08 # speaker: narrator
It will fall down before we agree, Walt. # id: ch6_paint.open.09 # speaker: square_cousin
Then it falls down Barn Red. # id: ch6_paint.open.10 # speaker: neighbor_leader
Somebody has to end this. # id: ch6_paint.open.11 # speaker: narrator
* [Let Pearl settle it. # id: ch6_paint.door.01 # hide_if_mem: office_manager broke_deal # rel: office_manager +3]
    Pearl Tackett uncaps her red pen. The room goes quiet out of habit. # id: ch6_paint.pearl.01 # speaker: narrator
    Chips on the table, please. Side by side. Thank you, hon. # id: ch6_paint.pearl.02 # speaker: office_manager
    Now turn them over. Read me the numbers on the back. # id: ch6_paint.pearl.03 # speaker: office_manager
* [Let Mayor Vu settle it. # id: ch6_paint.door.02 # show_if_mem: office_manager broke_deal # rel: mayor +2]
    Pearl would have ended this in one minute. Pearl answers Brock's phone now. # id: ch6_paint.vu.01 # speaker: narrator
    So you call Mayor Vu. She brings her own gavel. # id: ch6_paint.vu.02 # speaker: narrator
    I have a budget vote at four. Chips on the table. Turn them over. # id: ch6_paint.vu.03 # speaker: mayor
-
Two paint chips sit side by side. # id: ch6_paint.chips.01 # speaker: narrator
Same red. Same number on the back. They are the same chip. # id: ch6_paint.chips.02 # speaker: narrator
The cousins do not speak for a week. # id: ch6_paint.chips.03 # speaker: narrator
That night the Ruby's lights come on. First time in 20 years. # id: ch6_paint.chips.04 # speaker: narrator
Over at the bakery, Pip adds a tiny Ruby to his pastry box city. # id: ch6_paint.chips.05 # speaker: narrator
Amos Tulley watches the lights from his lawn chair. # id: ch6_paint.amos.01 # speaker: narrator
Six. Do not get excited. # id: ch6_paint.amos.02 # speaker: fence_regular
Then he holds up the small brass key. # id: ch6_paint.amos.03 # speaker: narrator
It winds the Brass Clock. She stopped at 4:10, the day the rail yard closed. # id: ch6_paint.amos.04 # speaker: fence_regular
She has not ticked since. # id: ch6_paint.amos.05 # speaker: fence_regular
* [Tell him to keep the key. # id: ch6_paint.key.01 # rel: fence_regular +8]
    Amos puts the key in his shirt pocket. He buttons the pocket. # id: ch6_paint.key.02 # speaker: narrator
    A bird had it long enough. My turn. # id: ch6_paint.key.03 # speaker: fence_regular
* [Ask what he would score a clock that runs. # id: ch6_paint.key.04 # rel: fence_regular +4 # rel: downtown_owner +2]
    Ask me when it runs. # id: ch6_paint.key.05 # speaker: fence_regular
    By morning, the Halloway Trust has heard that somebody asked. # id: ch6_paint.key.06 # speaker: narrator
-
Your phone lights up. # id: ch6_paint.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Channel 6 Glade News: the cranes have stopped. # id: ch6_paint.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
A small plane lands at Cedar Glade Regional. # id: ch6_paint.hook.03 # speaker: narrator
A man steps out in a new cowboy hat. The price tag is still on it. # id: ch6_paint.hook.04 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch6_ruby.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch6_ruby

// ch6, Fix one up. Plays when chapter 6 opens. Door on Nettie (ch5), then the contractor pick, then the ghost.
// Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
=== ch6_ruby ===
Redbud Square. Red brick, a courthouse, and the Ruby picture house. # id: ch6_ruby.open.01 # speaker: narrator
The Ruby has been dark for 20 years. The sign still says Now Showing. It does not say what. # id: ch6_ruby.open.02 # speaker: narrator
She's all yours, {player_name}. The roof is a little bit optional. # id: ch6_ruby.open.03 # speaker: square_cousin
Walt loves the past. I love a cashier's check. # id: ch6_ruby.open.04 # speaker: square_cousin
Walt Pruitt waits at the door. There is a ruler in his back pocket. # id: ch6_ruby.open.05 # speaker: narrator
That building was here before you were born. # id: ch6_ruby.open.06 # speaker: neighbor_leader
My Aunt Nettie called from Pine Ridge. She had a lot to say about you. # id: ch6_ruby.open.07 # speaker: neighbor_leader
He holds something out to you. # id: ch6_ruby.open.08 # speaker: narrator
* [Take what Walt hands you. It is a coffee. # id: ch6_ruby.door.01 # hide_if_mem: lodge_owner lowballed # rel: neighbor_leader +4]
    She says you were straight with her. Two sugars. Do not get used to it. # id: ch6_ruby.coffee.01 # speaker: neighbor_leader
* [Take what Walt hands you. It is a rule book. # id: ch6_ruby.door.02 # show_if_mem: lodge_owner lowballed # rel: neighbor_leader -4 # city: fee_pct +2]
    She says to watch you. So here. The heritage rules. All 300 pages. # id: ch6_ruby.rules.01 # speaker: neighbor_leader
-
First you need a contractor. Two trucks are parked out front. # id: ch6_ruby.hire.01 # speaker: narrator
Hector Salinas. I build it right. That costs more and takes longer. # id: ch6_ruby.hire.02 # speaker: careful_contractor
Hank Dobbs. I can start today. I may have started already. # id: ch6_ruby.hire.03 # speaker: fast_contractor
* [Hire Hector Salinas. Careful, and he costs more. # id: ch6_ruby.hire.04 # build: surprise_cost_pct -10 # build: speed_pct -10 # rel: careful_contractor +5]
    Good. First I find out what holds this place up. # id: ch6_ruby.hector.01 # speaker: careful_contractor
    Paint and habit. Mostly habit. We will fix that. # id: ch6_ruby.hector.02 # speaker: careful_contractor
* [Hire Hank Dobbs. Fast and cheap. # id: ch6_ruby.hire.05 # build: speed_pct +15 # build: surprise_cost_pct +15 # rel: fast_contractor +5]
    Hank finishes the tear out in two days. # id: ch6_ruby.hank.01 # speaker: narrator
    Good news. It is done. Other news. Come look at something. # id: ch6_ruby.hank.02 # speaker: fast_contractor
    He took out one wall too many. It belonged to the feed store. A customer waves. # id: ch6_ruby.hank.03 # speaker: narrator # cash: company -8000
    Real sorry about the wall. It looked like one of ours. # id: ch6_ruby.hank.04 # speaker: fast_contractor
-
Then the crew stops work. A full crew in hard hats, standing in the street. # id: ch6_ruby.ghost.01 # speaker: narrator
Something is upstairs. It rattles all night. Then it screeches. # id: ch6_ruby.ghost.02 # speaker: crew
The Ruby is haunted. Ask the last crew. We do not do screeching. # id: ch6_ruby.ghost.03 # speaker: crew
Pip Delgado walks past all of them with a broom. # id: ch6_ruby.ghost.04 # speaker: narrator
Ghosts don't pay rent. I'll go look. # id: ch6_ruby.ghost.05 # speaker: kid_partner
A screech. A thump. Then Pip, laughing. # id: ch6_ruby.ghost.06 # speaker: narrator
Come up here. You have to see this. Bring a bag. # id: ch6_ruby.ghost.07 # speaker: kid_partner
The ghost is one grackle. His nest is everything shiny that ever went missing. # id: ch6_ruby.nest.01 # speaker: narrator
Your grand opening ribbon. The tip of the gold shovel. Mayor Vu's reading glasses. # id: ch6_ruby.nest.02 # speaker: narrator
The hood badge off Brock's truck. And one small brass key. # id: ch6_ruby.nest.03 # speaker: narrator
Gerald looks very pleased. # id: ch6_ruby.nest.04 # speaker: narrator
Brock drives over to get his badge in person. # id: ch6_ruby.nest.05 # speaker: narrator
I filed a police report about that. # id: ch6_ruby.nest.06 # speaker: rival
They asked what the thief looked like. I said shiny, loud and rude. They wrote down my name. # id: ch6_ruby.nest.07 # speaker: rival
Amos Tulley has moved his lawn chair to the square. Pip hands him the key. # id: ch6_ruby.key.01 # speaker: narrator
Amos turns the key over in his hand. # id: ch6_ruby.key.02 # speaker: narrator
I know this key. # id: ch6_ruby.key.03 # speaker: fence_regular
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch6_stairs.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch6_stairs

// ch6, Fix one up. Plays in the first quarter of the fix up. The big choice is Mrs. Alvarado (door memory: holdout_neighbor evicted).
// Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
=== ch6_stairs ===
Under the Ruby's grand stairs there is a door. Nobody told you that you bought it. # id: ch6_stairs.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Behind it: one sewing machine, 400 spools of thread, and Mrs. Alvarado. # id: ch6_stairs.open.02 # speaker: narrator
You are the new owner. Stand still. Your sleeve is too long. # id: ch6_stairs.open.03 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
She has a pin in your cuff before you can say hello. # id: ch6_stairs.open.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Hold still. # id: ch6_stairs.pin.01 # rel: holdout_neighbor +3]
    Good. The last owner wiggled. I left his cuffs crooked. # id: ch6_stairs.pin.02 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
* [Say your sleeve is fine. # id: ch6_stairs.pin.03 # rel: holdout_neighbor -2]
    It is not fine. I could see it from across the square. # id: ch6_stairs.pin.04 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
-
I live upstairs. I sew down here. 40 years now. # id: ch6_stairs.rent.01 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
The first owner and I shook on that rent. Nobody ever asked me to shake again. # id: ch6_stairs.rent.02 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
You look up the rent. The crew spends more than that on lunch. # id: ch6_stairs.rent.03 # speaker: narrator
I have outlasted four owners. You seem nice. You will be the fifth. # id: ch6_stairs.rent.04 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
The plans are plain. Without her shop, the lobby is bigger and the job is faster. # id: ch6_stairs.rent.05 # speaker: narrator
Across the square, Walt Pruitt and the Heritage Society watch. One pair of binoculars. They take turns. # id: ch6_stairs.rent.06 # speaker: narrator
Well? Other arm. # id: ch6_stairs.rent.07 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
* [Build around her. The old handshake stands. # id: ch6_stairs.pick.01 # rep: honor_handshake # mem: holdout_neighbor honored_deal # build: speed_pct -15 # cash: company -40000 # rel: neighbor_leader +10 # neighbor: complaints -2]
    You hold out your hand. She looks at it for a while. # id: ch6_stairs.spare.01 # speaker: narrator
    40 years. Somebody finally asked. # id: ch6_stairs.spare.02 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
    She shakes. Then she goes back to your sleeve. # id: ch6_stairs.spare.03 # speaker: narrator
    The crew redraws the lobby around one small door. It costs more. It takes longer. # id: ch6_stairs.spare.04 # speaker: narrator
    Walt crosses the square. He shakes your hand in front of everybody. # id: ch6_stairs.spare.05 # speaker: narrator
    I still do not like your windows. # id: ch6_stairs.spare.06 # speaker: neighbor_leader
    Cedar Glade Courier: new owner of the Ruby keeps a 40 year old handshake. # id: ch6_stairs.news.01 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: the handshake of the year. # id: ch6_stairs.news.02 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: lovely news about the Ruby. The square still has 9 parking spots. # id: ch6_stairs.news.03 # speaker: narrator
    -> close
* [Pay a fair price and move her to a new shop on the square. # id: ch6_stairs.pick.02 # rep: fair_buyout # mem: holdout_neighbor fair_price # cash: company -60000 # rel: neighbor_leader +3]
    You find her a shop on the square with a real window. You pay for the move, and then some. # id: ch6_stairs.move.01 # speaker: narrator
    A window. After 40 years under the stairs. I will have to buy a plant. # id: ch6_stairs.move.02 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
    It is a fair price. I will miss the stairs. Both things are true. # id: ch6_stairs.move.03 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
    She hems the curtains for the new Ruby anyway. # id: ch6_stairs.move.04 # speaker: narrator
    I hemmed the curtains. You may thank me by leaving them alone. # id: ch6_stairs.move.05 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
    Across the square, Walt nods once. From Walt, that is a parade. # id: ch6_stairs.move.06 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: sewing shop moves onto the square. The Ruby's owner pays for it. # id: ch6_stairs.news.04 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: the move of the year. One woman. 400 spools. # id: ch6_stairs.news.05 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: the new sewing shop took my parking spot. Good hems, though. # id: ch6_stairs.news.06 # speaker: narrator
    -> close
* [End the old rent. She is out by the end of the month. # id: ch6_stairs.pick.03 # rep: lowball_buyout # mem: holdout_neighbor evicted # build: speed_pct +10 # neighbor: complaints +3 # rel: neighbor_leader -15]
    You say it plainly. The old rent ends. She has until the end of the month. # id: ch6_stairs.ruin.01 # speaker: narrator
    She takes the pins out of your sleeve. One at a time. # id: ch6_stairs.ruin.02 # speaker: narrator
    Then you are the fifth. I was right about that part. # id: ch6_stairs.ruin.03 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
    She loses her home and her shop in one week. # id: ch6_stairs.ruin.04 # speaker: narrator
    The job runs faster. The lobby is grand. Your sleeve is still too long. # id: ch6_stairs.ruin.05 # speaker: narrator
    Her face is on every Fence Line post about you. # id: ch6_stairs.ruin.06 # speaker: narrator
    Walt writes one line in the rule book. He underlines it twice. # id: ch6_stairs.ruin.07 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: Mrs. Alvarado leaves the Ruby after 40 years. # id: ch6_stairs.news.07 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: out after 40 years. The story of the year. # id: ch6_stairs.news.08 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: she hemmed my wedding dress. Also, where do we park for the meeting. # id: ch6_stairs.news.09 # speaker: narrator
    -> close

= close
The Heritage Society will remember this. # id: ch6_stairs.close.01 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch7_bust.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch7_bust

// ch7 opens, after the career beat "bust". Door on Rosa (ch2), then Thad, then the pledge.
=== ch7_bust ===
Channel 6 Glade News: the storm of the century hits Cedar Glade. # id: ch7_bust.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Channel 6 Glade News: one hour later. A second storm of the century. # id: ch7_bust.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Grant Pellerin of Channel 6 reports doom in front of a sign. It says CLOSING. # id: ch7_bust.open.03 # speaker: narrator
The camera pulls back. CLOSING AT 9 PM. Under it, a happy line waits for tacos. # id: ch7_bust.open.04 # speaker: narrator
The bust is real, though. For lease signs pop up like dandelions. # id: ch7_bust.open.05 # speaker: narrator
I have stopped smiling, {player_name}. Cash is tight. Hold on to yours. # id: ch7_bust.open.06 # speaker: banker
To save money, {company_name} moves back to the diner booth. # id: ch7_bust.open.07 # speaker: narrator
The pie case is your lobby again. Honestly, it is a good lobby. # id: ch7_bust.open.08 # speaker: narrator
* [Stop by the bakery. The window is lit. # id: ch7_bust.door.01 # hide_if_mem: baker broke_deal # rel: baker +3]
    The corner window glows. The line is short, but it is a line. # id: ch7_bust.lit.01 # speaker: narrator
    Two slow months. I can pay half now and half in spring. # id: ch7_bust.lit.02 # speaker: baker
    Pip's pastry box city sits in the window. Business there is booming. # id: ch7_bust.lit.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Drive past the back bay. The window is dark. # id: ch7_bust.door.02 # show_if_mem: baker broke_deal # rel: kid_partner -3]
    The back bay never had much of a window. Now it has no light either. # id: ch7_bust.dark.01 # speaker: narrator
    A paper sign on the door says BACK SOON. It does not say when. # id: ch7_bust.dark.02 # speaker: narrator
    Cluckwell Chicken got the corner. Today it has one customer. He is lost. # id: ch7_bust.dark.03 # speaker: narrator
-
Back at the diner, a stranger is sitting in your booth. # id: ch7_bust.thad.01 # speaker: narrator
New cowboy hat. The price tag is still on it. # id: ch7_bust.thad.02 # speaker: narrator
Thad Pemberton. Buzzard Peak Partners. I love this little town. # id: ch7_bust.thad.03 # speaker: outside_buyer
What is it called again? # id: ch7_bust.thad.04 # speaker: outside_buyer
I will have one barbecue, please. # id: ch7_bust.thad.05 # speaker: outside_buyer
Gerald the grackle lands on the window sill. He stares at the price tag. # id: ch7_bust.thad.06 # speaker: narrator
Well, look at that. A crow. Friendly little crow. # id: ch7_bust.thad.07 # speaker: outside_buyer
Gerald is not a crow. Gerald is not friendly. # id: ch7_bust.thad.08 # speaker: narrator
* [Tell Thad the price tag is still on his hat. # id: ch7_bust.tag.01 # rel: outside_buyer +2]
    Oh, I know. I like to remember what things cost. # id: ch7_bust.tag.02 # speaker: outside_buyer
    Gerald leans closer. Gerald would also like to know what it cost. # id: ch7_bust.tag.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Say nothing. Gerald saw it first. # id: ch7_bust.tag.04 # rel: outside_buyer -1]
    The tag swings when Thad nods. Gerald nods along with it. # id: ch7_bust.tag.05 # speaker: narrator
    You know something Thad does not. It feels nice. It will not last. # id: ch7_bust.tag.06 # speaker: narrator
-
I will be plain, friend. Hard times are my good times. # id: ch7_bust.plan.01 # speaker: outside_buyer
I buy towns like this at half price. Nothing personal. It's just math. # id: ch7_bust.plan.02 # speaker: outside_buyer
The door bell rings. Marisol Villanueva walks in with a pen and a tape measure. # id: ch7_bust.plan.03 # speaker: narrator
Don't get up. I already measured the booth. You fit. # id: ch7_bust.plan.04 # speaker: grocer
Every landlord on this street gets the same pledge and the same pen. # id: ch7_bust.plan.05 # speaker: grocer
Fair rent for small shops until the bust is over. Sign, or don't. # id: ch7_bust.plan.06 # speaker: grocer
Charming. Where I come from, we call that leaving money on the table. # id: ch7_bust.plan.07 # speaker: outside_buyer
Where I come from, we call it Tuesday. The pen is right there. # id: ch7_bust.plan.08 # speaker: grocer
* [Sign the pledge. # id: ch7_bust.pledge.01 # rep: tenant_rent_break # rel: ten +6 # rel: grocer +6 # lease: rent_pct -10]
    One name. I can even read it. Good. # id: ch7_bust.sign.01 # speaker: grocer
    Rent comes down a notch at every shop you own. The lights stay on. # id: ch7_bust.sign.02 # speaker: narrator
* [Sign it, and add a free month for the smallest shops. # id: ch7_bust.pledge.02 # rep: tenant_rent_break # rel: ten +10 # rel: grocer +8 # lease: free_months +1 # rel: bank -3]
    A free month. I did not ask for that. # id: ch7_bust.more.01 # speaker: grocer
    I am writing it big, so the next landlord has to look at it. # id: ch7_bust.more.02 # speaker: grocer
    Gil hears about it by lunch. He does not start smiling. # id: ch7_bust.more.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Pass. You have a bank to feed too. # id: ch7_bust.pledge.03 # rel: ten -6 # rel: grocer -6 # rel: bank +2]
    Fair enough. I will write "thinking" next to your name. In pencil. # id: ch7_bust.pass.01 # speaker: grocer
    The pen goes back in her pocket. Every shop on your street hears about it. # id: ch7_bust.pass.02 # speaker: narrator
-
Thad stands up. He sets his card on your pie plate. In the meringue. # id: ch7_bust.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Gerald watches the price tag walk out the door. # id: ch7_bust.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
When somebody on this street goes under, call me first. # id: ch7_bust.hook.03 # speaker: outside_buyer
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch7_cranes.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch7_cranes

// Chapter close, when m7_storm is done. Three way door on the ch7 choice, then the hook for ch8.
=== ch7_cranes ===
Morning. A sound you forgot about. One diesel engine. Then five. # id: ch7_cranes.open.01 # speaker: narrator
All over the city, the cranes are moving again. # id: ch7_cranes.open.02 # speaker: narrator
{company_name} kept every building. Some of them by a whisker. # id: ch7_cranes.open.03 # speaker: narrator
You look across the street. # id: ch7_cranes.open.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Open the envelope on your windshield. # id: ch7_cranes.door.01 # show_if_mem: rival helped # rel: rival +5]
    A thank you card. Inside, in block letters: THIS NEVER HAPPENED. THANKS. # id: ch7_cranes.saved.01 # speaker: narrator
    Under the wiper sits a coffee can. Your parking money is in it. # id: ch7_cranes.saved.02 # speaker: narrator
    Across the street, the Delacroix letters are still on the wall. Somebody polished them. # id: ch7_cranes.saved.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Watch a crane lift the Delacroix letters off the wall. # id: ch7_cranes.door.02 # show_if_mem: rival burned # rel: car_lot_owner -5]
    The D comes down first. It swings a while, like it is thinking it over. # id: ch7_cranes.gone.01 # speaker: narrator
    Brock sells cars every day now, not just Saturdays. He is good at it. # id: ch7_cranes.gone.02 # speaker: narrator
    Miss Odette's radio ad still says the deal is sweet. She reads it slower. # id: ch7_cranes.gone.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Read the new sign across the street. # id: ch7_cranes.door.03 # hide_if_mem: rival helped # hide_if_mem: rival burned # rel: outside_buyer -2]
    Buzzard Peak Plaza. The old letters left pale marks on the wall. # id: ch7_cranes.sold.01 # speaker: narrator
    The sign spells Corridor wrong. Nobody at Buzzard Peak has noticed. # id: ch7_cranes.sold.02 # speaker: narrator
    Brock waves from the car lot. It is a small wave. He has a customer. # id: ch7_cranes.sold.03 # speaker: narrator
-
Back at the booth, Gil is waiting. He is smiling again. It looks a little rusty. # id: ch7_cranes.gil.01 # speaker: narrator
You rode out the bust, {player_name}. You kept every building. # id: ch7_cranes.gil.02 # speaker: banker
A good track record beats a good pitch. Now you have both. # id: ch7_cranes.gil.03 # speaker: banker
You are big enough to sell shares of your company. Time to ring the bell. # id: ch7_cranes.gil.04 # speaker: banker
* [Ask what the bell looks like. # id: ch7_cranes.bell.01 # rel: banker +2]
    Big. Brass. Loud. I'm guessing. I have never been. # id: ch7_cranes.bell.02 # speaker: banker
* [Ask who you answer to after that. # id: ch7_cranes.bell.03 # rel: inv +2]
    Everyone who buys a share. Some of them will sell lemonade. # id: ch7_cranes.bell.04 # speaker: banker
* [Order pie for the table first. # id: ch7_cranes.bell.05 # rel: banker +3 # cash: personal -20]
    Yes. At this slice. # id: ch7_cranes.bell.06 # speaker: banker
-
Somebody slides into the booth next to Gil. Same hat. Same price tag. # id: ch7_cranes.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Gerald lands on the sill. He has waited on that tag all year. # id: ch7_cranes.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
Thad lays a check on the table. It is a very large check. It covers the pie. # id: ch7_cranes.hook.03 # speaker: narrator
Congratulations, friend. I want in before the bell. One small condition. # id: ch7_cranes.hook.04 # speaker: outside_buyer
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch7_kolache_day.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch7_kolache_day

// Second quarter of the bust. The laugh, then the big choice. Writes: rival helped | rival burned | nothing (stay out).
=== ch7_kolache_day ===
Your shops are hurting. So {company_name} throws Dollar Kolache Day. # id: ch7_kolache_day.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Grackle Talk 98. Big Earl Tibbs: one dollar, one kolache, zero excuses. # id: ch7_kolache_day.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Pip's pastry truck plays the old jingle all morning. He made a copy. He did not add an off switch. # id: ch7_kolache_day.open.03 # speaker: narrator
You planned for 300 people. About 3,000 show up. # id: ch7_kolache_day.open.04 # speaker: narrator
Coach Ames, Truck Watch. Four minutes a truck. My junior varsity unloads faster. # id: ch7_kolache_day.open.05 # speaker: neighbor
He blows his whistle. The whole line takes one step forward. # id: ch7_kolache_day.open.06 # speaker: narrator
The line crosses the street and fills the lot at Brock's half empty center. # id: ch7_kolache_day.open.07 # speaker: narrator
So Brock Delacroix stands at his own gate, holding a coffee can. # id: ch7_kolache_day.open.08 # speaker: narrator
Parking. Two dollars. No, I don't take kolaches. Okay. One kolache. # id: ch7_kolache_day.open.09 # speaker: rival
It is his first income in months. He keeps it in the coffee can. # id: ch7_kolache_day.open.10 # speaker: narrator
* [Pay Brock for the whole line's parking. # id: ch7_kolache_day.park.01 # rel: rival +4 # cash: company -600]
    Exact change. From you. This is the worst day of my life. # id: ch7_kolache_day.park.02 # speaker: rival
    He counts it twice. Then he shakes the can, just to hear it. # id: ch7_kolache_day.park.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Tell him your crowd earns you a cut. # id: ch7_kolache_day.park.04 # rel: rival -3 # cash: company +200]
    A cut? Of my lot? Fine. Here. Don't spend it all on dirt. # id: ch7_kolache_day.park.05 # speaker: rival
    He hands you a fistful of ones. They smell like coffee. # id: ch7_kolache_day.park.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Send him a kolache. On the house. # id: ch7_kolache_day.park.07 # rel: rival +2]
    I did not ask for this. Is it peach? I'm keeping it. # id: ch7_kolache_day.park.08 # speaker: rival
    He eats it behind the gate, where nobody can see him enjoy it. # id: ch7_kolache_day.park.09 # speaker: narrator
-
That night, Pip counts the take. He is a teenager now. He counts faster. # id: ch7_kolache_day.pip.01 # speaker: narrator
Every shop on your street sold out. Mom ran out of flour twice. # id: ch7_kolache_day.pip.02 # speaker: kid_partner
So. What does it do for the neighbors? # id: ch7_kolache_day.pip.03 # speaker: kid_partner
You ask who taught him that. # id: ch7_kolache_day.pip.04 # speaker: narrator
You did. Loudly. # id: ch7_kolache_day.pip.05 # speaker: kid_partner
The diner door rings. Brock, hat in hand. You have never seen the top of his head. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ask.01 # speaker: narrator
Cute booth. Sorry. Habit. I need to sit down. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ask.02 # speaker: rival
I built too big, too fast. The bank takes my center in a few weeks. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ask.03 # speaker: rival
And behind that loan sits the car lot. Grandma's lot. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ask.04 # speaker: rival
Miss Odette Delacroix sits down beside him. She has never asked anyone for anything. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ask.05 # speaker: narrator
Posture, Brock. C plus. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ask.06 # speaker: car_lot_owner
He is loud. He is not bad. Do not let them take his name off the wall. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ask.07 # speaker: car_lot_owner
One table over, Thad Pemberton lifts his sweet tea. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ask.08 # speaker: narrator
Or you wait. The bank takes it. You and I split it for pennies. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ask.09 # speaker: outside_buyer
Nobody breaks a single rule. That is the lovely part. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ask.10 # speaker: outside_buyer
* [Buy a fair share of his center and help him fill it. # id: ch7_kolache_day.pick.01 # rep: fair_buyout # mem: rival helped # rival: site shared # cash: company -150000 # rel: car_lot_owner +10]
    -> fair
* [Keep your cash. Send him your waiting list tenants and share your crowds. # id: ch7_kolache_day.pick.02 # rel_req: rival 45 # mem: rival helped # rival: site shared # rel: ten -3 # lease: rent_pct -5 # rel: car_lot_owner +8]
    -> share
* [Team up with Thad. Buy it for pennies once the bank takes it. # id: ch7_kolache_day.pick.03 # rep: lowball_buyout # mem: rival burned # mem: outside_buyer helped # rival: site won # deal: price_pct -40 # rel: car_lot_owner -20]
    -> ruin
* [Stay out of it. # id: ch7_kolache_day.pick.04 # rival: site lost # rel: rival -8 # rel: car_lot_owner -8]
    -> out

You write the check. It stings. Your own buildings wanted that cash. # id: ch7_kolache_day.fair.01 # speaker: narrator
Fine. Partners. On one building. Do not make this weird. # id: ch7_kolache_day.fair.02 # speaker: rival
And I'm still charging you for parking. # id: ch7_kolache_day.fair.03 # speaker: rival
Handshake. Firm. B plus. I don't give an A. Ask my late husband. # id: ch7_kolache_day.fair.04 # speaker: car_lot_owner
She drops the car lot keys back in her purse. They jingle all the way down. # id: ch7_kolache_day.fair.05 # speaker: narrator

You keep your cash. Brock gets your waiting list and half your crowd. # id: ch7_kolache_day.share.01 # speaker: narrator
Your own tenants grumble. The kolache line has two ends now. # id: ch7_kolache_day.share.02 # speaker: narrator
You are sending me customers. On purpose. Do not make this weird. # id: ch7_kolache_day.share.03 # speaker: rival
No money changed hands and the boy is saved. A minus. Never tell him. # id: ch7_kolache_day.share.04 # speaker: car_lot_owner
Cedar Glade Courier: {company_name} sends shoppers and tenants across the street. # id: ch7_kolache_day.share.05 # speaker: narrator
-> news

= ruin
You look at Brock. Then you slide your chair over to Thad's table. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ruin.01 # speaker: narrator
You are my kind of people. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ruin.02 # speaker: outside_buyer
Thad shakes your hand. It is like shaking a calculator. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ruin.03 # speaker: narrator
I would have done that to you. Last year. Not this year. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ruin.04 # speaker: rival
I grade everything, young developer. I will not waste the ink on this. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ruin.05 # speaker: car_lot_owner
She takes Brock's arm. They leave the coffee can on your table. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ruin.06 # speaker: narrator
Cedar Glade Courier: {company_name} and Buzzard Peak wait to buy Delacroix center cheap. # id: ch7_kolache_day.ruin.07 # speaker: narrator
-> news

= out
You say it is not your fight. That is true. It is also handy. # id: ch7_kolache_day.out.01 # speaker: narrator
Right. Sure. Forget I took my hat off. # id: ch7_kolache_day.out.02 # speaker: rival
Not a yes. Not a no. Incomplete. See me after class. # id: ch7_kolache_day.out.03 # speaker: car_lot_owner
More for me, then. I do love a quiet partner. # id: ch7_kolache_day.out.04 # speaker: outside_buyer
Weeks later, Thad gets the center alone. Nobody thanks you. Nobody was going to. # id: ch7_kolache_day.out.05 # speaker: narrator
Cedar Glade Courier: bank to take Delacroix center. Out of town buyer waits. # id: ch7_kolache_day.out.06 # speaker: narrator
-> news

= news
Channel 6 Glade News: kolache storm of the century buries the Corridor. # id: ch7_kolache_day.news.01 # speaker: narrator
Fence Line: 3,000 people and one parking lot. It cost me two dollars. # id: ch7_kolache_day.news.02 # speaker: narrator
The bust is not over. Hold every building. # id: ch7_kolache_day.news.03 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch8_handshake.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch8_handshake

// The big choice of ch8, at the windmill. Writes: mentor honored_deal | mentor helped | mentor broke_deal (+ outside_buyer helped).
=== ch8_handshake ===
The Okafor windmill. Nothing out here but grass, wind and one old truck. # id: ch8_handshake.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Lorraine is sitting on the tailgate. She does not look surprised. # id: ch8_handshake.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Sit. I heard about that check before the ink was dry. # id: ch8_handshake.open.03 # speaker: mentor
June called. Then June's sister. Then June again, louder. # id: ch8_handshake.open.04 # speaker: mentor
The windmill creaks. It needs oil. It has needed oil since 1985. # id: ch8_handshake.open.05 # speaker: narrator
For once, you ask it first. What does it do for the neighbors? # id: ch8_handshake.open.06 # speaker: narrator
She is quiet for a while. The windmill is not. # id: ch8_handshake.open.07 # speaker: narrator
Which neighbors? That is the whole trouble. # id: ch8_handshake.open.08 # speaker: mentor
The family that needs a front door. Or the families who were promised a park. # id: ch8_handshake.open.09 # speaker: mentor
You gave me your word. School first, park first. I tipped my hat on it. # id: ch8_handshake.open.10 # speaker: mentor
* [Ask her what you should do. # id: ch8_handshake.ask.01 # rel: mentor +2]
    No. I taught you the question. The answer is your job. # id: ch8_handshake.ask.02 # speaker: mentor
* [Ask if a handshake can ever change. # id: ch8_handshake.ask.03 # rel: mentor +3]
    A handshake can be changed by the two who shook. Never by one. # id: ch8_handshake.ask.04 # speaker: mentor
* [Tell her about the nurse and the welder. # id: ch8_handshake.ask.05 # rel: mentor +2]
    They are neighbors too. Good. Now you see why it is hard. # id: ch8_handshake.ask.06 # speaker: mentor
-
The check is still on the diner table. Bell day is close. # id: ch8_handshake.pick.01 # speaker: narrator
* [Keep your word. School first, park first. Sell fewer shares, and sell them to the town. # id: ch8_handshake.pick.02 # rep: honor_handshake # mem: mentor honored_deal # cash: company -200000 # rel: inv -5 # rel: outside_buyer -10 # neighbor: complaints -2]
    -> kept
* [Ask Lorraine to change the deal with you. Keep the school, a smaller park, some smaller homes. # id: ch8_handshake.pick.03 # rel_req: mentor 75 # rep: honor_handshake # mem: mentor helped # cash: company -80000 # neighbor: complaints +1]
    -> changed
* [Take Thad's check. Drop the school and the park. # id: ch8_handshake.pick.04 # rep: take_better_offer # mem: mentor broke_deal # mem: outside_buyer helped # cash: company +400000 # rel: inv +8 # neighbor: complaints +3]
    -> broken

= kept
You call Thad from the windmill. It is a short call. # id: ch8_handshake.kept.01 # speaker: narrator
He says no hard feelings. He says it twice, which means a few. # id: ch8_handshake.kept.02 # speaker: narrator
Bell day will be smaller. The first shares go on sale at the diner counter. # id: ch8_handshake.kept.03 # speaker: narrator
Smaller bell. Same ring. # id: ch8_handshake.kept.04 # speaker: mentor
Lorraine tips her hat. She holds it a second longer than usual. # id: ch8_handshake.kept.05 # speaker: narrator
Cedar Glade Courier: developer keeps school and park, sells shares to the town. # id: ch8_handshake.kept.06 # speaker: narrator
Channel 6 Glade News: local developer turns down giant check. Is the developer okay. # id: ch8_handshake.kept.07 # speaker: narrator
Fence Line: a park. Great. Where do we park at the park. # id: ch8_handshake.kept.08 # speaker: narrator
-> bell

= changed
Now that is a question worth a pot of coffee. # id: ch8_handshake.changed.01 # speaker: mentor
You both draw on the tailgate until dark. The school stays. The park shrinks. # id: ch8_handshake.changed.02 # speaker: narrator
Small homes go in along the creek. Front doors a nurse can afford. # id: ch8_handshake.changed.03 # speaker: narrator
Lorraine calls June herself. June yells. Then June says fine. From June, that is a parade. # id: ch8_handshake.changed.04 # speaker: narrator
Two people shook. Two people changed it. That is how it is done. # id: ch8_handshake.changed.05 # speaker: mentor
Lorraine tips her hat. # id: ch8_handshake.changed.06 # speaker: narrator
Cedar Glade Courier: school stays, park shrinks, small homes added at Greenfield Edge. # id: ch8_handshake.changed.07 # speaker: narrator
Channel 6 Glade News: park shrinks. The shrink of the century. # id: ch8_handshake.changed.08 # speaker: narrator
Fence Line: smaller park, same question. Where do I park. # id: ch8_handshake.changed.09 # speaker: narrator
-> bell

= broken
You tell her about the bigger number. You say young families need houses. It is even true. # id: ch8_handshake.broken.01 # speaker: narrator
It is. And you gave your word anyway. # id: ch8_handshake.broken.02 # speaker: mentor
Lorraine does not tip her hat. She gets in the truck. The windmill creaks. # id: ch8_handshake.broken.03 # speaker: narrator
By Friday the ranchers have turned on her. They trusted her, and she trusted you. # id: ch8_handshake.broken.04 # speaker: narrator
An Okafor handshake used to settle things in Cedar Glade. Now folks ask for it in writing. # id: ch8_handshake.broken.05 # speaker: narrator
Her seat at the Honeycomb Diner stays empty. Nobody else will sit in it. # id: ch8_handshake.broken.06 # speaker: narrator
Cedar Glade Courier: developer drops school and park for more houses. Okafor deal broken. # id: ch8_handshake.broken.07 # speaker: narrator
Channel 6 Glade News: the letdown of the century. Details after the weather. # id: ch8_handshake.broken.08 # speaker: narrator
Fence Line: 400 new houses, zero new roads. Guess where they will park. # id: ch8_handshake.broken.09 # speaker: narrator
-> bell

= bell
Now ring the bell. # id: ch8_handshake.bell.01 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch8_meeting.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch8_meeting

// Right after cs_bell. The laugh, one door on the ch8 choice, then the hook for ch9.
=== ch8_meeting ===
After all those practice swings, the bell was a button. # id: ch8_meeting.open.01 # speaker: narrator
You pressed it very well. Good follow through. # id: ch8_meeting.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Your phone buzzes. It is a text from Brock. # id: ch8_meeting.open.03 # speaker: narrator
A button. Cute. # id: ch8_meeting.open.04 # speaker: rival
Amos Tulley bought exactly one share so he could come. He brought his lawn chair. # id: ch8_meeting.open.05 # speaker: narrator
Five. Too loud. No chairs. # id: ch8_meeting.open.06 # speaker: fence_regular
Next morning. The first owners meeting of {company_name}. # id: ch8_meeting.open.07 # speaker: narrator
Thad Pemberton has the front row. He bought his shares like anybody else. # id: ch8_meeting.open.08 # speaker: narrator
I never stay mad at money. Now. First order of business. # id: ch8_meeting.open.09 # speaker: outside_buyer
Three shares. Where do I sit? # id: ch8_meeting.open.10 # speaker: kid_partner
Pip bought them with pastry truck money. He is wearing a tie. It clips on. # id: ch8_meeting.open.11 # speaker: narrator
* [Look at the back row. There is a hat you know. # id: ch8_meeting.door.01 # hide_if_mem: mentor broke_deal # rel: mentor +2]
    Lorraine bought one share. She paid cash and asked for a receipt. # id: ch8_meeting.hat.01 # speaker: narrator
    I am not here to vote. I am here to watch. Carry on. # id: ch8_meeting.hat.02 # speaker: mentor
* [Look at the back row. There is one empty chair. # id: ch8_meeting.door.02 # show_if_mem: mentor broke_deal # rel: mentor -1]
    Somebody saved it out of habit. Nobody sits in it. # id: ch8_meeting.gap.01 # speaker: narrator
    June Albrecht stares at you over the top of it. She owns one share and one grudge. # id: ch8_meeting.gap.02 # speaker: narrator
-
Thad stands and clears his throat. Pip stands faster. # id: ch8_meeting.move.01 # speaker: narrator
Question. Why does the company lobby have no lemonade stand? # id: ch8_meeting.move.02 # speaker: kid_partner
This company started next to one. I was there. It's in writing. # id: ch8_meeting.move.03 # speaker: kid_partner
I move that the lobby gets a lemonade stand. # id: ch8_meeting.move.04 # speaker: kid_partner
Seconded. I like lemonade. # id: ch8_meeting.move.05 # speaker: fence_regular
Hold on. I own a great many more shares than this child. # id: ch8_meeting.move.06 # speaker: outside_buyer
Then you get a great many more cups. # id: ch8_meeting.move.07 # speaker: kid_partner
* [Vote yes. # id: ch8_meeting.vote.01 # rel: kid_partner +6]
    Every hand in the room goes up. Two of them belong to Pip. # id: ch8_meeting.vote.02 # speaker: narrator
* [Vote yes, and add a pastry case. # id: ch8_meeting.vote.03 # rel: kid_partner +8 # rel: baker +4 # cash: company -2000]
    Mom will want it by the window. She has strong feelings about windows. # id: ch8_meeting.vote.04 # speaker: kid_partner
* [Call the meeting to order. # id: ch8_meeting.vote.05 # rel: kid_partner -3 # rel: inv +2]
    You bang the gavel. It is a cowbell. The room votes while it is still ringing. # id: ch8_meeting.vote.06 # speaker: narrator
-
The motion passes. # id: ch8_meeting.pass.01 # speaker: narrator
What just happened? # id: ch8_meeting.pass.02 # speaker: outside_buyer
Up in the light fixture, Gerald watches the tag on Thad's hat. He leans. # id: ch8_meeting.pass.03 # speaker: narrator
Thad puts the hat in his lap. Gerald does not get the tag. Not today. # id: ch8_meeting.pass.04 # speaker: narrator
The town has made up its mind about you. # id: ch8_meeting.pass.05 # speaker: narrator
Your phone buzzes. Celeste Halloway. # id: ch8_meeting.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
About the air over the old rail yard. Lunch. Bring the plans. Leave the bird. # id: ch8_meeting.hook.02 # speaker: downtown_owner
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch8_offer.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch8_offer

// ch8 opens. Thad's condition, with a real pull on both sides. No big choice here: that is ch8_handshake.
=== ch8_offer ===
The check sits on the table. Nobody touches it. Gerald thinks about it. # id: ch8_offer.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Here is my condition. Greenfield Ledge. Your big story for bell day. # id: ch8_offer.open.02 # speaker: outside_buyer
Edge. # id: ch8_offer.open.03 # speaker: banker
That's the one. Drop the school. Drop the park. Fill that land with houses. # id: ch8_offer.open.04 # speaker: outside_buyer
More houses, bigger number, louder bell. Simple. # id: ch8_offer.open.05 # speaker: outside_buyer
I will be honest, {player_name}. The bigger number makes bell day easy. # id: ch8_offer.open.06 # speaker: banker
People who buy shares like big. They like it a lot. # id: ch8_offer.open.07 # speaker: banker
A young couple stops at your booth. A nurse and a welder. Two kids, one stroller. # id: ch8_offer.open.08 # speaker: narrator
Sorry to bother you. Are you the one building Greenfield Edge? # id: ch8_offer.open.09 # speaker: buyer
We have looked for a year. We can't find a house we can afford. # id: ch8_offer.open.10 # speaker: buyer
Build more. Please. We don't need a fancy park. We need a front door. # id: ch8_offer.open.11 # speaker: buyer
I grew up in a town that said no to everything. # id: ch8_offer.open.12 # speaker: outside_buyer
It is a museum now. Nice gift shop. # id: ch8_offer.open.13 # speaker: outside_buyer
Two stools down sits June Albrecht of the Greenfield ranchers. She listens on purpose. # id: ch8_offer.open.14 # speaker: narrator
New houses before new roads. Over my dead fence post. # id: ch8_offer.open.15 # speaker: neighbor
And that park was a promise. I was there. I brought the potato salad. # id: ch8_offer.open.16 # speaker: neighbor
Everybody here is a little bit right. That is the trouble. # id: ch8_offer.open.17 # speaker: narrator
Between meetings, you practice your bell swing in the parking lot. # id: ch8_offer.swing.01 # speaker: narrator
The cowbell is from Pruitt's Feed and Seed. It was made for a cow. # id: ch8_offer.swing.02 # speaker: narrator
Elbow up. No. Other elbow. You swing like you are swatting Gerald. # id: ch8_offer.swing.03 # speaker: kid_partner
You swing. The cowbell leaves the handle and lands in a hedge. # id: ch8_offer.swing.04 # speaker: narrator
Three. Follow through. # id: ch8_offer.swing.05 # speaker: fence_regular
* [Fetch the bell and swing again, harder. # id: ch8_offer.again.01 # rel: fence_regular +2]
    The bell stays on this time. A car alarm goes off two rows over. # id: ch8_offer.again.02 # speaker: narrator
    Still three. But the hedge respects you now. # id: ch8_offer.again.03 # speaker: fence_regular
* [Hand Pip the cowbell. # id: ch8_offer.again.04 # rel: kid_partner +3]
    Pip rings it once. Clean. A dog three blocks away sits. # id: ch8_offer.again.05 # speaker: narrator
    Wrists. It is all in the wrists. You can't teach it. I will try anyway. # id: ch8_offer.again.06 # speaker: kid_partner
-
Thad is still in the booth when you get back. So is the check. # id: ch8_offer.leave.01 # speaker: narrator
Well, friend? Bell day is coming. # id: ch8_offer.leave.02 # speaker: outside_buyer
* ["I need to talk to Lorraine first." # id: ch8_offer.leave.03 # rel: mentor +4 # rel: outside_buyer -2]
    The lady with the hat. Of course. Take your time. # id: ch8_offer.leave.04 # speaker: outside_buyer
    I will be right here. The barbecue is growing on me. # id: ch8_offer.leave.05 # speaker: outside_buyer
* ["Put the number in writing." # id: ch8_offer.leave.06 # rel: outside_buyer +4 # rel: inv +3]
    I like you. It is already in writing. I wrote it on the plane. # id: ch8_offer.leave.07 # speaker: outside_buyer
    He slides a folded page under the check. It has a lot of zeros. # id: ch8_offer.leave.08 # speaker: narrator
* ["The park is not for sale." # id: ch8_offer.leave.09 # rel: outside_buyer -5 # rel: mentor +2]
    Everything is for sale, friend. Some things just take a little longer. # id: ch8_offer.leave.10 # speaker: outside_buyer
    He smiles, tips the hat, and walks out. The tag waves goodbye. # id: ch8_offer.leave.11 # speaker: narrator
-
The check stays on the table, face up, next to the pie. # id: ch8_offer.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch9_air.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch9_air

// ch9 opens. Lunch with Celeste, then the tower hearing. Doors on Danny (ch3) and Mrs. Alvarado (ch6, through Walt).
=== ch9_air ===
Lunch is on floor 30 of a dark Halloway tower. One table. One lamp. # id: ch9_air.open.01 # speaker: narrator
You left the bird. The bird followed. Gerald sits on the ledge outside, looking hurt. # id: ch9_air.open.02 # speaker: narrator
I said leave the bird. # id: ch9_air.open.03 # speaker: downtown_owner
Far below lie the old rail yard and the Brass Clock Depot. # id: ch9_air.open.04 # speaker: narrator
The clock says 4:10. It has said 4:10 since 2009. # id: ch9_air.open.05 # speaker: narrator
I don't own that dirt. I own the air above it. It is very good air. # id: ch9_air.open.06 # speaker: downtown_owner
My family has waited since 1921. I can wait for a better buyer. # id: ch9_air.open.07 # speaker: downtown_owner
One rule. The lights stay on at night. I am tired of looking at dark. # id: ch9_air.open.08 # speaker: downtown_owner
Then, the tower hearing. All eight neighborhood leaders came. That has never happened. # id: ch9_air.hear.01 # speaker: narrator
Pip's pastry box city sits on the council table. The new tower is a cake box. # id: ch9_air.hear.02 # speaker: narrator
One at a time, please. Margaret, lower the fishing pole. # id: ch9_air.hear.03 # speaker: mayor
Theo Banerjee, Loft Dwellers. A grocery at the base, please. I eat dinner from a gas station. # id: ch9_air.hear.04 # speaker: neighbor
Marisol Villanueva. I will run that grocery. I already measured. # id: ch9_air.hear.05 # speaker: grocer
Ruth Calloway, Creekside. I knew about this in March. I walk three dogs past that yard. # id: ch9_air.hear.06 # speaker: neighbor
Margaret Thistlewood, Hillside. Taller than the trees. I knew it. # id: ch9_air.hear.07 # speaker: neighbor
Coach Ames, Truck Watch. I have a stopwatch on your cranes. They are slow. I like slow. # id: ch9_air.hear.08 # speaker: neighbor
Rocco Benedetti, Game Day Merchants. A crowd like this, I sell 300 meatballs. Build it. # id: ch9_air.hear.09 # speaker: neighbor
June Albrecht, Greenfield. Roads first. I say it every time. # id: ch9_air.hear.10 # speaker: neighbor
* [Nod to Danny Okoro. He nods back. # id: ch9_air.danny.01 # hide_if_mem: car_wash_owner burned # city: approval_pct +5]
    Danny Okoro, Frontage Road. This one told the truth about my ramp. It cost real money. # id: ch9_air.danny.02 # speaker: car_wash_owner
    I had 212 cars last Saturday. I counted. Build the tower. # id: ch9_air.danny.03 # speaker: car_wash_owner
* [Nod to Danny Okoro. He does not nod back. # id: ch9_air.danny.04 # show_if_mem: car_wash_owner burned # city: approval_pct -5]
    Danny Okoro, Frontage Road. I used to get 212 cars on a Saturday. # id: ch9_air.danny.05 # speaker: car_wash_owner
    Ask this developer where they went. Then check every number twice. # id: ch9_air.danny.06 # speaker: car_wash_owner
    In the press row, Della Marsh opens a thick folder. Your name is on the tab. # id: ch9_air.danny.07 # speaker: narrator
-
The last one up has a rule book and a ruler. # id: ch9_air.walt.01 # speaker: narrator
* [Look at Walt Pruitt. He opens the rule book. # id: ch9_air.walt.02 # hide_if_mem: holdout_neighbor evicted # city: approval_pct +5]
    Walt Pruitt, Heritage Society. I measured the drawings. Twice. # id: ch9_air.walt.03 # speaker: neighbor_leader
    I still do not like the windows. Build it. # id: ch9_air.walt.04 # speaker: neighbor_leader
* [Look at Walt Pruitt. He holds up a photo. # id: ch9_air.walt.05 # show_if_mem: holdout_neighbor evicted # city: approval_pct -5]
    It is a photo of a sewing shop under a staircase. # id: ch9_air.walt.06 # speaker: narrator
    40 years she was there. That is all I have to say. It is plenty. # id: ch9_air.walt.07 # speaker: neighbor_leader
-
You heard them, {player_name}. Now tell me what my air buys this town. # id: ch9_air.terms.01 # speaker: downtown_owner
* [Promise lights on every night and a grocery at the base. # id: ch9_air.terms.02 # deal: handshake # rel: downtown_owner +8 # city: approval_pct +5]
    Theo Banerjee claps once. Marisol is already measuring the mayor's table. # id: ch9_air.terms.03 # speaker: narrator
    Lights and lettuce. Fine. I have signed for less. # id: ch9_air.terms.04 # speaker: downtown_owner
* [Promise the lights, and give Amos the clock room. # id: ch9_air.terms.05 # deal: handshake # rel: downtown_owner +6 # rel: fence_regular +10]
    In the back row, a lawn chair creaks. Amos Tulley stands up. Nobody has seen that before. # id: ch9_air.terms.06 # speaker: narrator
    I will need a ladder. I have the key. # id: ch9_air.terms.07 # speaker: fence_regular
* [Offer more money and fewer promises. # id: ch9_air.terms.08 # deal: handshake # deal: price_pct +10 # rel: downtown_owner -6]
    Money. How original. We had money before that clock stopped. # id: ch9_air.terms.09 # speaker: downtown_owner
    I will take it. The lights still stay on. That part is not for sale. # id: ch9_air.terms.10 # speaker: downtown_owner
-
Celeste signs with a fountain pen older than the freeway. # id: ch9_air.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Do not make me regret the air. # id: ch9_air.hook.02 # speaker: downtown_owner
-> END

@dialogue/story/ch9_beam.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch9_beam

// The payoff, right before cs_topping_out. Ten doors, one per big choice. A ruin memory is bare steel.
=== ch9_beam ===
The last beam rests on sawhorses in the lobby. It is painted white. # id: ch9_beam.open.01 # speaker: narrator
By tradition, everyone who helped signs it before it goes up. # id: ch9_beam.open.02 # speaker: narrator
You have one marker. You walk the beam. # id: ch9_beam.open.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Hand Pip the marker. # id: ch9_beam.pip.01 # hide_if_mem: kid_partner lowballed # rel: kid_partner +2]
    Pip Delgado. First tenant. In writing. Finally. # id: ch9_beam.pip.02 # speaker: kid_partner
    He dots the i with a tiny lemon. # id: ch9_beam.pip.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Hand Pip the marker. He takes his time. # id: ch9_beam.pip.04 # show_if_mem: kid_partner lowballed # rel: kid_partner +1]
    Pip Delgado. First tenant. Overcharged. # id: ch9_beam.pip.05 # speaker: kid_partner
    You gave me a twenty once. I have been billing you ever since. # id: ch9_beam.pip.06 # speaker: kid_partner
-
Next, the corner of the beam. The good spot. # id: ch9_beam.rosa.01 # speaker: narrator
* [Hold the marker out to Rosa. # id: ch9_beam.rosa.02 # hide_if_mem: baker broke_deal # rel: baker +2]
    You promised me the corner. You kept it. So I get the corner here too. # id: ch9_beam.rosa.03 # speaker: baker
    The corner held. # id: ch9_beam.rosa.04 # speaker: grocer
* [Look for Rosa's name. Bare steel. # id: ch9_beam.rosa.05 # show_if_mem: baker broke_deal # rel: grocer -1]
    Rosa did not come. Marisol Villanueva looks at the gap for a while. # id: ch9_beam.rosa.06 # speaker: narrator
    Then she caps the marker and hands it back. # id: ch9_beam.rosa.07 # speaker: narrator
-
* [Pass the marker to Danny Okoro. # id: ch9_beam.danny.01 # hide_if_mem: car_wash_owner burned # rel: car_wash_owner +2]
    Your name is on my sign. Mine goes on your beam. # id: ch9_beam.danny.02 # speaker: car_wash_owner
    He writes 212 after it. Nobody asks. Everybody knows. # id: ch9_beam.danny.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Look for Danny Okoro. Bare steel. # id: ch9_beam.danny.04 # show_if_mem: car_wash_owner burned # rel: ten -1]
    Danny did not come. There is nothing left to count at his car wash. # id: ch9_beam.danny.05 # speaker: narrator
-
* [Offer Pearl the marker. She brought her own pen. # id: ch9_beam.pearl.01 # hide_if_mem: office_manager broke_deal # rel: office_manager +2]
    Pearl signs in red. Then she fixes the name above hers. # id: ch9_beam.pearl.02 # speaker: narrator
    Tenant has two n's, hon. Not three. Scoot over. # id: ch9_beam.pearl.03 # speaker: office_manager
* [Look for Pearl. Bare steel. # id: ch9_beam.pearl.04 # show_if_mem: office_manager broke_deal # rel: mentor -1]
    Pearl did not come. The lobby sign spells Corridor wrong. Nobody caught it. # id: ch9_beam.pearl.05 # speaker: narrator
-
* [Tape up the postcard from Pine Ridge. # id: ch9_beam.nettie.01 # hide_if_mem: lodge_owner lowballed # rel: neighbor_leader +2]
    Nettie Pruitt writes: "A Texan paid me a fair price. Nobody up here believes it." # id: ch9_beam.nettie.02 # speaker: narrator
    Pruitt goes on the left of it. I am the older cousin. # id: ch9_beam.nettie.03 # speaker: neighbor_leader
    By four months, Walt. I brought my own marker. # id: ch9_beam.nettie.04 # speaker: square_cousin
* [Look for a postcard from Pine Ridge. Nothing came. # id: ch9_beam.nettie.05 # show_if_mem: lodge_owner lowballed # rel: neighbor_leader -1]
    Nettie Pruitt phoned Walt the night she signed. Walt has not forgotten. # id: ch9_beam.nettie.06 # speaker: narrator
    The Pruitts stand by the door with their hands in their pockets. # id: ch9_beam.nettie.07 # speaker: narrator
-
* [Make room for Mrs. Alvarado. # id: ch9_beam.sew.01 # hide_if_mem: holdout_neighbor evicted # rel: holdout_neighbor +2]
    She brings a ribbon she sewed herself. It is Barn Red. Or Brick Red. # id: ch9_beam.sew.02 # speaker: narrator
    I outlasted four owners. The fifth one I will sign for. # id: ch9_beam.sew.03 # speaker: holdout_neighbor
* [Look for a ribbon on the beam. There is none. # id: ch9_beam.sew.04 # show_if_mem: holdout_neighbor evicted # rel: ten -1]
    Nobody sewed one. The shop under the stairs is a coat closet now. # id: ch9_beam.sew.05 # speaker: narrator
-
* [Hand Brock the marker. Stand back. # id: ch9_beam.brock.01 # show_if_mem: rival helped # rel: rival +2]
    He signs in letters bigger than yours. He needs both hands. # id: ch9_beam.brock.02 # speaker: narrator
    Mine is taller. Theirs is better. I hate this. # id: ch9_beam.brock.03 # speaker: rival
    Penmanship, C. Spacing, D. Showing up, A. Do not tell him. # id: ch9_beam.brock.04 # speaker: car_lot_owner
* [Look for Brock's name. Bare steel. # id: ch9_beam.brock.05 # hide_if_mem: rival helped # rel: car_lot_owner -1]
    There is room there for very large letters. Nobody named Delacroix came. # id: ch9_beam.brock.06 # speaker: narrator
-
* [Offer Lorraine the marker. # id: ch9_beam.hat.01 # hide_if_mem: mentor broke_deal # rel: mentor +2]
    She signs small. You have to lean in to read it. # id: ch9_beam.hat.02 # speaker: narrator
    She tips her hat. Her hand stays in her pocket. For now. # id: ch9_beam.hat.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Look for Lorraine's name. Bare steel. # id: ch9_beam.hat.04 # show_if_mem: mentor broke_deal # rel: inv -1]
    The top spot was saved for an Okafor. It is bare. # id: ch9_beam.hat.05 # speaker: narrator
    Her truck is not in the lot. Nobody tips a hat. # id: ch9_beam.hat.06 # speaker: narrator
-
* [Wave Hector's crew over. # id: ch9_beam.crew.01 # hide_if_mem: careful_contractor burned # rel: careful_contractor +2]
    Whole crew signs. Welders first. They earned the good spot. # id: ch9_beam.crew.02 # speaker: careful_contractor
    41 names. One of them draws a rain cloud and crosses it out. # id: ch9_beam.crew.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Look for the crew that built it. Bare steel. # id: ch9_beam.crew.04 # show_if_mem: careful_contractor burned # rel: ten -1]
    Strangers in clean vests wait by the crane. They do not sign. They did not build it. # id: ch9_beam.crew.05 # speaker: narrator
-
* [Hand Gil the marker. He would rather use his pencil. # id: ch9_beam.gil.01 # hide_if_mem: banker broke_deal # rel: banker +2]
    Gil signs with a very sharp pencil. On steel. It takes a while. # id: ch9_beam.gil.02 # speaker: narrator
    Yes. At this beam. # id: ch9_beam.gil.03 # speaker: banker
* [Look for Gil's name. Bare steel. # id: ch9_beam.gil.04 # show_if_mem: banker broke_deal # rel: bank -1]
    Gil could not leave the drive through window. He sent a lollipop. # id: ch9_beam.gil.05 # speaker: narrator
-
Celeste Halloway signs last, with the old fountain pen. # id: ch9_beam.last.01 # speaker: narrator
For the lights. # id: ch9_beam.last.02 # speaker: downtown_owner
There is one spot left. It is yours. # id: ch9_beam.last.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Sign small, at the end, under everyone else. # id: ch9_beam.you.01 # rel: mentor +2]
    {player_name}. It fits in the last clean inch of steel. # id: ch9_beam.you.02 # speaker: narrator
* [Sign big, right in the middle. # id: ch9_beam.you.03 # rel: rival +2]
    {player_name}. You can read it from the parking lot. That was the idea. # id: ch9_beam.you.04 # speaker: narrator

@dialogue/story/ch9_storm.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ch9_storm

// Landmark about half built. The big choice of ch9 (for the beam). Writes: careful_contractor helped | paid_on_time | burned.
=== ch9_storm ===
Spring. It rains for 19 days. Channel 6 runs out of centuries. # id: ch9_storm.open.01 # speaker: narrator
The tower is half built. The crane has not moved in a week. # id: ch9_storm.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Hector Salinas finds you in the site trailer. He takes off his hard hat. # id: ch9_storm.open.03 # speaker: narrator
Rain cost us three weeks. I can catch up if you pay for Saturdays. # id: ch9_storm.open.04 # speaker: careful_contractor
I gave you my word on the date. I did not know about the storms. # id: ch9_storm.open.05 # speaker: careful_contractor
30 years I have built in this town. Never late. Ask anybody but my wife. # id: ch9_storm.open.06 # speaker: careful_contractor
Your contract has a late penalty. It is big enough to close his company. # id: ch9_storm.open.07 # speaker: narrator
And you promised your owners a finish date. Pip circled it. Twice. # id: ch9_storm.open.08 # speaker: narrator
Gil reads the page two times. Then he takes off his glasses. # id: ch9_storm.open.09 # speaker: narrator
The contract says you can. It does not say you should. That part is yours. # id: ch9_storm.open.10 # speaker: banker
* [Drop the penalty. Move the date. Take the hit in your own pay. # id: ch9_storm.pick.01 # rep: pay_contractor_on_time # mem: careful_contractor helped # build: speed_pct -10 # cash: personal -50000 # rel: inv -5]
    You are paying for my rain out of your own pocket. # id: ch9_storm.drop.01 # speaker: careful_contractor
    Then every bolt will be straight. I will check them myself. # id: ch9_storm.drop.02 # speaker: careful_contractor
    The date moves. Your owners grumble. Your paycheck takes a long nap. # id: ch9_storm.drop.03 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: tower date moves. Developer pays for the rain. # id: ch9_storm.drop.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Split it. Pay for Saturdays and hold the date close. # id: ch9_storm.pick.02 # mem: careful_contractor paid_on_time # cash: company -120000 # build: speed_pct +5]
    Saturdays. Good. My crew will complain. They complain better when they are paid. # id: ch9_storm.split.01 # speaker: careful_contractor
    The tower lights burn six days a week. The date holds, close enough. # id: ch9_storm.split.02 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: tower crews add Saturdays to beat the rain. # id: ch9_storm.split.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Charge the penalty. # id: ch9_storm.pick.03 # rep: stall_contractor # mem: careful_contractor burned # cash: company +150000 # build: surprise_cost_pct +10]
    You point at the page. The page is on your side. # id: ch9_storm.charge.01 # speaker: narrator
    Then that is what it says. I will finish this floor and hand you the keys. # id: ch9_storm.charge.02 # speaker: careful_contractor
    Hector peels the Salinas sign off his own truck. 30 years, one sticker. # id: ch9_storm.charge.03 # speaker: narrator
    A new crew comes in clean vests. They ask where the tower is. They are standing in it. # id: ch9_storm.charge.04 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: Salinas Construction closes after 30 years over a late penalty. # id: ch9_storm.charge.05 # speaker: narrator
-
The rain lets up for one afternoon. # id: ch9_storm.brock.01 # speaker: narrator
* [Look up. Something big is rolling onto your site. # id: ch9_storm.brock.02 # show_if_mem: rival helped # build: speed_pct +10 # rel: rival +5]
    It is a crane. The side says Delacroix, in letters you could read from the freeway. # id: ch9_storm.brock.03 # speaker: narrator
    You are behind. I had a crane sitting around. Do not make this weird. # id: ch9_storm.brock.04 # speaker: rival
    Cute tower. I mean it this time. # id: ch9_storm.brock.05 # speaker: rival
* [Look across the street. No help is coming from there. # id: ch9_storm.brock.06 # hide_if_mem: rival helped # rel: rival -1]
    Nobody over there owes you a thing. The rain starts again. # id: ch9_storm.brock.07 # speaker: narrator
-
Channel 6 Glade News: rain of the century delays tower of the century. # id: ch9_storm.news.01 # speaker: narrator
Fence Line: the crane is in my spot. Again. # id: ch9_storm.news.02 # speaker: narrator
One beam left. # id: ch9_storm.news.03 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/story/comeback_booth.ink:
// Comeback chapter, scene 1 of 3 (writer D). Plays right after the career beat broke, on the first comeback only.
// It can open in any chapter, so every line must read right early or late. Doors read choices from ch4 and ch7.
// Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 7. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> comeback_booth

=== comeback_booth ===
The Honeycomb Diner, back booth. You have been here before. # id: comeback_booth.open.01 # speaker: narrator
The new head office of {company_name} is one table. The nameplate is a napkin holder. # id: comeback_booth.open.02 # speaker: narrator
Out front, the old kolache truck is parked crooked. It still sings. Nobody asked it to. # id: comeback_booth.open.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Slide into the booth. Somebody beat you to the phone. # id: comeback_booth.pearl.01 # hide_if_mem: office_manager broke_deal # rel: office_manager +3]
    {company_name}, head office. Please hold. # id: comeback_booth.pearl.02 # speaker: office_manager
    Pearl Tackett listens. She writes. She listens some more. # id: comeback_booth.pearl.03 # speaker: narrator
    That was four pie orders, hon. I said yes to all of them. # id: comeback_booth.pearl.04 # speaker: office_manager
    We are in the pie business until Friday. Scoot over. # id: comeback_booth.pearl.05 # speaker: office_manager
* [Slide into the booth. The seat across from you is empty. # id: comeback_booth.pearl.06 # show_if_mem: office_manager broke_deal # rel: mentor +1]
    The diner phone rings. And rings. Nobody says please hold. # id: comeback_booth.pearl.07 # speaker: narrator
    Across town, a red pen is fixing Brock's spelling. It has a lot of work. # id: comeback_booth.pearl.08 # speaker: narrator
    At last somebody picks up. It is Lorraine Okafor, on her way in. # id: comeback_booth.pearl.09 # speaker: narrator
    They can't talk right now. They are in a meeting with a pie. # id: comeback_booth.pearl.10 # speaker: mentor
- A box lands on your table. # id: comeback_booth.box.01 # speaker: narrator
* [Open the box. It rattles. # id: comeback_booth.box.02 # show_if_mem: rival helped # rel: rival +5]
    A coffee can, full of parking money. Mostly quarters. # id: comeback_booth.box.03 # speaker: narrator
    Under the can, business cards. "{player_name}, Partner, Delacroix Ventures." # id: comeback_booth.box.04 # speaker: narrator
    You bailed me out. Now I bail you out. I hate it. We're even. # id: comeback_booth.box.05 # speaker: rival
    Do not make this weird. # id: comeback_booth.box.06 # speaker: rival
* [Open the box. It is ringing. # id: comeback_booth.box.07 # show_if_mem: rival burned # rel: outside_buyer -2]
    A phone. You answer it, because it will not stop. # id: comeback_booth.box.08 # speaker: narrator
    Thad Pemberton, Buzzard Peak. I heard the news, friend. So sorry. So, so sorry. # id: comeback_booth.box.09 # speaker: outside_buyer
    I'll take every building you have left. Half price. That's me being nice. # id: comeback_booth.box.10 # speaker: outside_buyer
    I just love Cedar Grove. # id: comeback_booth.box.11 # speaker: outside_buyer
    It is Cedar Glade. You hang up and put the phone back in the box. # id: comeback_booth.box.12 # speaker: narrator
* [Open the box. It smells like fresh ink. # id: comeback_booth.box.13 # hide_if_mem: rival helped # hide_if_mem: rival burned # rel: rival +2]
    Business cards. A whole box. Somebody already printed them. # id: comeback_booth.box.14 # speaker: narrator
    "{player_name}, Vice President of Cute, Delacroix Ventures." # id: comeback_booth.box.15 # speaker: narrator
    Job offer. Real desk. Real paycheck. You'd report to me. Daily. # id: comeback_booth.box.16 # speaker: rival
    I printed 500. No pressure. # id: comeback_booth.box.17 # speaker: rival
    You keep one card. It is the nicest insult anyone ever printed for you. # id: comeback_booth.box.18 # speaker: narrator
- Lorraine Okafor pulls a chair up to the booth. She does not order. # id: comeback_booth.wise.01 # speaker: narrator
Everybody in this town has been broke once. # id: comeback_booth.wise.02 # speaker: mentor
The good ones were never broke the same way twice. # id: comeback_booth.wise.03 # speaker: mentor
By the door, Amos Tulley unfolds a lawn chair. Then a second one. # id: comeback_booth.wise.04 # speaker: narrator
The second one is for you. # id: comeback_booth.wise.05 # speaker: narrator
Two. But the pie is good. # id: comeback_booth.wise.06 # speaker: fence_regular
He just scored your whole company. The pie did most of the work. # id: comeback_booth.wise.07 # speaker: narrator
* [Call every tenant yourself. Tell them the plain truth. # id: comeback_booth.move.01 # rel: ten +6]
    It takes all afternoon. Nobody hangs up on you. # id: comeback_booth.move.02 # speaker: narrator
    One tenant offers you a casserole. You say yes. You are broke, not foolish. # id: comeback_booth.move.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Ask Lorraine how she got out of it. # id: comeback_booth.move.04 # rel: mentor +5]
    I sold my good boots and kept my word. In that order. # id: comeback_booth.move.05 # speaker: mentor
    Start with the word. Keep the boots if you can. # id: comeback_booth.move.06 # speaker: mentor
* [Tell the whole booth it is a small bump. # id: comeback_booth.move.07 # rel: ten -2 # rel: rival +2]
    The napkin holder does not look convinced. # id: comeback_booth.move.08 # speaker: narrator
    It is exactly what Brock would say. That should worry you a little. # id: comeback_booth.move.09 # speaker: narrator
- The coffee has free refills. The comeback does not. # id: comeback_booth.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Mission one. Steady. # id: comeback_booth.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/story/comeback_gil.ink:
// Comeback chapter, scene 2 of 3 (writer D). The big choice. Plays when comeback mission 1, Steady, is done.
// Writes the Gil memory that every later scene reads: banker honored_deal (kept) or banker broke_deal (jumped).
// The bank only ever says "yes, at this payment" or "no". Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 7.
// Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune. This scene is never skipped.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> comeback_gil

=== comeback_gil ===
Prairie Lantern Savings. Gil Haverty keeps a bowl of lollipops on his desk. # id: comeback_gil.open.01 # speaker: narrator
He straightens his bolo tie. That is how you know it is serious. # id: comeback_gil.open.02 # speaker: narrator
I made your loans on my own good name, {player_name}. # id: comeback_gil.open.03 # speaker: banker
My bosses know it. They remind me at lunch. Every lunch. # id: comeback_gil.open.04 # speaker: banker
A good track record beats a good pitch. Yours has a dent in it now. # id: comeback_gil.open.05 # speaker: banker
I drive a truck with a dent. Still gets me to work. # id: comeback_gil.open.06 # speaker: banker
So. Yes, at this payment. # id: comeback_gil.open.07 # speaker: banker
He slides one page across the desk. One number on it. Nothing else. # id: comeback_gil.open.08 # speaker: narrator
And you bank here. Only here. # id: comeback_gil.open.09 # speaker: banker
If you run, I am the one they move. Shake on it. # id: comeback_gil.open.10 # speaker: banker
You shake. Gil shakes like he is signing something. # id: comeback_gil.open.11 # speaker: narrator
You make it as far as the parking lot. Your phone rings. # id: comeback_gil.call.01 # speaker: narrator
Hello there, friend. Thad Pemberton, Buzzard Peak Partners. Money from far away. # id: comeback_gil.call.02 # speaker: outside_buyer
I can send you more than your little lantern bank. Today. No questions. # id: comeback_gil.call.03 # speaker: outside_buyer
I love a comeback. And I love this town. Cedar Grove, is it? # id: comeback_gil.call.04 # speaker: outside_buyer
It is Cedar Glade. The number he says next is a lot bigger than Gil's. # id: comeback_gil.call.05 # speaker: narrator
Through the window, Gil is filing your handshake under H. # id: comeback_gil.call.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Keep the handshake with Gil. # id: comeback_gil.pick.01 # rep: honor_handshake # mem: banker honored_deal # rel: bank +6]
    You tell Thad thanks, but no. # id: comeback_gil.kept.01 # speaker: narrator
    No hard feelings, friend. I'll call again. I always call again. # id: comeback_gil.kept.02 # speaker: outside_buyer
    Back inside, Gil has not moved. He was not worried. He was a little worried. # id: comeback_gil.kept.03 # speaker: narrator
    Slow money is still money. And it knows your name. # id: comeback_gil.kept.04 # speaker: banker
    Gil keeps his desk. He holds out the bowl. You take a red one. # id: comeback_gil.kept.05 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: {company_name} stays with its hometown bank. # id: comeback_gil.kept.06 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: the loyalty of the year. More at six. # id: comeback_gil.kept.07 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: good for them. Now where do I park at that bank. # id: comeback_gil.kept.08 # speaker: narrator
* [Walk back in. Tell Gil about the call. Ask if he can stretch a little. # id: comeback_gil.pick.02 # rel: banker -2 # rel: bank +2 # cash: company +50000]
    Gil listens to the whole thing. He does not blink much. # id: comeback_gil.stretch.01 # speaker: narrator
    You came back in and told me. Most folks would not. # id: comeback_gil.stretch.02 # speaker: banker
    He takes the page back. He sharpens the pencil. It was already sharp. # id: comeback_gil.stretch.03 # speaker: narrator
    Yes, at this payment. # id: comeback_gil.stretch.04 # speaker: banker
    The new page has a bigger number on it. Gil's smile is one size smaller. # id: comeback_gil.stretch.05 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: {company_name} gets a second chance, and a little extra. # id: comeback_gil.stretch.06 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: developer walks back into bank. Lobby stunned. # id: comeback_gil.stretch.07 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: that bank lot has 9 spaces. I counted. Nine. # id: comeback_gil.stretch.08 # speaker: narrator
* [Take the fast money. # id: comeback_gil.pick.03 # rep: take_better_offer # mem: banker broke_deal # mem: outside_buyer helped # cash: company +250000 # rel: bank -10]
    You say yes to Thad. The money lands before you start the engine. # id: comeback_gil.jumped.01 # speaker: narrator
    You are my kind of people. # id: comeback_gil.jumped.02 # speaker: outside_buyer
    Gil watches you drive off. He takes your handshake back out of the H file. # id: comeback_gil.jumped.03 # speaker: narrator
    One week later, the bank moves Gil to the drive through window. # id: comeback_gil.jumped.04 # speaker: narrator
    He still only says two things. Now he says them through a speaker. # id: comeback_gil.jumped.05 # speaker: narrator
    You pull up to test it. # id: comeback_gil.jumped.06 # speaker: narrator
    No. # id: comeback_gil.jumped.07 # speaker: banker
    A lollipop comes up the tube anyway. It is green. Nobody likes the green ones. # id: comeback_gil.jumped.08 # speaker: narrator
    Cedar Glade Courier: {company_name} takes out of town money. Hometown banker moved. # id: comeback_gil.jumped.09 # speaker: narrator
    Channel 6 Glade News: bank betrayal of the year. Lollipops at six. # id: comeback_gil.jumped.10 # speaker: narrator
    Fence Line: the drive through line is too long now. Thanks a lot. # id: comeback_gil.jumped.11 # speaker: narrator
- You have money again. What you do not have is tenants. # id: comeback_gil.hook.01 # speaker: narrator
Mission two. Full again. # id: comeback_gil.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
-> END

","^If you run, I am the one they move. Shake on it. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.open.10 ","/#","#","^speaker: banker","/#","
","^You shake. Gil shakes like he is signing something. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.open.11 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^You make it as far as the parking lot. Your phone rings. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.call.01 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^Hello there, friend. Thad Pemberton, Buzzard Peak Partners. Money from far away. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.call.02 ","/#","#","^speaker: outside_buyer","/#","
","^I can send you more than your little lantern bank. Today. No questions. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.call.03 ","/#","#","^speaker: outside_buyer","/#","
","^I love a comeback. And I love this town. Cedar Grove, is it? ","#","^id: comeback_gil.call.04 ","/#","#","^speaker: outside_buyer","/#","
","^It is Cedar Glade. The number he says next is a lot bigger than Gil's. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.call.05 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^Through the window, Gil is filing your handshake under H. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.call.06 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","ev","str","^Keep the handshake with Gil. Tell Gil about the call. Ask if he can stretch a little. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.pick.03 ","/#","#","^rep: take_better_offer ","/#","#","^mem: banker broke_deal ","/#","#","^mem: outside_buyer helped ","/#","#","^cash: company +250000 ","/#","#","^rel: bank -10","/#","/str","/ev",{"*":".^.c-2","flg":20},{"c-0":["
","^You tell Thad thanks, but no. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.kept.01 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^No hard feelings, friend. I'll call again. I always call again. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.kept.02 ","/#","#","^speaker: outside_buyer","/#","
","^Back inside, Gil has not moved. He was not worried. He was a little worried. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.kept.03 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^Slow money is still money. And it knows your name. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.kept.04 ","/#","#","^speaker: banker","/#","
","^Gil keeps his desk. He holds out the bowl. You take a red one. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.kept.05 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^Cedar Glade Courier: ","ev",{"VAR?":"company_name"},"out","/ev","^ stays with its hometown bank. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.kept.06 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^Channel 6 Glade News: the loyalty of the year. More at six. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.kept.07 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^Fence Line: good for them. Now where do I park at that bank. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.kept.08 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","

","^Gil listens to the whole thing. He does not blink much. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.stretch.01 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^You came back in and told me. Most folks would not. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.stretch.02 ","/#","#","^speaker: banker","/#","
","^He takes the page back. He sharpens the pencil. It was already sharp. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.stretch.03 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^Yes, at this payment. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.stretch.04 ","/#","#","^speaker: banker","/#","
","^The new page has a bigger number on it. Gil's smile is one size smaller. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.stretch.05 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^Cedar Glade Courier: ","ev",{"VAR?":"company_name"},"out","/ev","^ gets a second chance, and a little extra. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.stretch.06 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^Channel 6 Glade News: developer walks back into bank. Lobby stunned. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.stretch.07 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^Fence Line: that bank lot has 9 spaces. I counted. Nine. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.stretch.08 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
",{"->":".^.^.g-0"},{"#f":5}],"c-2":["
","^You say yes to Thad. The money lands before you start the engine. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.jumped.01 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^You are my kind of people. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.jumped.02 ","/#","#","^speaker: outside_buyer","/#","
","^Gil watches you drive off. He takes your handshake back out of the H file. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.jumped.03 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^One week later, the bank moves Gil to the drive through window. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.jumped.04 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^He still only says two things. Now he says them through a speaker. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.jumped.05 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
