","^No. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.jumped.07 ","/#","#","^speaker: banker","/#","
","^A lollipop comes up the tube anyway. It is green. Nobody likes the green ones. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.jumped.08 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
","^Cedar Glade Courier: ","ev",{"VAR?":"company_name"},"out","/ev","^ takes out of town money. Hometown banker moved. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.jumped.09 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","

","^Fence Line: the drive through line is too long now. Thanks a lot. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.jumped.11 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","
",{"->":".^.^.g-0"},{"#f":5}],"g-0":["^You have money again. What you do not have is tenants. ","#","^id: comeback_gil.hook.01 ","/#","#","^speaker: narrator","/#","

@dialogue/story/comeback_shovel.ink:
// Comeback chapter, scene 3 of 3 (writer D). Plays when comeback mission 3, Build again, is done,
// right before the career beat comeback ("They said {company} was done." "They were wrong.").
// Doors read Rosa (ch2) and Gil (comeback_gil). Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 7.
// Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> comeback_shovel

=== comeback_shovel ===
The Prairie Star Corridor, under the Exit 14 water tower. One small building. Brand new. # id: comeback_shovel.open.01 # speaker: narrator
It is the smallest thing you have ever been this proud of. # id: comeback_shovel.open.02 # speaker: narrator
The gold shovel is back. Somebody saved it. Nobody fixed it. It is still bent. # id: comeback_shovel.open.03 # speaker: narrator
A crowd shows up. Nobody brings cash. Everybody brings something. # id: comeback_shovel.open.04 # speaker: narrator
High on the water tower, a grackle is watching. You eat your sandwich early this time. # id: comeback_shovel.open.05 # speaker: narrator
* [Take the first lease from Rosa Delgado. # id: comeback_shovel.rosa.01 # hide_if_mem: baker broke_deal # rel: baker +5 # rel: ten +4]
    I want the little one with the window. I already bought the ovens. Again. # id: comeback_shovel.rosa.02 # speaker: baker
    And I brought two friends. They both need shops. They both pay on time. I asked. # id: comeback_shovel.rosa.03 # speaker: baker
    She also brought kolaches. She does not charge you. Today. # id: comeback_shovel.rosa.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Take the first lease from a stranger. # id: comeback_shovel.rosa.05 # show_if_mem: baker broke_deal # rel: ten -2]
    He sells phone cases. He has never heard of you. That helps. # id: comeback_shovel.rosa.06 # speaker: narrator
    Two months free. And I want my sign bigger than your sign. # id: comeback_shovel.rosa.07 # speaker: tenant
    You say yes. Rosa Delgado is not here. Nobody brought kolaches. # id: comeback_shovel.rosa.08 # speaker: narrator
- You look around for one more face. # id: comeback_shovel.gil.01 # speaker: narrator
* [Wave at Gil. He came on his lunch break, bolo tie and all. # id: comeback_shovel.gil.02 # hide_if_mem: banker broke_deal # rel: banker +3]
    I'm on lunch. This is not a bank visit. The bank does not clap. # id: comeback_shovel.gil.03 # speaker: banker
    Gil claps. # id: comeback_shovel.gil.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Wave at the bank across the road. # id: comeback_shovel.gil.05 # show_if_mem: banker broke_deal # rel: banker +1]
    Gil waves back from the drive through window. He has three cars waiting. # id: comeback_shovel.gil.06 # speaker: narrator
    A lollipop comes up the tube for nobody. You think it might be for you. # id: comeback_shovel.gil.07 # speaker: narrator
- Pip Delgado has guarded the shovel all morning. He holds it out like a sword. # id: comeback_shovel.pick.01 # speaker: narrator
Somebody has to swing it. First swing is free. Comeback discount. # id: comeback_shovel.pick.02 # speaker: kid_partner
* [Hand it to Pip. # id: comeback_shovel.pick.03 # rel: kid_partner +6]
    Site Shovel Officer. I want that in writing. # id: comeback_shovel.pick.04 # speaker: kid_partner
    He hits the dirt as hard as he can. The shovel rings like a bell. # id: comeback_shovel.pick.05 # speaker: narrator
* [Walk it over to Gil. # id: comeback_shovel.pick.06 # hide_if_mem: banker broke_deal # rel: banker +5]
    Gil holds the shovel like it might be a loan. He takes one careful swing. # id: comeback_shovel.pick.07 # speaker: narrator
    I have never said yes with a shovel before. # id: comeback_shovel.pick.08 # speaker: banker
* [Swing it yourself. # id: comeback_shovel.pick.09 # rel: fence_regular +3]
    The dirt is baked hard. The shovel bounces. Then it bends the other way. # id: comeback_shovel.pick.10 # speaker: narrator
    Bent twice, it is almost straight. You call that progress. # id: comeback_shovel.pick.11 # speaker: narrator
- From his lawn chair, Amos Tulley studies the hole for a long time. # id: comeback_shovel.close.01 # speaker: narrator
Five. Same crooked hole. I missed it. # id: comeback_shovel.close.02 # speaker: fence_regular
Lorraine Okafor has watched the whole thing from her truck. Window down. Engine on. # id: comeback_shovel.close.03 # speaker: narrator
Land does not care how fast you are. # id: comeback_shovel.close.04 # speaker: mentor
She drives off before you can answer. She never waits for the answer. # id: comeback_shovel.close.05 # speaker: narrator
Around town, people still say {company_name} is done. # id: comeback_shovel.close.06 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/story/ending_fair.ink:
// Ending epilogue: New in Town and Fair Dealer, the hat (writer D). Plays after cs_ending, variant fair_dealer.
// Amos's score is the last spoken line. Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 8.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ending_fair

=== ending_fair ===
The last beam has most of the names. It also has a few gaps. # id: ending_fair.open.01 # speaker: narrator
You can see the gaps from here. So can Lorraine Okafor. # id: ending_fair.open.02 # speaker: narrator
The party is warm. The band is somebody's cousin. The pie runs out by nine. # id: ending_fair.open.03 # speaker: narrator
One chair stays empty all night. Nobody moves it. Everybody knows whose it is. # id: ending_fair.open.04 # speaker: narrator
Down by the old depot, the Brass Clock is running again. Five minutes slow. # id: ending_fair.open.05 # speaker: narrator
I will get to it. # id: ending_fair.open.06 # speaker: fence_regular
Fence Line: three and a half stars. Nice lobby. Still waiting on that ribbon. # id: ending_fair.open.07 # speaker: narrator
Lorraine sets a hat on the rail next to you. # id: ending_fair.open.08 # speaker: narrator
It is not her hat. It is a good one. # id: ending_fair.open.09 # speaker: narrator
You earned the hat. The cow stays at the ranch until you make it right. # id: ending_fair.open.10 # speaker: mentor
Her name is Handshake. She can wait. She is a cow. # id: ending_fair.open.11 # speaker: mentor
* [Ask Lorraine who you still owe. # id: ending_fair.pick.01 # rel: mentor +5]
    You know who. Go read your beam. # id: ending_fair.pick.02 # speaker: mentor
    You do know. Bare steel is easy to find. It has no name on it. # id: ending_fair.pick.03 # speaker: narrator
    Bring pie when you go. It helps. # id: ending_fair.pick.04 # speaker: mentor
* [Say most is pretty good. # id: ending_fair.pick.05 # rel: mentor -2]
    It is. It is not what I asked. # id: ending_fair.pick.06 # speaker: mentor
    She tips her hat anyway. With Lorraine, that is not nothing. # id: ending_fair.pick.07 # speaker: narrator
- The party thins out. Somebody saves you the last slice after all. # id: ending_fair.last.01 # speaker: narrator
By the elevator, Amos Tulley folds up the lawn chair he brought himself. # id: ending_fair.last.02 # speaker: narrator
Eight. The dumpster is still crooked. # id: ending_fair.last.03 # speaker: fence_regular
-> END

@dialogue/story/ending_hard.ink:
// Ending epilogue: Hard Dealer, a big hat you bought yourself (writer D). Plays after cs_ending, variant hard_dealer.
// The door reads the ch7 choice: Brock is at the rail unless you burned him, then it is Jazmine.
// Amos's score is the last spoken line. Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 8.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ending_hard

=== ending_hard ===
The party has 400 guests and a hired band. The band is very good. Nobody dances. # id: ending_hard.open.01 # speaker: narrator
By ten, the valet line is longer than the food line. # id: ending_hard.open.02 # speaker: narrator
The pie has not been cut. # id: ending_hard.open.03 # speaker: narrator
The last beam has more gaps than names. It looks like a smile with teeth missing. # id: ending_hard.open.04 # speaker: narrator
You are wearing a hat. You bought it yourself. # id: ending_hard.open.05 # speaker: narrator
It is so large it has its own shadow. # id: ending_hard.open.06 # speaker: narrator
Down by the old depot, the Brass Clock still says 4:10. # id: ending_hard.open.07 # speaker: narrator
The elevator opens. Della Marsh of the Courier steps out, typing with her thumbs. # id: ending_hard.open.08 # speaker: narrator
One question, {player_name}. Who is all this for? # id: ending_hard.open.09 # speaker: reporter
You start to answer. The elevator doors close on it. # id: ending_hard.open.10 # speaker: narrator
Cedar Glade Courier: tallest tower in town opens. Developer eats alone. # id: ending_hard.open.11 # speaker: narrator
* [Walk to the rail. Somebody loud is already there. # id: ending_hard.rail.01 # hide_if_mem: rival burned # rel: rival +2]
    Nice hat. Big. # id: ending_hard.rail.02 # speaker: rival
    From Brock Delacroix, that is a review. You cannot tell if it is a good one. # id: ending_hard.rail.03 # speaker: narrator
    Take it from a man who owns six. The hat is the easy part. # id: ending_hard.rail.04 # speaker: rival
* [Walk to the rail. Somebody fast is already there. # id: ending_hard.rail.05 # show_if_mem: rival burned # rel: top_broker +2]
    Brock said his piece and left. He took the stairs. All of them. # id: ending_hard.rail.06 # speaker: narrator
    I sold you half the dirt under this. You are welcome. # id: ending_hard.rail.07 # speaker: top_broker
    Great party. I'm leaving. Call me. Everybody does. # id: ending_hard.rail.08 # speaker: top_broker
- A waiter brings a card up from the front desk, on a tray. # id: ending_hard.card.01 # speaker: narrator
You know the handwriting. It is Lorraine Okafor's. # id: ending_hard.card.02 # speaker: narrator
It says, "The booth is still open." # id: ending_hard.card.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Put the card in your pocket. # id: ending_hard.card.04 # rel: mentor +3]
    It is the only thing up here tonight that you did not pay for. # id: ending_hard.card.05 # speaker: narrator
* [Leave it on the tray. # id: ending_hard.card.06 # rel: mentor -3]
    The waiter carries it off with the pie nobody ate. # id: ending_hard.card.07 # speaker: narrator
- Far below, one man in a lawn chair has watched the whole party. # id: ending_hard.last.01 # speaker: narrator
Six and a half. Do not ask me to round up. # id: ending_hard.last.02 # speaker: fence_regular
-> END

@dialogue/story/ending_shark.ink:
// Ending epilogue: Shark, all cattle, no hat (writer D). Plays after cs_ending, variant shark.
// The door reads the ch7 choice: Brock stays at the rail unless you burned him, then your only guest is Thad.
// Amos's score is the last spoken line. Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 8.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ending_shark

=== ending_shark ===
You own more buildings than anyone in Cedar Glade. A whole herd of them. # id: ending_shark.open.01 # speaker: narrator
You still do not own a hat. Nobody ever offered. You never asked. # id: ending_shark.open.02 # speaker: narrator
The last beam is mostly bare steel. Your name has room to spare. You checked the spelling yourself. # id: ending_shark.open.03 # speaker: narrator
The party is catered for 300. The caterer is the only one eating. # id: ending_shark.open.04 # speaker: narrator
Down by the old depot, the Brass Clock still says 4:10. # id: ending_shark.open.05 # speaker: narrator
Amos has the key. He has not wound it. He will not say why. # id: ending_shark.open.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Turn around. Somebody is still at the rail. # id: ending_shark.guest.01 # hide_if_mem: rival burned # rel: rival +2]
    Brock Delacroix. He did not leave. He is not sure why. # id: ending_shark.guest.02 # speaker: narrator
    You beat me at my own game, {player_name}. Nobody likes you. Everybody calls you. # id: ending_shark.guest.03 # speaker: rival
    He said it loud a minute ago. This time he says it like a warning. # id: ending_shark.guest.04 # speaker: narrator
    I used to want exactly this. Cute, right? # id: ending_shark.guest.05 # speaker: rival
* [Turn around. You have exactly one guest. # id: ending_shark.guest.06 # show_if_mem: rival burned # rel: outside_buyer +2]
    Thad Pemberton, with a glass of sweet tea. The price tag is still on his hat. # id: ending_shark.guest.07 # speaker: narrator
    What a view, friend. You can see all of Cedar Grove from up here. # id: ending_shark.guest.08 # speaker: outside_buyer
    You are my kind of people. # id: ending_shark.guest.09 # speaker: outside_buyer
    Bless your heart. # id: ending_shark.guest.10 # speaker: narrator
    Gerald lands on the rail. He studies the tag for a long moment. # id: ending_shark.guest.11 # speaker: narrator
    Then he takes it. At last. # id: ending_shark.guest.12 # speaker: narrator
    Did that crow just rob me? # id: ending_shark.guest.13 # speaker: outside_buyer
- Everyone else sent regrets. A few sent them twice, to be sure. # id: ending_shark.card.01 # speaker: narrator
Gerald comes back for the other half of your sandwich. Gerald does not send regrets. # id: ending_shark.card.02 # speaker: narrator
Under the plate, there is a card. No name on it. You know the handwriting. # id: ending_shark.card.03 # speaker: narrator
It says, "The booth is still open. So is the door." # id: ending_shark.card.04 # speaker: narrator
* [Keep the card. # id: ending_shark.card.05 # rel: mentor +2]
    You pocket it. It is the only thing up here you did not buy. # id: ending_shark.card.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Drop it off the roof. # id: ending_shark.card.07 # rel: mentor -2]
    It never lands. Gerald catches it. Even he thinks you should keep it. # id: ending_shark.card.08 # speaker: narrator
- Across the street, alone at the fence, Amos Tulley looks all the way up. # id: ending_shark.last.01 # speaker: narrator
Six. It is tall. I will give you that. # id: ending_shark.last.02 # speaker: fence_regular
-> END

@dialogue/story/ending_straight.ink:
// Ending epilogue: Straight Shooter, hat and cattle (writer D). Plays after cs_ending, variant straight_shooter.
// In that cutscene Lorraine has just set her hat on your head and held out her hand for the first time.
// Amos's score is the last spoken line. Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 8.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> ending_straight

=== ending_straight ===
The last beam is full. The last few names had to be written small. # id: ending_straight.open.01 # speaker: narrator
You shake Lorraine Okafor's hand. First time ever. Good grip. # id: ending_straight.open.02 # speaker: narrator
The hat fits. Of course it fits. She measures everything. # id: ending_straight.open.03 # speaker: narrator
One more thing. Freight elevator. Mind your boots. # id: ending_straight.open.04 # speaker: mentor
The doors open. It is a cow. # id: ending_straight.open.05 # speaker: narrator
One cow, from Okafor Land and Cattle, on top of a tower. # id: ending_straight.open.06 # speaker: narrator
Her name is Handshake. # id: ending_straight.open.07 # speaker: mentor
Brock said all hat, no cattle. Now you have one of each. # id: ending_straight.open.08 # speaker: mentor
Handshake looks at the view. Handshake is not impressed. # id: ending_straight.open.09 # speaker: narrator
Below you, downtown has its lights on. Every floor. # id: ending_straight.open.10 # speaker: narrator
The Brass Clock runs on time now. Once a day, at 4:10, it chimes. # id: ending_straight.open.11 # speaker: narrator
The town calls that handshake hour. # id: ending_straight.open.12 # speaker: narrator
* [Turn around. Somebody is late, and loud about it. # id: ending_straight.brock.01 # show_if_mem: rival helped # rel: rival +5]
    Brock Delacroix, out of breath, carrying a hat box. # id: ending_straight.brock.02 # speaker: narrator
    A hat like that needs a box. I checked. You never had a box either. # id: ending_straight.brock.03 # speaker: rival
    Cute. I still mean it. Do not make it weird. # id: ending_straight.brock.04 # speaker: rival
    Miss Odette is right behind him. She looks you over, top to bottom. # id: ending_straight.brock.05 # speaker: narrator
    Hat. A. Handshake. A. Parking. Still a C minus. # id: ending_straight.brock.06 # speaker: car_lot_owner
* [Turn around. A hat box sits by the elevator. # id: ending_straight.brock.07 # hide_if_mem: rival helped # rel: rival +1]
    The tag says Delacroix Motors. There is a card inside. # id: ending_straight.brock.08 # speaker: narrator
    The card has one word on it. "Cute." # id: ending_straight.brock.09 # speaker: narrator
    He did not come. He did send a box. From Brock, that is a parade. # id: ending_straight.brock.10 # speaker: narrator
- The next morning, the Honeycomb Diner bolts a brass plate to the back booth. # id: ending_straight.booth.01 # speaker: narrator
It says "First office of {company_name}." Somebody checked the spelling in red pen. # id: ending_straight.booth.02 # speaker: narrator
You sit down. Somebody slides in across from you with a napkin sketch. # id: ending_straight.booth.03 # speaker: narrator
Pip Delgado. All grown up. Still talking fast. # id: ending_straight.booth.04 # speaker: narrator
I bought a lot. It's empty. People say it's cursed. I got it cheap. # id: ending_straight.booth.05 # speaker: kid_partner
Pip Delgado, developer. It's on my card. # id: ending_straight.booth.06 # speaker: kid_partner
Before you ask, yes, there's a lemonade stand on it. It stays. # id: ending_straight.booth.07 # speaker: kid_partner
* [Ask him: "What does it do for the neighbors?" # id: ending_straight.pip.01 # rel: kid_partner +10]
    I knew you'd ask. The answer is on the back. # id: ending_straight.pip.02 # speaker: kid_partner
    He flips the napkin over. It is a list. It is a long list. # id: ending_straight.pip.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Tell him: "Call me when you get stuck. You will." # id: ending_straight.pip.04 # rel: kid_partner +8]
    I'm not going to get stuck. # id: ending_straight.pip.05 # speaker: kid_partner
    What time do you get up, though? Just in case. # id: ending_straight.pip.06 # speaker: kid_partner
* [Tip your new hat. # id: ending_straight.pip.07 # rel: kid_partner +6 # rel: mentor +5]
    Pip looks at the hat. Then at you. Then out the window, toward the ranch. # id: ending_straight.pip.08 # speaker: narrator
    You have a hat now. And cattle. I checked. # id: ending_straight.pip.09 # speaker: kid_partner
- Out front, a pastry truck pulls away from the curb. # id: ending_straight.last.01 # speaker: narrator
It plays the old kolache jingle. It still will not turn off. # id: ending_straight.last.02 # speaker: narrator
By the door, Amos Tulley folds up his lawn chair. He has seen enough. # id: ending_straight.last.03 # speaker: narrator
Ten. Do not let it go to your head. # id: ending_straight.last.04 # speaker: fence_regular
-> END

@dialogue/story/opening_exit14.ink:
// Story opening (writer D). Plays on New Game, right after the career beat cold_open, before the first tutorial step.
// Plan: Docs/story/scene-plan.md section 5. Every number in a tag is a guess for the owner to tune.
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"

-> opening_exit14

=== opening_exit14 ===
One hour earlier. # id: opening_exit14.open.01 # speaker: narrator
The Prairie Star Freeway, Exit 14. A rusty red pickup rattles down the ramp. # id: opening_exit14.open.02 # speaker: narrator
It used to deliver for Sunup Kolaches. Today it delivers {player_name}. # id: opening_exit14.open.03 # speaker: narrator
A little cash. A big idea. A sandwich for later. # id: opening_exit14.open.04 # speaker: narrator
The speaker on the roof still plays the kolache jingle. # id: opening_exit14.open.05 # speaker: narrator
There is no off switch. You have looked. Twice. # id: opening_exit14.open.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Thump the dashboard. # id: opening_exit14.jingle.01 # cash: personal -20]
    The glove box falls off. # id: opening_exit14.jingle.02 # speaker: narrator
    The jingle plays on. It sounds a little proud of itself. # id: opening_exit14.jingle.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Sing along. You know every word by now. # id: opening_exit14.jingle.04 # rel: kid_partner +2]
    Across the road, a kid gives you a thumbs up. # id: opening_exit14.jingle.05 # speaker: narrator
    Then he covers his ears. Fair. # id: opening_exit14.jingle.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Pretend it's on purpose. Wave at the next car. # id: opening_exit14.jingle.07 # rel: top_broker +1]
    The driver waves back. She is on the phone, and she is laughing. # id: opening_exit14.jingle.08 # speaker: narrator
    You will find out who she is in about two minutes. # id: opening_exit14.jingle.09 # speaker: narrator
- The light at the frontage road turns red. # id: opening_exit14.light.01 # speaker: narrator
A lifted truck pulls up next to you. # id: opening_exit14.light.02 # speaker: narrator
It is so shiny you can see your own rust in it. # id: opening_exit14.light.03 # speaker: narrator
The window slides down. Pearl snap shirt. Great big grin. # id: opening_exit14.light.04 # speaker: narrator
The door says Delacroix Ventures, in gold. So does the other door. # id: opening_exit14.light.05 # speaker: narrator
Selling kolaches? # id: opening_exit14.light.06 # speaker: rival
You say two words. "Buying dirt." # id: opening_exit14.light.07 # speaker: narrator
Brock Delacroix looks at your truck. Then at you. Then at the truck again. # id: opening_exit14.light.08 # speaker: narrator
All hat, no cattle. Cute. # id: opening_exit14.light.09 # speaker: rival
You do not even own a hat. Somehow that makes it worse. # id: opening_exit14.light.10 # speaker: narrator
* [Tip the hat you do not have. # id: opening_exit14.brock.01 # rel: rival +3]
    Ha! Okay. That was almost smooth. # id: opening_exit14.brock.02 # speaker: rival
    He tips his real one right back. It is a very nice hat. # id: opening_exit14.brock.03 # speaker: narrator
* [Ask if his truck comes with a ladder. # id: opening_exit14.brock.04 # rel: rival -3]
    It comes with a horn that turns off. Try one sometime. # id: opening_exit14.brock.05 # speaker: rival
    The jingle answers for you. # id: opening_exit14.brock.06 # speaker: narrator
* [Ask which lot he would buy. # id: opening_exit14.brock.07 # rel: rival +1 # broker: priority +1]
    Anything but that dirt under the water tower. Total dud. Trust me. # id: opening_exit14.brock.08 # speaker: rival
    He points away from the water tower. He does it a little too fast. # id: opening_exit14.brock.09 # speaker: narrator
- The light turns green. Brock is gone before your truck finds second gear. # id: opening_exit14.text.01 # speaker: narrator
Your phone buzzes. Jazmine Treviño, the broker who knows every deal in three counties. # id: opening_exit14.text.02 # speaker: narrator
Lot under the water tower. Cheap. Brock is circling. You first, for now. # id: opening_exit14.text.03 # speaker: top_broker
* ["On my way." # id: opening_exit14.text.04 # broker: priority +1]
    Good. Fast is my favorite color. # id: opening_exit14.text.05 # speaker: top_broker
    Bring a pen. Bring a hat, if you have one. # id: opening_exit14.text.06 # speaker: top_broker
* ["What is wrong with it?" # id: opening_exit14.text.07 # rel: top_broker +2]
    Three shops died there. Locals call it the Triple Flop. # id: opening_exit14.text.08 # speaker: top_broker
    Smart to ask. Most people ask after they sign. # id: opening_exit14.text.09 # speaker: top_broker
- One more thing. Was that you in the singing truck? Don't answer that. # id: opening_exit14.hook.01 # speaker: top_broker
You turn in under the Exit 14 water tower. The jingle turns in with you. # id: opening_exit14.hook.02 # speaker: narrator
High up on the tank, one grackle watches you park. Then he watches your sandwich. # id: opening_exit14.hook.03 # speaker: narrator
On the lot with the For Sale sign, somebody is already in business. # id: opening_exit14.hook.04 # speaker: narrator
It is a lemonade stand. # id: opening_exit14.hook.05 # speaker: narrator
-> END

@dialogue/tenant_late_rent.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR tenant_name = "Rosa Delgado"
VAR tenant_business = "Delgado Family Bakery"
VAR site_name = "Bluebonnet Plaza"

-> tenant_late_rent

=== tenant_late_rent ===
{tenant_name} of {tenant_business} stops you in the hall. # id: tenant_late_rent.open.01 # speaker: narrator
I am behind on rent, {player_name}. A freezer broke and a big order fell through. # id: tenant_late_rent.open.02 # speaker: tenant
I am sorry. I did not want you to hear it from somebody else. # id: tenant_late_rent.open.03 # speaker: tenant
* [Give them a short break on rent. # id: tenant_late_rent.help.01 # rep: tenant_rent_break # mem: @tenant rent_break # lease: free_months +1]
    Bless you. I will not forget this. # id: tenant_late_rent.help.02 # speaker: tenant
    -> END
* [Set up a payment plan. # id: tenant_late_rent.help.03 # mem: @tenant helped]
    A plan I can do. Thank you for not shutting the door. # id: tenant_late_rent.help.04 # speaker: tenant
    -> plan
* [Say you need it all by Friday. # id: tenant_late_rent.help.05 # rel: @tenant -5]
    Friday? I will try. But that is going to hurt. # id: tenant_late_rent.help.06 # speaker: tenant
    -> END
* [Start the eviction and re-lease the space fast. # id: tenant_late_rent.help.07 # rep: evict_fast # mem: @tenant evicted # lease: walk]
    So that is how it is. I will pack up. # id: tenant_late_rent.help.08 # speaker: tenant
    -> END

= plan
How would you like to do it? # id: tenant_late_rent.plan.01 # speaker: tenant
* [A little extra each month until it is caught up. # id: tenant_late_rent.plan.02 # rel: @tenant +4]
    That is gentle. I can handle that. # id: tenant_late_rent.plan.03 # speaker: tenant
    -> END
* [Add a year to the lease to spread it out. # id: tenant_late_rent.plan.04 # lease: term_years +1 # rel: @tenant +2]
    I was planning to stay anyway. Deal. # id: tenant_late_rent.plan.05 # speaker: tenant
    -> END
* [Half now, half next month. # id: tenant_late_rent.plan.06 # rel: @tenant +1]
    I can scrape that together. Thank you. # id: tenant_late_rent.plan.07 # speaker: tenant
    -> END

@dialogue/tenant_lease.ink:
VAR player_name = "Sam"
VAR company_name = "Bluebonnet Builders"
VAR tenant_name = "Rosa Delgado"
VAR tenant_business = "Delgado Family Bakery"
VAR site_name = "Bluebonnet Plaza"

-> tenant_lease

=== tenant_lease ===
{tenant_name} walks in with flour on one sleeve. # id: tenant_lease.open.01 # speaker: narrator
Hi, {player_name}. I run {tenant_business}. I want the corner space at {site_name}. # id: tenant_lease.open.02 # speaker: tenant
I have talked to two other landlords. Let us see if we can make this work. # id: tenant_lease.open.03 # speaker: tenant
* [Ask what matters most to them. # id: tenant_lease.open.04 # mem: @tenant met # rel: @tenant +3]
    Honestly, rent and a fair start. Ovens are not cheap. # id: tenant_lease.open.05 # speaker: tenant
* [Say the space will sell itself. # id: tenant_lease.open.06 # mem: @tenant met # rel: @tenant -2]
    It is a nice space. But a nice space still has to pay for itself. # id: tenant_lease.open.07 # speaker: tenant
- Let us start with the rent. # id: tenant_lease.rent.01 # speaker: tenant
* [Hold the rent where it is posted. # id: tenant_lease.rent.02 # rel: @tenant -2]
    Hmm. That is firm. I can live with it, if the rest is fair. # id: tenant_lease.rent.03 # speaker: tenant
* [Offer five percent off. # id: tenant_lease.rent.04 # lease: rent_pct -5 # rel: @tenant +4]
    That helps a lot. Thank you. # id: tenant_lease.rent.05 # speaker: tenant
* [Show the foot traffic and hold a higher rent. # id: tenant_lease.rent.06 # skill_req: negotiation 3 # lease: rent_pct +5]
    You brought real numbers. Fine. A busy corner is worth it. # id: tenant_lease.rent.07 # speaker: tenant
* [Say take it or leave it, and ask for more. # id: tenant_lease.rent.08 # lease: rent_pct +15 # lease: walk]
    That is not a talk, that is a shove. I will keep looking. # id: tenant_lease.rent.09 # speaker: tenant
    -> walk_away
- Now, how long are we talking? # id: tenant_lease.term.01 # speaker: tenant
* [Three years. # id: tenant_lease.term.02 # lease: term_years +3]
    Three works. Gives me room to grow. # id: tenant_lease.term.03 # speaker: tenant
* [Five years, with one month free. # id: tenant_lease.term.04 # lease: term_years +5 # lease: free_months +1]
    Five is a big promise. The free month helps me say yes. # id: tenant_lease.term.05 # speaker: tenant
* [Promise to host their grand opening. # id: tenant_lease.term.06 # skill_req: charisma 2 # lease: term_years +4 # rel: @tenant +6 # miss: A party is kind. I still need to think about the term.]
    You would do that? Now that makes me smile. Four years it is. # id: tenant_lease.term.07 # speaker: tenant
* [One year only, we can see how it goes. # id: tenant_lease.term.08 # lease: term_years +1 # rel: @tenant -3]
    A year is short. I will need to think about that. # id: tenant_lease.term.09 # speaker: tenant
- One more thing. My bank wants somebody bigger on the paper. # id: tenant_lease.signer.01 # speaker: tenant
* [Ask a guarantor to sign too. # id: tenant_lease.signer.02 # lease: signer guarantor # rel: @tenant -1]
    My brother can do that. He will not love it. # id: tenant_lease.signer.03 # speaker: tenant
* [Ask the parent company to sign. # id: tenant_lease.signer.04 # lease: signer parent_company]
    The family company can sign. That is the safest for you. # id: tenant_lease.signer.05 # speaker: tenant
* [You alone can sign. We trust you. # id: tenant_lease.signer.06 # lease: signer tenant # rel: @tenant +5]
    Wow. Thank you. I will not let you down. # id: tenant_lease.signer.07 # speaker: tenant
- {tenant_name} holds out a pen. # id: tenant_lease.close.01 # speaker: narrator
Well, {player_name}. Do we have a deal? # id: tenant_lease.close.02 # speaker: tenant
* [Shake hands and sign. We kept our word to each other. # id: tenant_lease.close.03 # lease: sign # skill_xp: lease_up # mem: @tenant honored_deal]
    Welcome to {site_name}. I will bring the first cinnamon rolls. # id: tenant_lease.close.04 # speaker: tenant
    -> END
* [Sign, but keep it short and business like. # id: tenant_lease.close.05 # lease: sign # skill_xp: lease_up # mem: @tenant met]
    Good. Let us get to work. # id: tenant_lease.close.06 # speaker: tenant
    -> END
* [Say you need a day to think it over. # id: tenant_lease.close.07 # lease: walk # mem: @tenant met]
    Alright. But I cannot wait long. # id: tenant_lease.close.08 # speaker: tenant
    -> walk_away

= walk_away
{tenant_name} gathers the papers and heads for the door. # id: tenant_lease.walk.01 # speaker: narrator
Maybe next time. Good luck with the plaza. # id: tenant_lease.walk.02 # speaker: tenant
-> END
